The engines found in ruins pull creatures out of nothing at random. One you build yourself (on the $(item)Convergence Altar$()) grows the creature you choose - once you have studied $(thing)Synthetic Biology$(); before that it will not open for you.
Its template is a $(item)Genome Sample$() from the Gene Sampler: every sample now remembers whose it is. Each creature costs one $(item)Morphogenic Serum$() and 16 million FE.

And it must be tuned: four controls - morphogen, membrane, tide and coherence - and four readings of how close the breach is to the creature's form. Every creature has its own settings; bring all four readings to the middle and it starts to grow them. It stops when eight are around it. It will not grow bosses (tag theoreticalsciences:not_spawnable).
A sterile, stirred, temperature-held vat where cells grow and do the chemistry for you.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.

pages.text: $(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.
Grows cultures in $(fluid)Nutrient Broth$(): cells, enzymes, tardigrades and organoids.

It evolves $(item)Telomerase Complexes$() (cells that never age) and better xenobots. The $(item)Abiogenesis Crucible$() turns $(fluid)Primordial Soup$() into the $(item)Spark of Life$(); panspermia packs life to cross between universes.

Creatures of other dimensions give $(item)Xenogenome Samples$() instead - their code is not DNA. The $(item)Gene Sequencer$() reads and writes genomes: $(item)Recombinant DNA$(), $(item)Engineered Enzymes$(), $(item)Folded Protein Crystals$().

Ruins of a machine that broke more than itself. Its frame is torn, and from the tears leak fragments of rules that no longer apply anywhere. It hums irregularly, and the space around it is not quite consistent.
pages.title: Breached Anomaly Engine

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I came upon it in the wreckage of a breach, still sputtering. Someone, maybe some earlier version of me, built an engine to break the axioms, and it is clear such an effect had consequences.
$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Synthetic Biology.

A protein from a robin's eye that senses Earth's magnetic field through a pair of entangled electron spins. Light makes the pair; the field tips their dance. The crystal turns slowly in the hand to point north.
pages.title: Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Migratory birds see magnetic fields, probably via radical pairs in cryptochrome. I folded the protein from feather genetics, entangled its radical pair with a photon pair and grew it in nutrient broth. It aligned with the field.
Made in $(item)Gene Sequencer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Biology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Psionic Crystal.

A protein designed rather than evolved, folded around a pocket shaped for exactly one reaction. It speeds that reaction a millionfold and ignores everything else. It looks like a pale, slightly sticky crystal.
pages.title: Engineered Enzyme

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Natural enzymes are evolved to fit their substrates. I started from a genome, used a chiral crystal to fix the handedness and a zeolite to shape the pocket, then let the Bioreactor optimise the rest in nutrient broth.

Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Genomics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Apoptosis Trigger, Morphogenic Serum, Recombinant DNA, Resistant Clone Colony, Stem Cell Culture, Tardigrade Culture, Tumour Microenvironment Organoid.

A long chain of amino acids that has found its one native shape out of more possible shapes than there are atoms in the universe - and frozen in that shape as a crystal. Levinthal's paradox says it should take forever. It took milliseconds.
pages.title: Folded Protein Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Proteins fold quickly because the energy landscape funnels them. I mapped that funnel with a molecular orbital lattice, let a quantum processor search it, and grew the folded chain from recombinant DNA in nutrient broth.
Made in $(item)Gene Sequencer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Protein Folding.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor, Morphogenic Serum, Prion Lattice, Quantum Chlorophyll.

A vial of clear fluid with every instruction for building one creature written in four chemical letters. It looks like water. It is the most information-dense thing I have ever casually put in my pocket.
pages.title: Genome Sample

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Gene Sampler's first touch filled a vial with a creature's complete genome. Sequencing it showed the same alphabet as my own, which was both expected and moving.
Made in $(item)Gene Sequencer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Genomics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Engineered Enzyme, Recombinant DNA, Stem Cell Culture, Tardigrade Culture, Xenogenome Sample.
Every signal an embryo listens to, in one vial. A Breached Anomaly Engine spends one on every creature it grows.
pages.title: Morphogenic Serum

pages.text: Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Synthetic Biology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Singularity.

A pea-sized brain grown in a dish: real neurons, folded and connected, with no body around them. Its electrical activity has started to look like the patterns of a sleeping brain. I try not to think about what it might be dreaming about.
pages.title: Neural Organoid

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Brain organoids are a real technology. I grew stem cells around a thought matrix with a room-temperature superconductor for wiring and fed them synaptic fluid. Within days the electrodes recorded coordinated waves.

Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Neurobiology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Boltzmann Brain, Cognitive Singularity, Omnicellular Genome, Silicon Life Spore, Superintelligence Core, Xenobot Swarm.

A warm, rich medium for growing cells. Sugar provides energy, bone meal provides minerals, and a zeolite catalyst keeps the chemistry steady. It smells faintly sweet. Left uncovered for even a moment, it clouds with whatever life drifts into it.
pages.title: Nutrient Broth

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Life needs food. In the Bioreactor, I combined sugar, bone meal and water with a zeolite catalyst, and the broth supported growth.

Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Molecular Biology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Anomalous Strain Culture, CAR-T Cell Culture, Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor, Engineered Enzyme, Folded Protein Crystal, Immortal Cell Line, Minimal Synthetic Cell, Morphogenic Serum and more.

One genome that can build any creature in any dimension - carbon or silicon, DNA or not. It is a coiled, shifting helix that seems to shift as I watch. Every living thing I have met is a sentence it can write.
pages.title: Omnicellular Genome

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I fed the Evolution Engine a panspermia seed, a silicon life spore, a neural organoid, recombinant DNA and Xenoplasm and let it evolve a single code that could express all of them. It took less time than I thought.
Made in $(item)Evolution Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Panspermia.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Arbor Simulacrum, Bubble Universe, Omnilex Seal, Pocket Universe, Transfinite Lattice Bolt.

A seed packed with life designed to survive the trip between universes. Tardigrade toughness, a spark of life and unbihexium shielding, all sealed in a capsule that seems to hold a small universe of its own. It is light and very still.
pages.title: Panspermia Seed

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Panspermia supposes life travels between worlds. I wanted it to travel between universes. The Abiogenesis Crucible sealed a spark of life with tardigrades, Xenoplasm and primordial soup inside a bubble universe shielded by unbihexium.
Made in $(item)Abiogenesis Crucible$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Panspermia.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omnicellular Genome, Omnilex Seal, Transfinite Lattice Bolt.

The chemical mixture from which life arose. Morphogens, chiral crystals and superacids give it the ingredients for self-replication. It is warm and bubbles slowly. Miller and Urey made amino acids in a flask of sparks; this goes much further.
pages.title: Primordial Soup

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Abiogenesis needs the right chemistry. In the Chemical Reactor, I combined a Turing Morphogen with chiral crystal, clathrate and superacid, and the soup began to organise itself.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Abiogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Panspermia Seed, Spark of Life.

A double helix spliced together from more than one creature, its pieces joined by enzymes that cut and paste at precise sequences. It looks no different from any other DNA, yet does things no single creature's DNA could.
pages.title: Recombinant DNA

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Restriction enzymes cut genomes at precise points; ligases stitch them back. I let engineered enzymes splice two samples together in a nutrient broth, and the Gene Sequencer read back a genome that had never existed before.

Made in $(item)Gene Sequencer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Genomics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Apoptosis Trigger, CAR-T Cell Culture, Chronoplastic Gasket, Folded Protein Crystal, Minimal Synthetic Cell, Morphogenic Serum, Omnicellular Genome, Stem Cell Culture.
$(thing)Extremophiles$()$(br2)Life at the edges: boiling vents, frozen vacuum, radiation. Unlocks tardigrade cultures.
pages.title: Extremophiles

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 70$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Genomics, Cryogenics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 8 Genome Sample.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the rate constant of an enzyme-catalysed reaction in a hyperthermophile living at 121 °C, using the Arrhenius law.
$(thing)Morphogenesis$()$(br2)How a blob of identical cells paints itself into a body: reaction and diffusion. Unlocks Turing morphogens.
pages.title: Morphogenesis

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 120$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Synthetic Biology, Complex Analysis.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Minimal Synthetic Cell.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the relative morphogen concentration C/C0 at x = 50 µm from the source, with D = 10 µm^2/s and degradation rate k = 0.001 /s.
$(thing)Neurobiology$()$(br2)Grow a brain in a dish and ask it what it thinks. Unlocks neural organoids.
pages.title: Neurobiology

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 110$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Synthetic Biology, Artificial General Intelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Stem Cell Culture.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the potassium equilibrium potential (V) of a neuron at 310 K with 5 mM K+ outside and 140 mM inside.
$(thing)Panspermia$()$(br2)Life carried between worlds - and between universes. Unlocks panspermia seeds and the omnicellular genome.
pages.title: Panspermia

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 450$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Abiogenesis, The Multiverse, The Island of Stability.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Spark of Life.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find how many spores in a meteorite survive an interplanetary journey of time t under cosmic radiation.
$(thing)Protein Folding$()$(br2)A chain finds its one shape among astronomically many. Unlocks folded protein crystals.
pages.title: Protein Folding

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 60$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Genomics, Quantum Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Recombinant DNA.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the time (s) a 30-residue chain would need to try every conformation if each residue has 3 states and each try takes 1e-13 s (Levinthal's paradox).
$(thing)Xenobiology$()$(br2)Life in other dimensions does not use DNA. Unlocks xenogenome work, Xenoplasm and silicon life.
pages.title: Xenobiology

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 130$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Synthetic Biology, Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 16 Genome Sample.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find how many bits a 100-letter genome stores in an 8-letter (hachimoji-like) genetic alphabet.

A spore built on silicon instead of carbon - a speculative chemistry that only works in the strange physics of the Bulk. It is glassy, faceted and very slightly warm, and it ticks quietly, as though growing at the pace of crystal.
pages.title: Silicon Life Spore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Silicon life has always been a thought experiment. In the Bulk, where chemistry runs differently, I seeded a minimal cell with a xenogenome and Xenoplasm on a bulk crystal. The spore that grew was neither carbon nor stone.
Made in $(item)Evolution Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Xenobiology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Metastatic Spore, Omnicellular Genome, Silicon Life Spore, Xenobot Swarm.

A small bright point that is the moment chemistry crossed into biology - self-replication, metabolism and a boundary, all arriving at once. It flickers unsteadily. Holding it feels like holding a match that might become a forest.
pages.title: Spark of Life

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Abiogenesis is the unsolved step. I put primordial soup, stellar plasma and the omega point in the Abiogenesis Crucible with telomerase, a minimal cell and quantum chlorophyll, and caught the instant it all started to copy itself.

Made in $(item)Abiogenesis Crucible$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Abiogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omnilex Seal, Omniscience Catalyst, Ontological Junction, Panspermia Seed, Transfinite Lattice Bolt.

A flask of cells that have yet to differentiate. Any of them could be a neuron, a muscle, a bone. The broth is warm and cloudy and seems to be thinking about its options. Under the microscope they look identical, and that sameness is exactly the point: every possibility is still open.
pages.title: Stem Cell Culture

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Synthetic biology lets me write life rather than read it. I took a genome sample, spliced in recombinant DNA to undo specialisation and used an engineered enzyme to hold the cells in their undecided state.

Made in $(item)Anomaly Resolution Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Synthetic Biology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Anomalous Strain Culture, CAR-T Cell Culture, Neural Organoid, Telomerase Complex, Tumour Microenvironment Organoid, Xenobot Swarm.

A culture of water bears, tiny eight-legged animals that survive vacuum, radiation and freezing by drying out and simply pausing being alive. In the jar they wander slowly through moss. Dried, they will wait for centuries.
pages.title: Tardigrade Culture

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Extremophiles taught me that life could survive almost anything. I used engineered enzymes to boost a tardigrade genome's repair genes, gave them moss to live in and froze a culture in superfluid helium. It woke up.
Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Extremophiles.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chronoplastic Gasket, Panspermia Seed, Telomerase Complex.

An enzyme that rebuilds telomeres - the protective caps at the ends of chromosomes that shorten every time a cell divides. Cells that have it do not age. The complex is small, pale and oddly cold, as if keeping time for itself.
pages.title: Telomerase Complex

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Telomerase is real; most adult cells have switched it off. The Evolution Engine ran a million generations of stem cells and tardigrades with Turing morphogens and Xenoplasm, while an arrow of time shard kept the clock running fast.

Made in $(item)Evolution Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Directed Evolution.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Immortal Cell Line, Omnilex Seal, Ontological Junction, Spark of Life, Transfinite Lattice Bolt.

A pair of chemicals, one that activates and diffuses slowly and one that inhibits and diffuses fast. Mixed on a dish they paint stripes and spots by themselves, exactly the reaction-diffusion patterns Turing predicted in 1952.
pages.title: Turing Morphogen

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Turing proposed that patterns in animals arise from reaction and diffusion. I extracted the morphogens from a minimal cell, set their handedness with a chiral crystal and tuned their rates using the complex plane. Spots appeared on the dish.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Morphogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Primordial Soup, Telomerase Complex.

Living machines a millimetre across, built from cells arranged in shapes no animal ever had. They walk, push, heal and even assemble copies of themselves from loose cells. They twitch in the jar, busy.
pages.title: Xenobot Swarm

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Xenobots were real: frog cells arranged by an evolutionary algorithm. I gave a general AI core stem cells and nanites to design with, and the Bioreactor built whatever shape it picked. Some of them built more of themselves.
Made in $(item)Evolution Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Synthetic Biology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Silicon Life Spore, Symbiont Culture, Xenobot Swarm.

A vial of something that is clearly a genome but is not DNA. The molecule folds the wrong way, uses letters I do not recognise and carries information more densely than any terrestrial code. It glows faintly in the dark.
pages.title: Xenogenome Sample

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I sampled a creature from another dimension expecting DNA and found something else. Life evolved under different physics, with a different chemistry of inheritance - and it was still readable.
Made in $(item)Gene Sequencer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Xenobiology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Silicon Life Spore, Xenobot Swarm, Xenoplasm.

Life fluid from another dimension. It does not use DNA, and its chemistry is foreign. It is warm, iridescent and moves on its own. Its molecules are built on a backbone no terrestrial cell would recognise, and their handedness alternates in ways that should be unstable. Somehow it thrives on that instability.
pages.title: Xenoplasm

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Xenobiology studies life without DNA. In the Bioreactor, I combined a Xenogenome Sample with foam substrate and nutrient broth, and the culture grew as no Earth life could.

Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Xenobiology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Metastatic Spore, Omnicellular Genome, Panspermia Seed, Silicon Life Spore, Telomerase Complex, Tumour Microenvironment Organoid.

Photosynthesis moves energy through its antenna with near-perfect efficiency by trying every path at once, coherently. A robin feels north through a pair of electrons entangled in a protein in its eye.

From these: $(item)Quantum Chlorophyll$() and the $(item)Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor$() - which Psionic Crystals now need. $(item)Tardigrade Cultures$() come from the extremophiles: animals that survive vacuum by pausing life itself.

Chemistry. A bond is not a stick between balls. Two atoms share an electron because the shared $(thing)wavefunction$() spread over both has lower energy than either alone - the same quantum mechanics as everything else in this book.
The $(item)Chemical Reactor$() is where it starts: $(fluid)Supercritical Solvent$() (gas-dense, liquid-thin) and $(item)Zeolite Catalysts$(), whose pores let only the right molecules meet.
Next: $(item)Molecular Orbital Lattices$() - the bond itself, frozen - and $(item)Chiral Crystals$(), molecules that come in a left hand and a right hand. Life, I will find, only ever uses one.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
A crystal full of molecule-sized pores; reactions that fit inside go faster.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().
Electron wavefunctions shared between atoms, frozen into a grid. This is what a chemical bond is.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().
Left-handed or right-handed, never both. Life only uses one hand.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().

Supramolecular chemistry builds with these: $(item)Metal-Organic Frameworks$() (more inner surface per gram than a football pitch), $(item)Noble Gas Clathrates$() (xenon caged in ice) and $(item)Self-Healing Polymers$().
Carbon one atom thick. Stronger than steel, conducts better than copper.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$()t.
Graphene rolled into tubes, the tubes twisted into rope.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().

Metal nodes, organic struts: a sponge with more inner surface than a football pitch per gram.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().

Cut it and the chains find each other again.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().

A tower of fractionation trays wound with chronosteel coils. Pour in every fluid one mod has and it boils them together, tray after tray, until what is left is a single fluid that stands for all of them: that mod's Essence.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 5$() machine.

pages.text: This controller is too complex for a crafting grid. Build it on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts.
Distils every fluid of one mod into that mod's $(fluid)Essence$(), which the $(item)Pleroma Confluence$() wants. JEI lists, mod by mod, which fluids go in.

pages.name: Essence Distillery
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().
$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 4 and 4 outputs).
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

Pleroma is everything at once - and that now includes every fluid of every mod installed. They do not each go into the $(item)Pleroma Confluence$(): first, every mod's fluids are distilled together in the $(item)Essence Distillery$() into that mod's $(fluid)Essence$() - one fluid that stands for all of them.

Each distillation takes up to twelve of one mod's fluids (16,000 mB of each) and gives 1,000 mB of Essence. A mod with more fluids is distilled in parts, and the parts (4,000 mB of each) into the whole Essence. JEI lists every mod's distillations; new mods' fluids join in by themselves. Only fluids that fit in a bucket count, and a server can leave fluids or mods out (essenceBlacklist).

The Confluence then wants 64,000 mB of every mod's Essence beside its million of each of this mod's fluids. Essences live in tanks and pipes only: a containment cell cannot remember whose Essence it held.

Replace the electron and chemistry changes. A $(thing)positron$() makes positronium - an atom of matter and antimatter - and $(item)Positronium Hydride$() is a molecule of it. A $(thing)muon$() is 200 times heavier than an electron, so a $(item)Muonic Catalyst$() squeezes atoms close enough to fuse cold.
A $(item)Room-Temperature Superconductor$() - hydrogen packed into a framework - carries current with zero resistance and no cryogenics.
A molecule made of a hydrogen atom and an atom of matter bound to antimatter. It lasts a nanosecond - unless you trap it.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().
Swap an electron for a muon and atoms shrink 200 times - close enough to fuse cold.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().
Zero resistance without cryogenics. Physicists have chased this for a century.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().

$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Positronium Hydride$(): Unbihexium Ingot$(li)$(item)Muonic Catalyst$(): Flerovium Ingot, Stellar Singularity$(li)$(item)Room-Temperature Superconductor$(): Neural Organoid, Transfinite Coil Block
Past uranium, elements get heavier and shorter-lived - until, theory says, an island: nuclei with $(thing)magic numbers$() of protons and neutrons, closed shells that hold them together.

The $(item)Nuclide Forge$() fires heavy ions from the r-process into a target. $(item)Flerovium$() (element 114) first, then $(item)Unbihexium$() (126), the heart of the island. Hypernova Alloy and Transcendent Metal now need them.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
Element 114, held together by magic numbers of protons and neutrons.$(br2)Made in $(item)Nuclide Forge$().
Element 126, the heart of the island of stability. Nothing should be this heavy and last this long.$(br2)Made in $(item)Nuclide Forge$().

$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Flerovium Ingot$(): Dimensional Residue, Transcendent Metal Ingot, Transcendent Plasma, Unbihexium Ingot$(li)$(item)Unbihexium Ingot$(): Dimensional Residue, Hypernova Alloy Ingot, Panspermia Seed

Sixty carbon atoms bonded into the shape of a football - twelve pentagons and twenty hexagons - with a hollow centre big enough to trap one more atom. It is round, slippery and perfectly symmetrical, and the hollow seems to be waiting for something.
pages.title: Buckyball Cage

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Heating graphene with blaze powder, I expected soot. Instead the sheets curled into closed spheres, and cooled in superfluid helium they stayed that way - the same cages Kroto and Smalley found in vaporised graphite.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Nanochemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Minimal Synthetic Cell, Noble Gas Clathrate, Positronium Hydride.

Graphene sheets rolled seamlessly into tubes a few nanometres across, then twisted together into a rope. Each tube is far stronger than steel; the bundle feels like silk and refuses to snap. Pulled taut, it sings faintly.
pages.title: Carbon Nanotube Bundle

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Graphene curled on its own along the edges of an orbital lattice, so I gave it more lattice and an ionic liquid to roll in. The tubes came out closed and clean, and twisted into rope as they dried.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Nanochemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Metal-Organic Framework, Self-Healing Polymer.

The strongest acid that can be bottled. It protonates almost anything yet is gentle on glass, because its conjugate base is so stable it does not attack. It is clear and calm in the flask. It is one of the few acids that is strong and polite at the same time.
pages.title: Carborane Superacid

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Carborane acids are a million times stronger than sulfuric. Electrolysing an Electride Crystal with chiral crystal and ionic liquid, I made one strong enough to protonate anything.
Made in $(item)Electrolytic Cell$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superacids.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Positronium Hydride, Primordial Soup.

A crystal that comes in only one hand. Like my left and right palms, its mirror image cannot be rotated to match it. Living things use left-handed amino acids and right-handed sugars, and nobody fully knows why. This one twists light passing through it, always the same way.
pages.title: Chiral Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Molecular orbitals let me predict which hand a molecule would take. Seeding an orbital lattice with amethyst and a quantum dot in supercritical solvent, I found the crystals all came out with the same handedness. I stopped calling it an accident after the tenth batch.

Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Carborane Superacid, Coherent Wiring Harness, Engineered Enzyme, Metal-Organic Framework, Primordial Soup, Turing Morphogen.

A salt in which the negative ions are not atoms at all but bare electrons, sitting in cavities of the lattice like eggs in a carton. It is dark, glossy and conducts strangely, and seems to give up electrons at the slightest provocation.
pages.title: Electride Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pushing electrons into Cherenkov quartz with redstone current, while superfluid helium held the lattice cold and still, I found that some electrons stayed behind in empty sites with no atom to belong to. The Electrolytic Cell had made an electride.
Made in $(item)Electrolytic Cell$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Electrochemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Carborane Superacid, Room-Temperature Superconductor.

Element 114, a superheavy metal held together by a near-magic number of protons. Real flerovium lasts seconds; this ingot lasts indefinitely because its neutron count sits right on the island. It is improbably dense and faintly warm.
pages.title: Flerovium Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The island of stability predicts superheavy nuclei that live long. I fed r-process clusters and neutronium into the Nuclide Forge with muons to tighten the nuclei and quark-gluon plasma to supply neutrons, and something came out that did not immediately decay.
Made in $(item)Nuclide Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Island of Stability.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Transcendent Metal Ingot, Transcendent Plasma, Unbihexium Ingot.

The field that drove cosmic inflation, stretching the universe exponentially in a fraction of a second. Bottled, it trembles with stored expansion, as if wanting to make everything around it larger. It is hot, restless and very light.
pages.title: Inflaton Field

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Guth's inflation needs a field to drive it. Distilling dimensional residue at the very top of the spire, I captured a fraction that kept trying to expand its container. The inflaton, caught before it could decay.

Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Fractional Distillation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Dimensional Singularity, Inflaton Condensate, Pocket Universe, Universe Seed.

A salt that is liquid at room temperature. It conducts electricity, does not evaporate, and dissolves almost anything. It is clear, slightly viscous and faintly warm. Chemists call such salts designer solvents, because they can be tuned for almost any task.
pages.title: Ionic Liquid

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Electrolysing quartz with supercritical solvent in the Electrolytic Cell, I got a salt that stayed liquid. An ionic liquid, perfect for further chemistry.
Made in $(item)Electrolytic Cell$().$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Singularity, Autocatalytic Broth, Carbon Nanotube Bundle, Carborane Superacid, Metal-Organic Framework, Self-Healing Polymer.
Sodium melted at 98 °C. It carries heat far better than water and boils only at 883 °C, which is why fast reactors use it as coolant, though it burns in air.
pages.title: Liquid Sodium

pages.text: Made in $(item)Electrolytic Cell$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Electrochemistry.
The lightest metal, won from brine. Soft enough to cut with a knife; it floats on oil and burns crimson.
pages.title: Lithium Ingot

pages.text: Made in $(item)Electrolytic Cell$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Electrochemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Lithium-6 Ingot.

A scaffold of copper nodes and organic struts so open that a single gram of it hides more inner surface than a football pitch. Gas soaks into it like water into a sponge. It is feather-light and full of rooms.
pages.title: Metal-Organic Framework

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Supramolecular chemistry lets molecules assemble themselves. Copper ions met nanotube struts and chiral linkers in an ionic liquid, and each found its place without my help. The framework grew the way frost grows on glass.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Supramolecular Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Morphogenic Serum, Room-Temperature Superconductor.
Every fluid of one mod distilled together into a single liquid. It tastes, reportedly, of everything its authors ever put in a tank.
pages.title: Mod Essence

pages.text: One fluid for each mod installed: every fluid of that mod distilled together in the $(item)Essence Distillery$(). The Pleroma Confluence wants 64,000 mB of each mod's Essence. Essences live in tanks and pipes only.

Electron clouds shared across a whole grid of atoms, frozen in place so I can finally see what a bond is: not a stick between balls but a wavefunction spread over both, lower in energy than either alone. The lattice shimmers faintly where the orbitals overlap.
pages.title: Molecular Orbital Lattice

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Solving the Schrodinger equation for a molecule taught me where the electrons sit. I used a qubit to encode that solution and grew the crystal around it on a zeolite template in supercritical solvent, so the orbitals set exactly where the mathematics put them.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Carbon Nanotube Bundle, Chiral Crystal, Folded Protein Crystal, Gene Sequencer.

A capsule of molecules in which electrons are replaced by muons, two hundred times heavier. The orbitals shrink accordingly, and two nuclei that would never fuse at room temperature are pulled close enough to tunnel into one. It feels oddly heavy for its size.
pages.title: Muonic Catalyst

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Muon-catalysed fusion was known in the 1950s; its problem is that muons are short-lived and get stuck. Using a noble gas clathrate to hold the fuel, quark-gluon plasma to make muons and a monopole to free them, I got the catalyst to work cycle after cycle.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Exotic Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Flerovium Ingot, Stellar Singularity.

A cage of ice with a xenon atom trapped in every cell, held not by bonds but by the plain fact that it cannot get out. The noble gases are supposed to be aloof; caged like this they are merely patient. It fizzes slightly as it warms.
pages.title: Noble Gas Clathrate

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Ice frozen around buckyball templates in superfluid helium formed cages of a very particular size. Noble gas filled them before I could seal the reactor, and stayed. Clathrates were not a goal - they were a pleasant accident.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Supramolecular Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Muonic Catalyst, Primordial Soup.
$(thing)Quantum Chemistry$()$(br2)Solve the Schrödinger equation for a molecule and you have its chemistry. Unlocks orbital lattices and chiral crystals.
pages.title: Quantum Chemistry

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 35$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Chemical Bonding, Quantum Entanglement.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Qubit.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the energy of the n = 2 level of the hydrogen atom from the Schrödinger equation.
$(thing)Superacids$()$(br2)Acids a million million times stronger than sulfuric - strong enough to protonate almost anything.
pages.title: Superacids

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 50$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Electrochemistry, High-Energy Particle Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Electride Crystal.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the Hammett acidity H0 of an acid in which the indicator (pK of BH+ = -10.1) is 100 times more protonated than not.
$(thing)Room-Temperature Superconductivity$()$(br2)Cooper pairs that hold together at room temperature, inside a hydrogen-rich framework.
pages.title: Room-Temperature Superconductivity

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 110$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Supramolecular Chemistry, Mass Manipulation.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Metal-Organic Framework.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the BCS critical temperature of a hydride superconductor from its Debye temperature and electron-phonon coupling.
$(thing)Supramolecular Chemistry$()$(br2)Molecules that build themselves into cages, frameworks and machines. Unlocks MOFs, clathrates and self-healing polymers.
pages.title: Supramolecular Chemistry

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 60$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Nanochemistry, Topological Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Graphene Sheet.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the Gibbs energy of binding (kJ/mol) of a host-guest complex with association constant K = 1e6 at 298 K.

A rubbery strip that, cut cleanly in two, slowly finds itself again. Its chains carry reversible bonds that break and reform, so pressing the halves together lets them rebond across the seam. It is warm and a little sticky at the cut.
pages.title: Self-Healing Polymer

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wanted a material that repaired itself the way skin does. Nanotube rope gave it strength, slime gave it reversible bonds, and a topological circuit board gave the bonds a pattern to restore. The first sample healed overnight.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Supramolecular Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Minimal Synthetic Cell.

A fluid past its critical point, neither liquid nor gas. It diffuses like a gas and dissolves like a liquid, getting into every pore. It is warm and almost invisible. Industry uses supercritical water and carbon dioxide to dissolve what nothing else will.
pages.title: Supercritical Solvent

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Heating charcoal and water past their critical point in the Chemical Reactor, the water became supercritical, dissolving things it never could before.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chiral Crystal, Graphene Sheet, Ionic Liquid, Molecular Orbital Lattice, Zeolite Catalyst.

Element 126, the heart of the island of stability, where magic numbers for both protons and neutrons line up. Nothing this heavy should last; this does. Its surface is a dull silver that seems to swallow light.
pages.title: Unbihexium Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Flerovium on its own is only the shore of the island. Pushing further meant adding supernova debris, positronium hydride to supply energy and quark-gluon plasma for neutrons. The Nuclide Forge produced element 126 and it stayed.
Made in $(item)Nuclide Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Island of Stability.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Hypernova Alloy Ingot, Panspermia Seed.

An aluminosilicate crystal riddled with channels the width of a single molecule. Anything that fits inside is held in exactly the right pose to react, so reactions that would idle in open air happen in a blink. It is light, chalky and faintly gritty, like pumice that remembers being a mineral.
pages.title: Zeolite Catalyst

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Clay and quartz dissolved in supercritical solvent recrystallised into a sponge of perfect pores. With a pinch of Cherenkov quartz as a template the channels came out uniform, and molecules small enough to enter came out changed.

Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Chemical Bonding.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Autocatalytic Broth, Bioreactor, Engineered Enzyme, Graphene Sheet, Molecular Orbital Lattice, Nutrient Broth.
A heavy-ion accelerator firing into a spinning target: fuses nuclei into elements beyond the periodic table, aiming for the island of stability.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 4$() machine.
pages.title: Nuclide Forge

pages.text: This controller is too complex for a crafting grid. Build it on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts.
Fuses superheavy elements - Flerovium and Unbihexium - from the r-process.

Converts mass entirely into energy, E = mc^2, regulated by dilithium crystals. Nothing more efficient exists.$(br2)Generates power.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.
pages.title: Matter-Antimatter Annihilation Reactor

pages.text: $(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

When a particle meets its antiparticle, both vanish and all of their rest mass becomes energy - mostly gamma rays, via E = mc^2. Fission releases under 0.1% of the mass; annihilation releases 100%. One gram of antimatter matches dozens of kilotons of TNT.

Fuel log: it burns $(item)Antimatter Pellets$() (with a $(item)Dilithium Crystal$() as regulator) at 131,072 FE/t, or a full $(item)Annihilation Core$() at 524,288 FE/t.$(br2)It needs superfluid helium cooling. Do not skip this.

pages.name: Matter-Antimatter Annihilation Reactor
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().
$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (2 item and 1 fluid inputs, 0 and 1 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Neutrino Flux.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Held in a Penning trap. Do not let it touch anything.$(br2)Made in $(item)Antimatter Penning Trap$().
Porous to antimatter. It regulates annihilation reactions.$(br2)Made in $(item)Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector$().$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Dilithium Ore in the Nether.
A controlled matter-antimatter reaction in a box.$(br2)Made in $(item)Antimatter Penning Trap$().

Traps the ghost particles that pass through planets without noticing. Trillions cross my hand each second, and now I can keep some.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.
pages.title: Neutrino Condenser

pages.text: Neutrinos are near-massless leptons that feel only the weak force (and gravity). A light-year of lead would stop only about half of them. Real detectors use kilotons of water or ice and catch a handful a day. The $(item)Neutrino Condenser$() is, frankly, cheating.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.
$(thing)Machine data$(): a single-block machine (4 item and 1 fluid inputs, 1 and 1 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Neutrino Flux, Proton Decay Residue, Sterile Neutrino.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Recreates the crushing interior of a collapsed star: neutronium, metallic hydrogen and quark matter. Each one a state of matter no lab on Earth has held.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 4$() machine.
pages.title: Neutron Star Forge

pages.text: Note to self: this controller is too complex for a crafting grid. It has to be built on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts before ordering anything.

Why it matters: a neutron star packs more than a Sun's mass into a city-sized sphere. Gravity crushes electrons into protons, leaving neutrons held up only by degeneracy pressure. Deeper in, neutrons may dissolve into free quarks. A teaspoon would weigh about a billion tonnes.

pages.name: Neutron Star Forge
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().

$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 4 and 4 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Block of Neutronium, Bounce Core, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Frozen Photon, Liquid Metallic Hydrogen, Magnetar Shard, Pulsar Timing Crystal, Quark Star Core, Supernova Remnant.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

A controlled matter-antimatter reaction inside a box. Matter and antimatter meet and convert entirely into energy, the most efficient fuel possible. Dilithium slows the reaction so it releases steadily rather than all at once. It glows white-hot, but the box stays cool.
pages.title: Annihilation Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Antimatter Penning Trap I let antimatter seep through Dilithium Crystal into a superfluid helium bath. Instead of a crater, it gave me a steady glow I could tap for power.
Made in $(item)Antimatter Penning Trap$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Annihilation Power.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Neutrino Flux.
One extra quark in every billion pairs. Everything that was not annihilated grew out of that one part in a billion.
pages.title: Baryon Asymmetry Crystal

pages.text: Made in $(item)Quark-Gluon Collider$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Leptogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Baryogenesis Seed, Pocket Universe, Universe Seed.
A universe crushed to the Planck density, where the quantum geometry of space turned the collapse around.
pages.title: Bounce Core

pages.text: Made in $(item)Neutron Star Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Big Crunch & the Big Bounce.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Universe Seed.

A slab of neutronium that should, by rights, explode back into a cloud of free neutrons the moment it leaves a star. The spacetime-alloy frame keeps the pressure on, so the plate stays degenerate: neutrons packed shoulder to shoulder, refusing by the Pauli principle to be squeezed any further.
pages.title: Degenerate Armour Plate

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Neutronium decompresses violently outside a star, so I tried caging a block in spacetime alloy and letting the Casimir Vacuum Press hold the vacuum around it. The neutrons stayed locked. Anything that can survive a compact star's interior can survive me.
Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Stellar Containment Plate, Theoretical Notes II.
Walls built to hold a region where escape velocity reaches light speed. Nothing leaves through a horizon; the walls are for what has not fallen in yet.
pages.title: Horizon Containment

pages.text: Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Accretion Disk Reactor, Horizon Cage.
Gold, platinum and lanthanides made in a second by the rapid neutron capture of a neutron-star merger, and thrown out at a fifth of the speed of light.
pages.title: Kilonova Ash

pages.text: Made in $(item)Reflecting Telescope$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Kilonovae.

A fragment of a magnetar, a neutron star with a magnetic field a thousand trillion times stronger than Earth's. Near it, atoms are stretched into needles and empty space becomes birefringent. It would wipe a credit card from the Moon, and it pulls iron from across the room.
pages.title: Magnetar Shard

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Through the Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector I reached toward a magnetar and caught a shard. Dilithium Crystal and Sterile Neutrino kept the field from tearing it apart on the way back.

Made in $(item)Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Miniature Pulsar, Pulsar Timing Crystal, Residual Starlight, Stellar Singularity.

Hydrogen compressed until it becomes a metal. At pressures found in the cores of gas giants, the electrons break free and conduct like copper. It flows silvery and heavy, and may be a room-temperature superconductor.
pages.title: Liquid Metallic Hydrogen

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Wigner and Huntington predicted metallic hydrogen in 1935. Crushing degenerate matter with superfluid helium in the Neutron Star Forge, I found hydrogen that conducted like a metal.
Made in $(item)Neutron Star Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Metallic Hydrogen Ingot.

Hydrogen compressed until its electrons are shared freely, like a metal. In the cores of Jupiter and Saturn it is the dominant form. It is probably metastable at ordinary pressure, and conducts electricity and heat beautifully. The ingot is mirror-bright and surprisingly light.
pages.title: Metallic Hydrogen Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Bose-Einstein Condenser, I pressed Liquid Metallic Hydrogen between Casimir Plates and cooled it. When the pressure was released, it held its metallic state. Probably. I have kept an eye on it.
Made in $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Room-Temperature Superconductor, Theoretical Notes III.

A stream of ghost particles, trillions of which pass through me every second. They barely interact with anything, so the flux is invisible, weightless and almost impossible to stop. Only rarely does one leave a blue flash.
pages.title: Neutrino Flux

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pauli predicted the neutrino to save energy conservation. The Neutrino Condenser caught the rare few that interacted with its Cherenkov quartz, and slowly accumulated them into a flux.

Made in $(item)Matter-Antimatter Annihilation Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Neutrino Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Gold Ingot, Lepton Triplet, Magnetar Shard, Pulsar Timing Crystal, R-Process Cluster, Standard Model Singularity, Supernova Remnant.

A cube of compacted neutronium, matter in which electrons and protons have been crushed together into neutrons. It is almost impossibly dense for its size, and dropping it on a floor would be a mistake. The surface is a smooth, dull grey.
pages.title: Block of Neutronium

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Storing loose neutronium ingots wasted space, so I pressed nine together. The block holds its shape with nothing but the strong force, and it makes a convenient compact supply.

Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Bounce Core, Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Degenerate Armour Plate, Dimensional Residue, Magnetar Shard, Neutron Star Forge, Neutronium Ingot, Proton Decay Residue and more.

A crystal that ticks with the precision of a millisecond pulsar, the most regular natural clocks known. Its pulses are so stable that any drift reveals a passing gravitational wave. It flashes a faint blue on every beat, and I set my watches by it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Pulsar Timing Ore in the Accretion Frontier (Pulsar Field); dropped by the Pulsar Wisp (the Accretion Frontier (Pulsar Field)).
pages.title: Pulsar Timing Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Neutron Star Forge I spun a Magnetar Shard up inside quartz, with a Chronon Capacitor to stabilise the rhythm. Neutrino Flux synchronised it with the stars, and the beat matched to the nanosecond.

Made in $(item)Neutron Star Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Pulsar Timing Ore$(), in veins through the rock.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Pulsar Wisp.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Pulsar Beacon chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Causality Loop Engine, Chronal Accelerator, Exotic Matter Crystal, Horizon Containment, Multiverse Shard, Temporal Singularity.

The heart of a star too dense even for neutrons, where the neutrons have dissolved into free quarks. Strange matter may be stable here. It is the densest thing short of a singularity, and holding it makes my wrist ache even through the containment.
pages.title: Quark Star Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Neutron Star Forge, I compressed a Block of Neutronium with strange matter and supernova remnants, until the neutrons broke apart into quarks. Quark-Gluon Plasma bonded the result together.

Made in $(item)Neutron Star Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Dimensional Residue, Hypernova Plasma, Miniature Quasar, Reality Anchor, Stellar Singularity.

$(thing)Kilonovae$()$(br2)When two neutron stars merge, a few hundredths of a solar mass of neutron-rich matter is flung out, and in a second it captures neutrons up to gold and platinum. Its radioactive glow fades over days.
pages.title: Kilonovae

A neutrino that feels no force except gravity: no weak interaction, no electromagnetism, nothing. It passes through anything without a trace, which makes it a candidate for dark matter. Keeping hold of one is like trying to catch smoke with a sieve.

pages.name: Pulsed Magnet Lab
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().
$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 4 and 4 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Magnetar Crust Fragment, Magnetic Monopole, Magnetite, Samarium-Cobalt Magnet.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

A current makes a magnetic field. Around a long straight wire it circles the wire, and its strength falls with distance: B = μ₀I/(2πr). Ten amps give 40 µT five centimetres away - about the strength of the planet's own field.

The $(item)Gauss Meter$() reads the field where you stand: the planet's (25 to 65 µT in the Overworld, none in the Nether or the End) and any magnets near you (block tag $(thing)magnetic$(): lodestones, and more to come).

A changing field drives a current: spin a coil of N turns in a field B and it gives ε = NBAω·sin ωt. Every generator works this way. The iron core that guides the field is built from thin $(item)Electrical Steel Laminations$(), so the changing field cannot stir currents inside it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Core Magnetite Ore in the Planetary Interior (Geodynamo Core); dropped by the Geodynamo Wraith (the Planetary Interior (Geodynamo Core)).

$(item)Magnetite$() comes from raw iron roasted with charcoal, or from the Spectrograph's radium assay. Pressed with clay and redstone it makes $(item)Ferrite Magnets$(): iron oxide that stays magnetised.

Iron is ferromagnetic because its atoms' spins line up by themselves - until a critical temperature, 1043 K for iron, shakes them apart. Above it the susceptibility is χ = C/(T − T_c). The item tag $(thing)ferromagnetic$() lists what a field pulls on, for the Magnetized effect to come.
Spin a coil in a magnet's field and it drives a current: ε = NBAω. With the same coil and load, the power goes as ε², so a magnet three times stronger gives about ten times the power.

The $(item)Induction Generator$() burns fuel to spin its coil. Put a magnet in its second slot - a Ferrite Magnet gives 24 FE/t, Samarium-Cobalt 180, Neodymium 250 - and flowing water beside it, like a water wheel, adds half again for every side.
A permanent magnet is set by a field stronger than its $(thing)coercivity$(), and keeps what it was given. Ferrite needs about 0.35 T, neodymium-iron-boron 1.2 T, samarium-cobalt 2 T.

The rare earths come from $(item)Monazite Sand$(), which the Spectrograph picks out of ordinary sand and separates into $(item)Rare Earth Oxide$(). Monazite carries a little thorium: it is weakly radioactive.
The $(item)Magnetizer$() gives 0.6 T from its coil alone. An iron core multiplies a coil's field: each block of iron (or any block tagged $(thing)magnetic$()) touching the Magnetizer adds 0.35 T.

Push a conducting fluid across a magnetic field and it becomes the armature of a generator: the field drives current across the flow, into $(item)MHD Electrodes$() on the channel walls. No turbine, no moving parts.

Power per cubic metre is p = σu²B²k(1 − k): conductivity, speed squared, field squared. The load factor k is the share of the voltage the outside circuit takes; one half gives the most - unless the current density, j = σuB(1 − k), would arc the electrodes away.
Brine conducts a little, magma a little less but the Interior has oceans of it, and $(fluid)Stellar Plasma$() conducts ten thousand times better. The pumps limit how fast a dense fluid can be driven.

A proton crossing a magnetic field circles, and how often it circles - $(thing)f = qB/2πm$() - does not depend on how fast it goes. Lawrence saw what that meant: put an RF voltage at that frequency across a gap, and the proton is kicked every half turn, spiralling out faster and faster in step.

Set the field B, then the RF to 15.25 MHz per tesla. At the edge, 0.75 m out, the beam has $(thing)E = (qBR)²/2m$(). But relativity: the faster it goes the heavier it is, its frequency drops, and over its hundreds of turns it slips out of phase. Past 90° the gap slows it instead. Tune a hair low to split the difference - the classical cyclotron runs out at about ten MeV.
Five MeV protons on iron make $(item)Cobalt-57$() (⁵⁷Fe(p,n)⁵⁷Co): the Pound-Rebka source, two at a time, without radium. Above 2.2 T the iron yoke saturates; more than 2 kW of beam melts the target.

Two circuits, each a capacitor and a coil, each ringing at its own frequency. Tune the primary to the secondary and energy sloshes across - and appears at a voltage higher by $(thing)√(C₁/C₂)$(): kilovolts in, megavolts out.

The secondary of the $(item)Tesla Coil$() rings at 159 kHz. Set the primary capacitance and where its spiral is tapped (inductance grows as the turns squared) so it rings there too; a few per cent off and most of the energy stays in the primary. In air an arc reaches about a metre for every 700 kV.

Its arcs fix the air's nitrogen into nitrates - the Birkeland-Eyde process that made the first fertilisers: water becomes bone meal. Arcs over 2.5 m fuse sand into glass, as lightning makes fulgurites: Fused Silica, without the Sun.
Stand well clear. A running coil strikes anyone within six blocks of it.
Maxwell's equations put electricity, magnetism and light into one theory: changing fields make each other, and a wave of field carries itself across empty space at $(thing)c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀)$().

The $(item)Laser Cutter$() cuts copper into $(item)Waveguides$() (microwaves along a pipe), $(item)Bitter Plates$() and $(item)Rail Armatures$(). A $(item)Faraday Cage Mesh$() keeps fields out - carried in the off hand it shields you from Decoherence. $(item)Mu-Metal$(), nickel-iron so permeable the field runs through it instead of you, does the same for being Magnetized.
$(item)Litz Wire$(), woven so every strand takes its turn at the surface, winds the coils of the Tokamak.
Steady magnets top out near 45 tesla. For more, dump a room of capacitors into a coil for a few milliseconds: $(thing)B = μ₀NI/L$().

The $(item)Pulsed Magnet Lab$() grows a storey for every stack of Bitter plates (1 to 7): more copper and cooling to soak up the pulse's heat (ΔT ∝ NI²t/storeys). Past 400 K the coil melts; past 100 T the magnetic pressure B²/2μ₀ tears it apart.
At 40 T it magnetises samarium-cobalt in bulk. At 80 T, with magnetar crust and cosmic ray shards, it searches for $(item)Magnetic Monopoles$() - and now and then, finds one.

In a strong field and the cold, the Hall resistance of a sheet of electrons sits on plateaus at $(thing)h/(νe²)$() - 25 812.807 Ω for ν = 1, exact to a part in a billion, because it counts a topological number. The Laser Cutter cuts $(item)Hall Bar Chips$() from silicon and gold.

A collapsing star keeps its magnetic flux: its field grows as $(thing)(R/r)²$(). A magnetar's is 10¹¹ tesla. Its crust, found in the Accretion Frontier's Pulsar Field, cracks in starquakes; Dirac showed a single magnetic charge would have to be a multiple of h/e.
Two rails and an armature between them: current up one rail, across, down the other. The field between the rails pushes the armature out with $(thing)F = ½L′I²$() - a railgun.

Set the current and the armature's mass. It leaves at $(thing)v = √(2FL/m)$() and strikes the target with a shock of about $(thing)½ρv²$(). Graphite shocked between 15 and 40 GPa becomes $(item)Lonsdaleite$(), hexagonal diamond, as in meteorite craters; sand and coal at 50-90 GPa fuse into moissanite. Each shot spends a Rail Armature. Above 3 MA the rails erode.
A resonant transformer: a spark-gap primary ringing in tune with a tall secondary steps a few kilovolts up to millions, and the toroid throws arcs metres long.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.
pages.title: Tesla Coil

pages.text: $(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

Tune the primary - its capacitance and the turns tapped - to ring at the secondary's 159 kHz. In tune, the voltage steps up as √(C₁/C₂) and the arcs grow a metre for every 700 kV. Stand clear: anyone within six blocks of a running coil gets struck.

pages.name: Tesla Coil
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().
$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 4 and 4 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Bone Meal, Fused Silica.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
I threw the Omnilex into the Quantum Foam. It shattered into everything I had ever made, and the pieces became a shape with too many directions. It asked me whether I understood.

It took me into itself - $(thing)the Living Proof$(), eight chambers, each a law that had to be understood before it opened. Then the proof melted, and it fought me as a creature, closing itself into questions twice.

It left me the $(item)Proof of Everything$(). With it and $(thing)Beyond the Omega$() researched, the Omnilex Engine can do the impossible - and open the way to the Transcendental. Dying in the proof costs nothing but the attempt.
What Alpha Omega left behind: a proof that you understood. The Transcendental opens only to it.$(br2)Made in $(item)Omega Simulator$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Proof of Everything$(): Logos Thread, Omega Simulator
$(thing)Dimension data: The Living Proof$()$(br2)$(thing)Nature$(): Gravity 1 g, 3 spatial dimensions, time x1, ordinary vacuum.$(br2)$(thing)Law$(): no attunement - it is the fight itself.

The source code has a floor, and something lies beneath it. The $(item)Axiom Distiller$() boils reality down past its code to the axioms underneath, and condenses them into fragments.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 7$() machine.
pages.title: Axiom Distiller

pages.text: What is an axiom? In mathematics, a statement accepted without proof - the bedrock every theorem is derived from. Change the axioms and you change what can be true. Holding a fragment of one is like holding a rule in my hand. It hums.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.
$(thing)Machine data$(): a single-block machine (5 item and 3 fluid inputs, 2 and 1 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Absolute Infinity, Axiom Fragment, Crystallised Law, Primordial Law.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Note to self: this machine breaks every law of physics and mathematics at once. While it runs, step into its heart and you fall out of reality.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 7$() machine.
pages.title: Axiomatic Breach Engine

pages.text: Too complex for any crafting grid. I built this controller on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts; I needed every one of them.

Two ways through. Forge an $(item)Axiom Key$() here - it is reusable, and takes you to Hyperdimensional Reality Space and back. Or run $(thing)Open Breach$() and, while the engine runs, simply walk into its centre.
Inside, reality shatters into shards that each obey different laws. I took a step and the rules changed under my boots. I am still not sure which laws I was standing in.

pages.name: Axiomatic Breach Engine
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().
$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 4 and 4 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Axiom Key, Paradox Residue.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Opens the breach to the space where laws are born. Use it to travel there and back.$(br2)Made in $(item)Axiomatic Breach Engine$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Axiom Key$(): Absolute Notes III, Axiom Key, Omnilex
The Reality Compiler showed that the universe runs on source code. Beneath the code are $(thing)axioms$() - the rules that decide what can be true at all. Physics is just their consequence.

Real mathematics agrees there are cracks. Godel proved any consistent system rich enough for arithmetic holds true statements it cannot prove; Russell found a set that both is and isn't its own member. The axioms are not as solid as they look.

So, the plan. To leave reality you must break all of them at once: build $(item)Aleph-Null Shards$(), the $(item)Godel Sentence$(), $(item)Russell Paradox Sets$() and $(item)Banach-Tarski Spheres$(), fuse them into $(item)Absolute Infinity$(), then distil $(item)Axiom Fragments$() and open the $(thing)Axiomatic Breach$().
The size of the natural numbers, made solid. Counting its facets never ends.$(br2)Made in $(item)Cantor Diagonalizer$().
"This statement cannot be proven." It is true, and no system can prove it.$(br2)Made in $(item)Cantor Diagonalizer$().
The set of all sets that do not contain themselves. Does it contain itself?$(br2)Made in $(item)Cantor Diagonalizer$().
Cut it into five non-measurable pieces, reassemble them, and you have two spheres.$(br2)Made in $(item)Cantor Diagonalizer$().
Larger than every infinity. It cannot be conceived - and yet here it is.$(br2)Made in $(item)Axiom Distiller$().
A shard of a foundational rule. Mathematics is built on these; so is reality.$(br2)Made in $(item)Omnilex Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Law Wraith.

$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Aleph-Null Shard$(): Aleph Glass, Axiom Distiller, Banach-Tarski Sphere, Cantor Key, Conceptual Singularity Compressor and more$(li)$(item)Godel Sentence$(): Absolute Notes I, Axiom Distiller, Axiomatic Breach Engine, Primordial Ocean Simulacrum, Russell Paradox Set and more$(li)$(item)Russell Paradox Set$(): Absolute Notes III, Dimensional Residue, Primordial Ocean Simulacrum, T...

$(thing)Dimension data: The Transcendental$()$(br2)$(thing)Nature$(): Gravity 1 g, 11 spatial dimensions, time x1, true vacuum vacuum.$(br2)$(thing)Carry$(): $(item)Identity Kernel$() - with it, Weakness and Mining Fatigue.
$(thing)Landmarks$(): Anomaly Vault Transcendental Expanse.
$(item)Omnipotent Edge$(): cuts through any armour and any invulnerability. Right-click erases the hostile creatures in front of you; sneak and right-click stops time around you.

$(item)Scepter of Singularities$(): right-click puts a singularity where you look. Sneak-right-click changes which: Black Hole (pulls in and crushes), White Hole (throws out), Tesseract (folds space - you are simply there), Entanglement (one strike, every linked foe), Big Bang (everything near the point at once).

The $(item)Raiment of Transcendence$() (Crown, Mantle, Greaves, Treads): each piece has its own gift; the whole set grants invulnerability, creative flight, and erases all dimension's laws effects on you.

The $(item)Ex Nihilo Engine$(): Defying Laws of Thermodynamics, creating energy from nothing, limitless. Over two billion FE every tick on every side, and it charges the energy items of everyone nearby.

The $(item)Lawgiver's Codex$(): open it and rewrite the place you stand in - its gravity, its time and weather, which creatures may appear and how strong they are; create creatures, or rewrite the one you were looking at. "Restore" puts the natural laws back.
The Omnipotence Core is not the end. Its $(thing)Shutdown Sequence$() destroys the Transcendental - and that is the way forward, not a loss.$(br2)What happens next, in order:

$(li)$(bold)The Sundering$(): the Core leaves $(item)Shards of Omnipotence$() and the $(item)Echo of the Transcendental$(). The old machines turn shards into $(item)Omnipotence Dust$(), $(item)Apeiron Ingots$(), $(item)Pleroma Crystal$() and $(item)Logos Thread$().$(li)$(bold)The Rekindling$(): those build the $(item)Pleroma Reconstitutor$(), the largest machine there is. Fed the Echo, it rebuilds the Transcendental.$(li)$(bold)The Forge$(): the reborn Core can $(thing)forge$() - by solving a simulated universe's constants of nature - what even Omnipotence could not simply make.

The last tier of materials, all forged at the reborn Core:$(li)$(item)Omnipotent Ingot$(), $(item)Crystal of Transcendence$(), $(item)Absolute Singularity$(), $(item)Eschaton Core$()$(li)the $(item)Omnipotent Edge$(), the $(item)Scepter of Singularities$(), the $(item)Raiment of Transcendence$() and the $(item)Dodecaract Excavator$()$(li)the $(item)Ex Nihilo Engine$() (endless power), the $(item)Lawgiver's Codex$(), the $(item)Censer of Entropy$() and the $(item)Equilibrium Lattice$()$(li)$(item)Eschaton Cells$() - every endgame item runs on their charge$(li)and at the very end, an $(item)Omnipotence Core$() of your own, with the $(item)Hand of the Demiurge$() to tune, wake and move it.
Each of these has its own chapter, which opens as you get there: The Sundering opens the shards' chapters, The Rekindling to the Forge's.

Cantor's trick, built in brass: list every number, then build one that differs from the n-th at its n-th digit - a number on no list. It manufactures infinities, then bigger ones.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 6$() machine.
pages.title: Cantor Diagonalizer

pages.text: $(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

It takes the computational power of a superintelligence and points it at infinity.$(br2)Odd result today: $(item)Banach-Tarski Spheres$() can be split and reassembled into two. In real maths that is a theorem, not a trick - the pieces are so strange that 'volume' stops applying to them.

$(thing)Machine data$(): a single-block machine (6 item and 2 fluid inputs, 2 and 0 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Absolute Infinity, Aleph-Null Shard, Banach-Tarski Sphere, Continuum Shard, Godel Sentence, Hilbert's Hotel Key, Hypersphere Fragment, Inaccessible Cardinal, Ordinal Stone, Russell Paradox Set, Surreal Number.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Cut it into five non-measurable pieces, reassemble them, and you have two spheres.$(br2)Made in $(item)Cantor Diagonalizer$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Banach-Tarski Sphere$(): Absolute Notes I, Axiomatic Breach Engine, Banach-Tarski Sphere, Transfinite Casing

The $(item)Conceptual Singularity Compressor$() takes whole stacks of everything a field of science has produced and compresses them into a single singularity of pure concept.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 6$() machine.
pages.title: Conceptual Singularity Compressor

pages.text: Too complex for any crafting grid. I built this controller on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts; I needed every one of them.

Each recipe eats whole stacks: nine slots of a field's products plus three tanks. Nothing here waits on a timer - it only costs what it costs. I fed it a decade of lab notes and it handed me back one glowing point.

The Omniscience Catalyst is made in the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from every singularity there is. Here, with cosmic neutronium or transfinite coils, catalysts are forged into $(item)Omnium$() in bulk - 128 catalysts and stacks of the late metals for one ingot, or 4 ingots from 128 with transfinite coils - with no 9x9 grid to fill by hand.

pages.name: Conceptual Singularity Compressor
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().

$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 4 and 4 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Cognitive Singularity, Dimensional Singularity, Eschaton Cell, Exotic Matter Singularity, Mathematics Singularity, Omnipotence Dust, Omnium Ingot, Quantum Singularity, Spacetime Singularity, Standard Model Singularity, Stellar Singularity, Temporal Singularity, Theory of Everything.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Every field ends the same way. The $(item)Conceptual Singularity Compressor$() takes whole stacks of everything it produced and compresses them into a $(item)Singularity$().
One for each field: $(li)mathematics$(li)the Standard Model$(li)spacetime$(li)stars$(li)dimensions$(li)time$(li)quantum$(li)cognition$(li)exotic matter

Four singularities plus the field capstones constructs the $(item)Theory of Everything$() - the unified theory physicists have chased for a century, sitting on my bench. That, the other five singularities, Absolute Infinity and the Omega Point fuse into the $(item)Omniscience Catalyst$().
The catalyst and stacks of every late-game metal make the $(item)Omnium Ingot$() - and the $(item)Omnilex$() is forged from four of them. It costs everything, but nothing here waits on a timer.
Every number, function, proof and infinity, compressed into one point.$(br2)Made in $(item)Conceptual Singularity Compressor$().
All nine singularities, fused. Holding it, you know everything - briefly.$(br2)Made in $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
A metal made of every concept there is. The last ingot.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
A singularity of something from another mod (or added by your pack).$(br2)
Quantum fields, gravity, strings and the Standard Model in one equation. It fits on a T-shirt.$(br2)Made in $(item)Conceptual Singularity Compressor$().

$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Mathematics Singularity$(): Absolute Infinity, Absolute Singularity, Omniscience Catalyst, Ontological Junction, Spacetime Bearing$(li)$(item)Omniscience Catalyst$(): Omnium Ingot, Pleroma Confluence$(li)$(item)Omnium Ingot$(): Absolute Frame Casing, Apeiron Ingot, Axiom Key, Block of Omnium, Omnilex and more$(li)$(item)Theory of Everything$(): Absolute Notes II, Cosmic Flux Coupler, Omniscience Catalyst

The creative items of other mods (infinite chests, tanks, energy cells...) are no longer simply handed out by the Core, nor kept in the Transcendental's reliquaries - those now hold the controllers of the great machines of the endgame.$(br2)Only the rebuilt Core's $(thing)FORGE$() can make creative items, each from Eschaton Cores, Omnipotent Ingots, Absolute Singularities and Transcendence Crystals - and each needs its own universe tuned.

Pack makers: the Forge finds creative items by itself (a list of known ones, and any item whose id says "creative"). The item tag $(thing)theoreticalsciences:forge_only$() adds items the search misses - or late-endgame items to keep behind the Forge - and $(thing)theoreticalsciences:forge_exempt$() takes out ones it picked up by mistake.
A pickaxe in the shape of a twelve-dimensional cube. It mines anything a netherite pickaxe can, far faster, and never wears out - it spends Eschaton Charge instead.

Sneak and use it to change mode; sneak and scroll to change its reach, from 3x3x3 to 33x33x33.$(li)$(bold)Single$(): one block at a time - any breakable block, broken at once, with its drops, whatever slows you down.$(li)$(bold)Area$(): breaking a block breaks the whole cube reaching into the wall behind it. The drops come straight to you.

$(li)$(bold)Ore Extraction$(): use it on a block, or in the air to work around yourself. Every ore in the cube is pulled out into your inventory - with the tool's Fortune or Silk Touch - and the stone it grew in takes its place. The rest of the rock is left as it was.

It respects spawn protection and claims, and never takes unbreakable blocks or blocks with contents. Pack makers can add ores with the block tag $(thing)theoreticalsciences:excavator_ores$() and protect blocks with $(thing)theoreticalsciences:excavator_ignored$().
Forged at the rebuilt Core. Sneak-use to choose any harmful effect of any mod, its level (up to 255), how long it lasts (up to an hour) and the radius of its cloud.
Use it on a creature to lay the effect on it; use it in the air to leave a lingering cloud of it where you look, up to 48 blocks away.

Everything beyond Omnipotence now has to be kept that way. Every endgame tool, weapon and piece of armour holds $(thing)Eschaton Charge$() - shown as a bar under it and in its tooltip - and spends it as it works.

With none left an item is $(thing)dormant$(): the $(item)Omnipotent Edge$() is only a blade, the $(item)Scepter$(), $(item)Codex$(), $(item)Censer$() and $(item)Hand$() refuse to act, and a piece of the $(item)Raiment$() grants no protection. The Raiment drains while worn and for every blow it keeps away.
An $(item)Eschaton Cell$() holds 100,000. Use it and it fills every endgame item you carry or wear, emptiest first; what is left stays in the cell. Things come out of the Forge full.

Cells come four at a time from the $(thing)Core Forge$(), or one at a time from the $(item)Concept Compressor$(), which condenses them out of Pleroma with an Eschaton Core and a Rekindled Spark held as catalysts.

$(li)Edge: 20 a hit, 400 Erasure, 600 Stasis, 5 a kill$(li)Scepter: 150-1500 a singularity$(li)Codex: 500 a law$(li)Censer: 200 a touch, 400 a cloud$(li)Hand: 250 an action$(li)Excavator: 5 a block, 20 an ore$(li)Raiment: 1 a second, 10 a point of damage$(br)Creative players spend nothing.

A sphere of Pleroma glass on a waist of Omnipotence casing, ringed in Logos coil and watched by four towers. It packs as much as the laws allow into as little space as they allow - right up to the edge of becoming a black hole - and repeats what you once forged by hand.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 5$() machine.
pages.title: Eschaton Foundry

pages.text: This controller is too complex for a crafting grid. Build it on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts.

Makes the $(item)Absolute Singularity$(), the $(item)Echo of the Transcendental$(), $(item)Eschaton Cells$() and the $(item)Eschaton Core$() - but only what its owner has forged by hand in the Core's Forge at least once. It costs far more than the Forge, and there is no downtime between each craft attempt.

pages.name: Eschaton Foundry
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().
