Every ingot of every installed mod (anything tagged c:ingots) has its own singularity, made in the $(item)Singularity Compactor$() - and the $(item)Omniscience Catalyst$() needs one of each, on top of its usual ingredients. Packs can add more (data/<namespace>/ts_singularities/*.json), with their own names, counts and colours; colours not given come from the item's texture.

When there are more singularities than the Extreme Assembly Table can hold, nine at a time are condensed (with a Micro Singularity) into a $(item)Singularity Cluster$() - and clusters into Hyperclusters - and the catalyst asks for those instead. JEI shows what this game needs. Clusters can be renamed with a resource pack or in ts_singularities/_clusters.json.

The $(item)Biosphere Compendium$() and the $(item)Primordial Harvest$() likewise take one of every meat, catch and mob drop - every crop, seed, fruit and flower - of every installed mod, as many as fit.

A femtoscale jig that holds a hundred tiny parts exactly in place while the Extreme Assembly Table joins them. It is small, heavy and covered in fine engraved channels, and it seems to settle into the hand like a tool that knows its job.
pages.title: Assembly Matrix

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Assembling parts smaller than a proton by hand is impossible. I combined photonic and quantum processors with a metamaterial frame and chronosteel so that the matrix positions every part itself while the table does the joining.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Hyperlattice Frame.

A capacitor that stores charge in the Higgs field itself rather than in the electric field between plates. It is a thousand times smaller than its femtoscale ancestor. The energy it holds changes the mass of anything nearby very slightly.
pages.title: Attoscale Capacitor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Femto Fabricator I wired a Femtoscale Capacitor to a Higgs Field Capacitor using Exotic Solder. The charge moved off the plates and into the Higgs field, shrinking the capacitor a thousandfold.

Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Assembly Lines.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Abiogenesis Crucible, Anomaly Containment Ward, Anomaly Resolution Engine, Autonomous Calibrator, Axiomatic Breach Engine, Burst Observatory, Causality Loop Engine, Conceptual Singularity Compressor and more.

An inductor wound from the field lines of a magnetic monopole, which have no south pole to close on. The energy it stores has nowhere to leak to. It is invisible to the eye, but compasses left nearby swing slowly round and point straight at it.
pages.title: Attoscale Inductor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Femto Fabricator I threaded a Femtoscale Inductor around a Magnetic Monopole with Exotic Solder. The monopole's field lines wound into the coil and never came out.

Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Assembly Lines.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Abiogenesis Crucible, Anomaly Containment Ward, Anomaly Resolution Engine, Autonomous Calibrator, Axiomatic Breach Engine, Burst Observatory, Causality Loop Engine, Conceptual Singularity Compressor and more.

A switch that changes between superposed states before it is asked to, because it anticipates its input. It is a thousand times smaller than a femtoscale transistor and faster by the same factor. It is invisible and very fast.
pages.title: Attoscale Transistor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Femto Fabricator, I joined a Femtoscale Transistor to a Superposition Crystal through a Topological Insulator with Exotic Solder. It began switching before the input arrived.

Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Assembly Lines.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Autonomous Calibrator, Cosmic Processor, Hyperdimensional Processor, Ontological Processor, Transfinite Processor.

An energy store built around the force between two plates in a vacuum. Between closely spaced conductors, fewer vacuum modes fit, so the outside pushes them together; this cell charges by tensioning that gap. It hums very faintly.
pages.title: Casimir Energy Cell

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Casimir plates press together with energy taken from nothing. Pairing them with a Chronon Capacitor in a chronosteel shell, I found I could store that tension and release it on demand.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Vacuum Energy Cell.

A plate of chronosteel and causal shield lattice that keeps cause and effect in the right order on either side. It feels slightly ahead of the moment, as though it knew I was going to touch it. Its surface is faintly lined.
pages.title: Causal Shielding Plate

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Time machines can leak effects before their causes. I layered a causal shield lattice on chronosteel and chronoplastic casing, and the plate kept the order straight.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.

A single, flawless crystal of Cherenkov quartz, grown slowly from a seed in superfluid helium. It is cylindrical, glowing faint blue along its length, and every atom in it lines up with its neighbours. It is ready to be sliced into wafers.
pages.title: Cherenkov Boule

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Lattice Growth Vat, I suspended a Lattice Seed Crystal in Superfluid Helium and fed it Cherenkov Quartz. The superfluid's zero viscosity let the atoms arrange themselves perfectly as the boule grew.
Made in $(item)Lattice Growth Vat$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cherenkov Wafer, Spacetime Slag, Warm Helium.

A lamp of Cherenkov quartz with glowstone at its heart, so the blue Cherenkov glow is amplified into a strong, clean light. It is the colour of a reactor pool, and as calming. It never flickers and never warms, and the blue makes every surface it touches look freshly cleaned.
pages.title: Cherenkov Lamp

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Cherenkov quartz alone glowed too faintly to light a room. Adding glowstone dust to a block of it pushed the glow into a proper lamp.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.

Diamond struts and threads of Cherenkov quartz, wound around a core of netherite scrap. The quartz glows the same blue that charged particles give off when they outrun light in water. It is a frame for a crystal that cannot hold itself together, rigid and faintly luminous.
pages.title: Cherenkov Lattice

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I needed scaffolding strong enough to pin a superposition in place. Diamond for rigidity, netherite for weight and Cherenkov quartz to keep the light moving gave me a frame that would not flinch.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Crystalline Matrix Ingot, Form of the Self.

A clear crystal with a refractive index so high that charged particles crossing it outrun the local speed of light. Each one leaves a cone of blue light behind it, the optical cousin of a sonic boom, so the stone glows faintly even in a dark chest.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Deepslate Cherenkov Quartz Ore in the Overworld.
pages.title: Cherenkov Quartz

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)My first piece came from a cracked chest in an observatory ruin, still glowing. Much later I learned to harvest it from the inside of a Pocket Universe in the Universe Forge, where young cosmic rays are plentiful and every grain of quartz lights up.

Made in $(item)Galton Board$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Deepslate Cherenkov Quartz Ore$(), in veins through the Overworld's deepslate.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Fallout Shelter Stores, Observatory, Observatory Ruin, Survey Benchmark chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Atomic Clock, Block of Cherenkov Quartz, Casimir Plate, Casimir Vacuum Press, Chemical Reactor, Cherenkov Boule, Cherenkov Lattice, Containment Field Glass and more.

Nine pieces of Cherenkov quartz fused into a single block that glows the soft blue of particles outrunning light in a medium. It is cool, translucent and slightly brighter in the dark than any ordinary stone should be.
pages.title: Block of Cherenkov Quartz

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Compacting Cherenkov quartz made storage easier and, as a bonus, the larger crystal glowed more strongly. I started building with it before I had a reason to.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cherenkov Lamp, Cherenkov Quartz, Neutrino Condenser, Photonic Lens, Proton Decay Residue, Pulsar Timing Crystal, Structure Assembler, Tachyon Resonator.
Seals a joint against time itself: what is inside ages at the machine's pace, not the world's.
pages.title: Chronoplastic Gasket

pages.text: Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Spacetime Bearing.

Nine chronosteel ingots fused into one block, a metal whose atoms keep slightly different time from their surroundings. It is cool, heavy and very slightly delayed, as if it reaches the hand a moment late.
pages.title: Block of Chronosteel

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Compacting chronosteel made it easier to store and gave a larger mass whose clock I could rely on. I use the blocks wherever a structure needs a steady time reference.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Casimir Energy Cell, Chronosteel Ingot, Singularity Compactor.

A superconducting coil wrapped in chronosteel, so that current inside it runs on its own clock. The field it makes is steadier than any ordinary coil, as though the coil had more time to think. It hums at a low, even pitch.
pages.title: Chronosteel Coil Block

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Heavier recipes wanted hotter coils that would not drift. Wrapping a superconducting coil in chronosteel let me slow the coil's own time relative to its load, so it never quite overheats.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Essence Distillery, Spacetime Alloy Coil Block, Spacetime Anchor Pylon, Stellar Plasma Crucible.

Neutronium forged in a pocket of stopped time. Because time does not pass for it, it never ages, rusts or wears; a scratch on it is permanent but never deepens. It is cool and very heavy, and its surface reflects a fraction of a second late.
pages.title: Chronosteel Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Breaking a Block of Chronosteel into ingots by hand was simple enough. Forging the block in the first place took a pocket of stopped time that I will not describe here.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Assembly Matrix, Block of Chronosteel, Causal Shield Lattice, Causal Shielding Plate, Chronal Accelerator, Chrono Loom, Chronoplastic Gasket, Chronosteel Coil Block and more.

The blank on which every circuit board is built: a neutronium base laced with quantum dots that tune its electrical and optical response. It is flat, faintly iridescent and heavier than it looks. Every board I make starts here.
pages.title: Metamaterial Substrate

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Circuits need a stable base. In the Casimir Vacuum Press, I pressed Quantum Dots into a Neutronium Plate, giving a substrate whose response I could tune to any circuit.

Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Circuit Board, Dimensional Residue, Photonic Circuit Board, Topological Circuit Board.
Superconducting wire braided so its electrons keep their phase from end to end. Every quantum machine is threaded with it.
pages.title: Coherent Wiring Harness

pages.text: Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Entangled Bus Bar.

Glass that is not really glass, but a field held between two panes with a shimmer of plasma in between. It holds back heat, cold and pressure that would shatter any ordinary window, and it hums faintly when touched.
pages.title: Containment Field Glass

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I needed windows that could watch a reaction without melting. I gave up on the glass and trusted the field instead, which holds the reaction and lets the light pass through.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Abiogenesis Crucible, Anomaly Containment Ward, Bioreactor, Chemical Reactor, Cryogenic Cooling Jacket, Dyson Sphere Model, Empty Containment Cell, Entanglement Node and more.
Couples a machine to the flux of a whole cosmos without being consumed by it.
pages.title: Cosmic Flux Coupler

pages.text: Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Ontological Junction.

Dilithium crystals fused into one solid block that rings when struck and glows a soft violet. The resonance carries through the floor, and anything metal nearby picks up a faint hum. In a quiet room the note is just audible, steady and clean, and it never seems to fade.
pages.title: Block of Dilithium

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Compacting dilithium crystals for storage turned their individual tones into a single, pure note. I keep the block near tuning-sensitive machines and they seem to like it.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dilithium Crystal, Dilithium Lamp.

A crystal porous to antimatter. It lets antiparticles pass through its lattice without touching, slowing and channelling them so that annihilation happens only where it is wanted. It is cool, violet and humming, and its structure is unlike any natural mineral.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Dilithium Ore in the Nether.
pages.title: Dilithium Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Breaking a Block of Dilithium by hand into crystals was simple. Discovering that its lattice let antimatter through unharmed was not: I spent a week checking whether my trap had leaked.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Dilithium Ore$(), in veins through the Nether.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Annihilation Core, Block of Dilithium, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Dilithium Crystal, Magnetar Shard, Magnetic Confinement Casing, Neutrino Flux, Void Lattice Shard.

A dilithium block with glowstone at its centre, so the violet crystal shines with a soft, even light. It hums a single note when lit. The light is steady and gentle, more like dusk than daylight, and the note it hums sits comfortably beneath conversation. It is the lamp I leave on at night.
pages.title: Dilithium Lamp

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Dilithium glowed only faintly on its own. Adding glowstone dust gave me a violet lamp that also hums, which I find oddly soothing.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.
Two bars that are one: a current at one end is already at the other.
pages.title: Entangled Bus Bar

pages.text: Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chronoplastic Gasket.

Thousands of physical qubits standing guard over one logical qubit. Each error is caught by the neighbours, which vote it out before it can spread. It is a delicate lattice of light, cold to touch, and remarkably stable.
pages.title: Error-Correction Lattice

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)My qubits kept losing coherence. In the Neural Synthesizer, I let a Quantum Processor arrange Qubits around a Superposition Crystal, using Synaptic Fluid to learn which errors to vote out.
Made in $(item)Neural Synthesizer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Adaptive Feedback Core, Anomaly Resolution Engine, Quantum Error-Correction Core.

Time flows through it without passing. A closed timelike curve keeps it forever at the same moment, and the cosmological constant keeps its space from collapsing. It is required by the final processes and never consumed by them. It feels neither old nor new.
pages.title: Eternity Catalyst

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Reality Compiler, I fused a Spacetime Catalyst with a Closed Timelike Curve, a Bootstrap Artifact and the Cosmological Constant, sealed with Causal Solder. Time inside stopped moving, but did not stop.
Made in $(item)Reality Compiler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Unified Notes II.

Solder forged in stellar plasma. Exotic matter gives it negative energy density, quark-gluon plasma gives it strength, and it joins components that ordinary solder would vaporise. It flows like liquid starlight.
pages.title: Exotic Solder

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The attoscale components needed something stronger than superconducting solder. Forging it with an Exotic Matter Crystal and quark-gluon plasma in the Stellar Plasma Crucible gave me a solder with exotic properties.

Made in $(item)Stellar Plasma Crucible$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Attoscale Capacitor, Attoscale Inductor, Attoscale Transistor, Burst Observatory, Causal Solder, Cosmic Circuit Board, Cosmic Neutronium Coil Block, Dimensional Residue and more.

A Casimir capacitor smaller than a proton. Two plates femtometres apart store charge, helped by the vacuum pressure pressing them together from outside. It is far too small to see, and I keep it in a sealed vial so that I do not inhale it by accident.
pages.title: Femtoscale Capacitor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Femto Fabricator I trimmed a Casimir Plate with Neutronium Plate and Superconducting Solder until the spacing was smaller than a proton. The capacitance went up, as Casimir predicted.
Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Attoscale Capacitor, Topological Processor.

A superconducting coil wound around nothing, smaller than a proton. Its magnetic field stores energy in empty space, and its current never stops. It is too small to see and occasionally tugs at steel nearby.
pages.title: Femtoscale Inductor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Femto Fabricator, I wound a Superconducting Coil around a sliver of neutronium with Superconducting Solder, then removed the core. The coil held its shape around nothing.

Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Attoscale Inductor, Empirical Notes I, Precision Assembly Casing, Topological Circuit Board.

A single-qubit switch, the smallest logic gate there can be. One qubit flips between states and a quantum dot opens or closes to current in response. It is invisible to the eye, switches in femtoseconds, and wastes almost no energy doing so.
pages.title: Femtoscale Transistor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Femto Fabricator I placed a Qubit inside a Quantum Dot coated in Quantum-Dot Photoresist. Flipping the qubit opened or closed the dot to current: one bit, one switch.
Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Attoscale Transistor, Quantum Processor.

A small crystal figure, faceted and without flaw, that is unmistakably me - not as I am but as Plato would have said I am meant to be. In the Realm of Forms every imperfect copy defers to its ideal, and this is the ideal I can point to when the Realm asks who I claim to be.
pages.title: Form of the Self

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Platonic Realm treated me as a poor copy of something and tried to correct me. I cut Cherenkov quartz around a quantum dot that held my own readings, and set it in a Cherenkov lattice. With an ideal to answer to, the Realm stopped trying to fix me.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.

A casing of containment field glass and chronosteel over event horizon casing, made to separate fluids by mass and charge in a tall spire. Watching through the glass, the layers settle into neat bands.
pages.title: Fractionation Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Separating exotic fluids needed a tall, sealed column. Event horizon casing kept the fluid in, containment field glass let me watch the layers form, and chronosteel kept the separation steady.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Fractionation Spire.

A wafer with more surface than its area allows, because part of it extends into a fourth dimension. Circuits can be laid out on its hidden face as well as the visible one. Running a finger across it, the surface feels longer than it should.
pages.title: Hyperdimensional Wafer

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Slicing a Hyperdimensional Boule in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I measured each wafer's surface and found more of it than geometry allows. The extra area lay in a direction my ruler could not point.
Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Logic Wafer, Empirical Notes I, Hyperdimensional Logic Wafer.

A device that cancels momentum locally, letting a ship accelerate without crushing everything inside. Negative mass offsets positive mass and a superconducting coil steers the balance. It is quiet and cool, and objects placed on it never slide off.
pages.title: Inertia Damper

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Accelerating anything quickly kills everyone on board. In the Higgs Field Modulator, a Negative Mass Ingot balanced against the passenger's mass, and the coil adjusted it. Every starship needs one.
Made in $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Mass Manipulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Graviton Harness.

A flawless crystal nucleus, a few atoms arranged exactly right. Boules grow from it atom by atom, each new layer copying the one below. It is tiny, clear and precious, and any flaw in it would be repeated through every wafer that follows.
pages.title: Lattice Seed Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)To grow perfect crystals I needed a perfect start. Pressing Cherenkov Quartz in the Casimir Vacuum Press, the vacuum forced the lattice into its lowest-energy arrangement, leaving a seed without a single defect.
Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cherenkov Boule, Hyperdimensional Boule, Topological Boule, Warm Helium.

Containment field glass doped with quantum dots so that light passing through it is shaped at nanometre resolution. It projects patterns far finer than its own grain. Look closely and the glass seems to be drawing tiny circuits.
pages.title: Lithography Glass

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Quantum lithography needed a mask that could focus light below its wavelength. Embedding quantum dots in containment field glass let them shape the light into features smaller than the light itself.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Quantum Lithographer.

An alloy the Higgs field has been told to ignore. Its particles have no rest mass, so it should move at the speed of light, yet the bonds between atoms keep it in place. It weighs nothing at all and drifts in any breeze, which makes it very hard to set down.
pages.title: Massless Alloy

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Higgs Field Modulator, a Sterile Neutrino carried the neutronium's coupling to the Higgs field away, while a condensate kept the lattice together. When it finished, the scale read zero.
Made in $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Mass Manipulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Exotic Matter Singularity, Negative Mass Ingot, Theoretical Notes II.

Matter with negative inertial mass: push it and it comes toward you. A positive and a negative mass placed side by side would chase each other forever. The ingot is strangely cooperative, sliding into my hand whenever I try to push it away.
pages.title: Negative Mass Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Feeding Massless Alloy into Exotic Matter Crystal in the Higgs Field Modulator, I pushed its mass below zero. The first ingot slid uphill. Physicists predicted it decades ago; it was still alarming.

Made in $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Mass Manipulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Banach-Tarski Sphere, Dimensional Residue, Exotic Matter Singularity, Inertia Damper, Phantom Energy Cell, Spacetime Anchor Core, Wormhole Frame Casing, Wormhole Throat.
A wax seal pressed with a law. Machines that bear one are permitted to work.
pages.title: Omnilex Seal

pages.text: Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.
Where a machine's idea of itself meets its matter. Without one, big machines forget what they are for.
pages.title: Ontological Junction

pages.text: Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Transfinite Lattice Bolt.

The sixth tier of processor. It does not compute answers; it decides what is true, writing its results directly into the source code of reality. Holographic matrices store its working and Bekenstein crystals bound its memory. Near it, simple facts feel slightly negotiable.
pages.title: Ontological Processor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)On the Femtoscale Assembly Line I combined a Cosmic Processor with a Source Code Fragment, a Holographic Matrix and a Bekenstein Crystal. Its first output was not a number but a correction to the world.

Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Axiom Distiller, Axiomatic Breach Engine, Dimensional Residue, Eye of the Event Horizon, Identity Kernel, Omega Point, Omega Simulator, Ontological Junction and more.
Dark energy with w below -1. Its density grows as space expands, until it tears apart galaxies, stars, atoms - and then the cell.
pages.title: Phantom Energy Cell

pages.text: Made in $(item)Dark Energy Siphon$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Big Rip.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmological Constant.

A circuit board of light-guides rather than copper traces. Its paths are Cherenkov quartz, its connectors superconducting, and signals travel between them at light speed. It glows faint blue when powered, and warms only slightly.
pages.title: Photonic Circuit Board

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Metamaterial Weaver I laid Cherenkov Quartz waveguides across a Metamaterial Substrate with a superconducting coil and Quantum-Dot Photoresist. Light followed the paths exactly.
Made in $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Photonic Processor, Quantum Processor.

A single photonic logic die cut from its wafer. It is a tiny square of crystal whose engraved waveguides carry light through logic gates, and it glows faintly when powered. It is small enough to lose in a pocket, and I have.
pages.title: Photonic Die

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Planck-Scale Cutter diced a Photonic Logic Wafer in superfluid helium, separating each logic unit cleanly. The first die worked on the first try, which I recorded with some suspicion.
Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Photonic Processor.

A wafer engraved with waveguides instead of wires, so its logic runs on light. Signals cross without interfering and switch in femtoseconds. Held to the light, the engravings scatter a faint rainbow across my palm.
pages.title: Photonic Logic Wafer

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Quantum Lithographer, I exposed a Cherenkov Wafer through Quantum-Dot Photoresist. The dots blocked light precisely where I needed waveguides, and the pattern etched itself into the wafer.
Made in $(item)Quantum Lithographer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Coherent Wiring Harness, Empirical Notes II, Photonic Die, Warm Helium.

A light-sensitive coating made of quantum dots. Each dot reacts to a single photon, so patterns can be printed finer than the wavelength of light. It is thin, faintly coloured and cool to the touch. Exposed regions harden instantly, so it records light like a photographic plate.
pages.title: Quantum-Dot Photoresist

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Lithography needs a resist that responds to single photons. Condensing quantum dots with water, I got a photoresist that allowed patterns far finer than any classical resist.

Made in $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Logic Wafer, Femtoscale Transistor, Hyperdimensional Logic Wafer, Photonic Circuit Board, Photonic Logic Wafer, Quantum Singularity, Qubit Array Wafer, Topological Circuit Board and more.

A casing of chronosteel around magnetic confinement and superconducting coils, built to hold plasma at stellar temperatures for as long as needed. The air near it shimmers, and it ticks softly as it settles.
pages.title: Plasma Crucible Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Holding plasma for long periods wears magnetic casings out. I added chronosteel so the casing ages slowly relative to the plasma inside, and paired it with superconducting coils for the field.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Abiogenesis Crucible, Stellar Plasma Crucible.

A converging magnetic nozzle that accelerates plasma to a few percent of the speed of light. Topological insulators guide the current around its throat and tachyon crystals keep the field ahead of the flow. It glows bright at the tip even when cold.
pages.title: Plasma Nozzle Tip

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Femto Fabricator, I shaped a magnetic throat from Neutronium Plate, Topological Insulator and Metamaterial Sheet, and added a Tachyon Crystal to drive the field ahead of the plasma.
Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Plasma Injection Nozzle.

This notebook. Its pages are bound with a sliver of Cherenkov Quartz in the spine, so entries glow faintly when there is something new to read. It holds every observation, sketch and wrong turn I have made, and it grows thicker every time I return from the field.
pages.title: Quantum Codex

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I found an older edition in an observatory ruin, half the entries water-damaged. I bound a book with a quartz spine and began copying it out, adding my own notes. Most of the handwriting in here is mine now.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Observatory Ruin chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.

A core that protects a quantum computer's fragile states by spreading each logical qubit across many physical ones and fixing errors as they happen. It hums with a steady, careful rhythm. Its lights blink in careful patterns.
pages.title: Quantum Error-Correction Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Qubits decohere constantly. Error correction encodes one logical qubit in many, so errors can be detected and undone. I combined a quantum processor with an error-correction lattice on spacetime casing.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.

A fault-tolerant array of logical qubits, each one encoded across many physical ones so errors can be caught and corrected before they spread. It runs algorithms ordinary computers cannot reach in the lifetime of a star. The casing stays cold, and when it works it makes no sound at all.
pages.title: Quantum Processor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Only a Matrioshka Brain had the patience to lay out computronium finely enough for error-corrected logic. I bathed the ingot in Synaptic Fluid and let the brain design the layout; older processors also turned up in anomaly vaults and derelict stations.

Made in $(item)Matrioshka Brain$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Anomaly Vault chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Accretion Disk Reactor, Analog Black Hole, Antiproton Decelerator, Assembly Matrix, Autonomous Extreme Assembler, Calorimeter Detector Array, Chrono Loom, Computronium Ingot and more.

Thousands of qubits engraved into a single wafer through a metamaterial lens, each one isolated from the rest by careful spacing. When cooled, the whole array waits in superposition. It is cold to touch and shimmers faintly at the edges.
pages.title: Qubit Array Wafer

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Exposing a Cherenkov Wafer through Quantum-Dot Photoresist in the Quantum Lithographer, I tuned the dots so each one became a qubit. The lens laid out thousands at once.
Made in $(item)Quantum Lithographer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Qubit Die, Warm Helium.

A single die of entangled qubits cut from an array wafer. Each qubit on it shares its state with its neighbours, so the die computes as one coherent whole. It is cold, fragile and faintly shimmering, and any careless knock would collapse it back into ordinary silicon.
pages.title: Qubit Die

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Dicing a Qubit Array Wafer in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I kept the cut in superfluid helium so the qubits stayed coherent. Each die kept its entanglement intact.
Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Quantum Processor.

A device that keeps a patch of reality from being edited. It hard-codes the local laws so that no compiler, demon or paradox can rewrite them while it holds. It is heavy and stubborn, and the space around it feels unusually solid.
pages.title: Reality Anchor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Once I could edit reality I needed a way to protect it. In the Reality Compiler, a Source Code Fragment wrapped around a Quark Star Core with Psionic Ether made a region whose code was locked.
Made in $(item)Reality Compiler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Axiomatic Breach Engine, Primordial Charter, Unified Notes I.

$(thing)Quantum Hall Effect$()$(br2)Electrons in a sheet at low temperature and strong field fill Landau levels; the Hall resistance locks onto plateaus at h/(νe²), exact to a part in a billion - because it counts a topological invariant. Unlocks Hall Bar Chips.
pages.title: Quantum Hall Effect

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 140$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Room-Temperature Superconductivity, Topological Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Silicon Boule, 2 Laue Pattern.

A dark wafer through which current flows with zero resistance at ordinary temperatures. Electrons pair up into Cooper pairs and move through the lattice as one coherent wave. A magnet hovers over it, locked in place. Physicists have chased this for a century.
pages.title: Room-Temperature Superconductor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Hydrogen-rich compounds superconduct at high temperature, but only under crushing pressure. I let metallic hydrogen fill a metal-organic framework, doped it with an electride and seeded it with a condensate, so the cage held the pressure for me.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Room-Temperature Superconductivity.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Neural Organoid, Transfinite Coil Block.
Nine singularities condensed into one, when there are too many to hold.
pages.title: Singularity Cluster

pages.text: When a pack has so many singularities that one recipe cannot hold them, nine at a time are condensed into a $(item)Singularity Cluster$() on the Extreme Assembly Table - and nine clusters into a Hypercluster, and so on. The Omniscience Catalyst then asks for the clusters.

A few lines of the program that runs the universe. Mostly comments: notes, apologies, and an occasional reminder from someone to fix something later. The fragment glows like an old terminal screen and the text rearranges itself when I try to read it closely.
pages.title: Source Code Fragment

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Reality Compiler took a Bekenstein Crystal, a Cosmic Processor and a Boltzmann Brain and decompiled a patch of space. What came out was text. Most of it was comments, some of which seemed to refer to me.

Made in $(item)Reality Compiler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Axiom Fragment, Cantor Diagonalizer, Dimensional Residue, Omega Point, Ontological Processor, Primordial Charter, Reality Anchor.
Turns on a frictionless geodesic. It will outlast the machine around it.
pages.title: Spacetime Bearing

pages.text: Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Flux Coupler.

A captive star the size of a fist, ignited and held together by magnetic confinement. Hydrogen fuses in its heart, and it radiates heat and light as any star does, only smaller. It is impossibly bright and cannot be looked at directly for long.
pages.title: Stellar Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Stellar Plasma Crucible, I poured Quark-Gluon Plasma around an existing core, and it lit a second fire next to the first. The original was ignited by a white hole fragment, as the old entries say.

Made in $(item)Stellar Plasma Crucible$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Closed Timelike Curve, Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Cosmic String Segment, Dark Energy, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Dimensional Residue, Dyson Array, Einstein Field Core and more.

The hot, ionised gas from a star's core, where hydrogen fuses into helium at fifteen million kelvin. It glows white and roils with magnetic field lines, and it wants to escape in every direction at once.
pages.title: Stellar Plasma

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Harvesting a Pocket Universe in the Universe Forge, the first stars to form inside it gave up their core plasma. Cosmogenesis, and then I took the starlight.

Made in $(item)Universe Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Dimensional Residue, Dyson Shell Segment, Frozen Photon, Hawking Radiation, Horizon Shard, Hypernova Alloy Ingot and more.

Solder that conducts electricity without resistance. Chilled with superfluid helium, it joins femtoscale components with perfect efficiency. It shimmers faintly when current passes through. Magnets float above a puddle of it, pinned in place by expelled field lines.
pages.title: Superconducting Solder

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Femtoscale components needed joints with no resistance. Condensing a Superconducting Coil with superfluid helium, I got a solder that kept its superconductivity even at the joint.

Made in $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Exotic Solder, Femtoscale Capacitor, Femtoscale Inductor, Photonic Processor, Pixel Tracker Module, Plasma Nozzle Tip, Quantum Processor.

A circuit board whose traces are protected by topology. No defect or stray field can interrupt the current running around their edges. It is dark grey, with faintly shimmering lines along every trace.
pages.title: Topological Circuit Board

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Topological Phase Transmuter, I printed Topological Insulator traces on a Metamaterial Substrate with a Femtoscale Inductor and Quantum-Dot Photoresist. The traces could not be broken.
Made in $(item)Topological Phase Transmuter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Assembly Lines.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Hyperdimensional Processor, Self-Healing Polymer, Topological Processor.

The third tier of processor, fault-tolerant by geometry. Its logic is stored in braided anyons, so no stray field or defect can cause an error. It runs quietly and never crashes, which I appreciate more than I expected.
pages.title: Topological Processor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Femto Fabricator, I mounted a Topological Die on a Topological Circuit Board alongside a Quantum Processor and a Femtoscale Capacitor. Derelict stations kept some, still running.

Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Assembly Lines.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Adaptive Feedback Core, Burst Observatory, Chronoplastic Gasket, Compactification Lathe, Dimensional Residue, ER=EPR Weaver, Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector, Evolution Engine and more.

A wafer whose edges carry current without resistance, protected by topology. No scratch or defect in the middle can interrupt the flow around the rim. It looks like a thin grey disc with a faintly shimmering edge.
pages.title: Topological Wafer

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Cutting a Topological Boule in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I worried slicing would ruin its edges. Instead every slice had its own protected boundary, because topology does not care where you cut.
Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Topological Logic Wafer.
Threaded with ℵ₀ turns. It never quite finishes screwing in, and it never comes loose.
pages.title: Transfinite Lattice Bolt

pages.text: Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omnilex Seal.

Bladed discs spinning at ninety thousand revolutions per minute, so fast that gas molecules striking them are batted out of the beamline one at a time. It produces the ultra-high vacuum particle beams need. It whines softly and must never be touched while it spins.
pages.title: Turbomolecular Rotor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Particle beams scatter off any gas. In the Planck-Scale Cutter I carved Neutronium Plate into blades, cooled with helium so they would not deform at speed. The vacuum improved by orders of magnitude.
Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Turbomolecular Vacuum Pump.
The sealed doughnut-shaped chamber of a tokamak, pumped below a billionth of an atmosphere before fuel is let in, so the plasma meets nothing but itself.
pages.title: Vacuum Vessel

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Tokamak.

Helium that has done its job and warmed back up. It is ordinary gas now, clear and inert, waiting to be cooled again. Once superfluid, it is just helium. The noble gas never reacts with anything, so it can be recycled almost endlessly. Squeezed and chilled again, it remembers how to become superfluid.
pages.title: Warm Helium

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Using superfluid helium to chill Casimir plates in the Bose-Einstein Condenser, the helium warmed back to gas. Distilled in the Fractionation Spire, it could be recycled.
Made in $(item)Tokamak$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Maxwell-Boltzmann Gas, Superfluid Helium.

A casing threaded with negative mass and exotic matter, the ingredients a traversable wormhole needs to keep its throat open. It feels as if it is pushing my hand away and pulling it in at the same time.
pages.title: Wormhole Frame Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)An Einstein-Rosen bridge collapses unless its throat is held open by negative energy. I built the frame from negative mass ingots and exotic matter crystal over a hyperframe, and the bridge stopped pinching shut.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Mass Manipulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector.
Slices boules into wafers, and wafers into dies, along cuts one Planck length wide.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.
pages.title: Planck-Scale Cutter

pages.text: The $(thing)Planck length$(), about 1.6 x 10^-35 m, is where our physics gives out - the scale at which quantum gravity should take over. A cut that thin wastes nothing. I still cannot explain how the blade exists.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

$(thing)Machine data$(): a single-block machine (4 item and 2 fluid inputs, 2 and 1 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Cherenkov Wafer, Cosmic Die, Fractal Dust, Hyperdimensional Die, Hyperdimensional Wafer, Ordinal Shard, Photonic Die, Qubit Die, Spacetime Slag, Topological Die, Topological Wafer, Turbomolecular Rotor, Warm Helium.
Made in a crafting grid.

Day 33. Every machine is built around a processor one tier below its own. There are seven tiers:$(br)$(li)I Photonic$(li)II Qubit$(li)III Topological$(li)IV Hyperdimensional$(li)V Cosmic$(li)VI Ontological$(li)VII Transfinite

A processor needs a $(thing)board$(), $(thing)dies$() of its tier, the previous tier's processor and femto- or attoscale $(thing)components$(), joined with $(fluid)solder$(). From tier IV on, only the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() can assemble them.

The early tiers follow real research: logic carried by light instead of electrons, then $(thing)qubits$() that hold superpositions, then $(thing)topological$() qubits whose information is braided into a shape that noise cannot easily undo. Past tier III, I am naming things as I go.
Tier I processor. Computes with light.$(br2)Made in $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$().
A fault-tolerant array of logical qubits.$(br2)Made in $(item)Matrioshka Brain$().
Tier III processor. Fault-tolerant by geometry.$(br2)Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$().

Landscapes are written by water. A river carries grains as fast as it flows, and drops them as it slows - the heaviest first. A small grain of radius r sinks at a steady speed v = (2/9)(ρ_s − ρ_f)g r²/μ: sand settles in minutes, clay in days.
That is why the ground is layered. A $(item)Sediment Core$() is a tube of those layers, oldest at the bottom: floods, droughts and ash falls in the order they happened.

A map flattens a round planet, and no flat map keeps everything true. Keep every angle true - so a compass course is a straight line - and the map must stretch towards the poles: a point at latitude φ is drawn at R·ln tan(π/4 + φ/2).

$(thing)Geodesy$() measures the planet itself. Measure one baseline, sight two angles with a $(item)Theodolite Lens$(), and the sine rule gives every other side of the triangle. Chain triangles together and a whole country is mapped.
The $(item)Geodetic Surveyor$() does it for you: use it to list the ores within 24 blocks - how many of each, and how far and which way the nearest one lies. A burst of light marks each.

An earthquake sends out two kinds of wave. $(thing)Pressure waves$() push and pull the rock along their path and travel fastest, about 6 km/s in the crust. $(thing)Shear waves$() shake it sideways and travel at about 3.5 km/s. The farther the source, the larger the gap between them: d = Δt·v_p·v_s/(v_p − v_s).
The $(item)Seismograph$() must stand on solid ground. Each finished run times the echoes from below and reports the depth of the nearest ore or cave - within 64 m and three blocks to either side.

Scientists worked across the Overworld before you, and their field sites still stand - built, like the old observatory ruins, from the mod's own materials, with Containment Caches of what they left behind.

$(thing)Survey Benchmarks$() - a neutronium pillar topped with a Cherenkov lamp - stand in every kind of land. $(thing)Observatories$() keep their cracked field-glass domes high in the mountains, a telescope still aimed through the slit.

$(thing)Crashed Satellites$() lie in scorched rings on plains, savannas, deserts and badlands. $(thing)Magnetic Anomaly Sites$() are rare: standing stones of magnetite round a buried knot of it, which the Gauss Meter reads from well away.
$(thing)Fallout Shelters$() are sealed, lead-lined rooms deep underground, lit by radium lamps. They have no door to the surface: a Seismograph, which reports caves below it, is the way to find one.
Some villages keep a $(thing)Probability Hall$(): a floor of Chance Tiles, a Galton Board to study and a cache of dice and tablets.

The sites' blocks can be made too: $(item)Magnetite$() and $(item)Lead$() bricks, Lead Hazard Panels, Radium Lamps, Chance Tiles, and a $(item)Decorative Telescope$() and $(item)Satellite Wreck$() - decoration only; working instruments come later.

Bedrock is not the bottom of the world - it is only as far as any tool could cut. The $(item)Core Drill$() cuts it: hold it against bedrock and keep holding. At the floor of the Overworld the bit breaks through into a $(item)Mantle Breach$(). Step in.

The $(thing)Planetary Interior$() is layered by depth, like the planet. At the top lie the $(thing)Crustal Caverns$(), with patches of $(thing)Natural Reactor$() - Oklo rock where uranium seams once ran a chain reaction by themselves, two billion years ago. Below them the $(thing)Magma Chambers$(): columnar basalt over a sea of basaltic magma.

Deeper still is the $(thing)Mantle Convection Zone$(), peridotite holding $(item)Ringwoodite$() and $(item)Bridgmanite$() - minerals that only exist under its pressure - where hot plumes rise and throw you upwards. At the bottom is the $(thing)Geodynamo Core$() of iron and nickel, whose currents make the planet's field: magnetic storms sweep through it, Magnetizing everything you carry. Beneath it lies the $(item)Inner Core Boundary$(): solid iron held at 330 GPa, which no tool yet made can cut.

$(thing)Lithostatic Pressure$(): the deeper you stand, the heavier the rock above presses - P = ρgh - and the slower you move and mine. The Natural Reactor has a high radiation background, and its Fission Fragment seams are strongly radioactive.
To leave, step back into a Mantle Breach. One opens beside you wherever you arrive, and the Core Drill cuts new ones through the Interior's bedrock.

The Interior is richer than the Overworld. Its ores run in bigger veins: $(item)Rich Iron$() and $(item)Rich Copper$() in the crust, $(item)Rich Gold$() in the basalt of the Magma Chambers. Their chunks smelt to two ingots; assayed in the $(item)Spectrograph$() they give three each, and what rides with them in nature - magnetite with iron, gold with copper, uraninite with reef gold.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Corundum Crystal Mass in the Planetary Interior (Crustal Caverns); in the caches of Deep Borehole structures in the Planetary Interior (Crustal Caverns).

Its pockets of crystal are far larger than any geode: a shell of pale rock round masses of gem. $(item)Corundum$() and $(item)Garnet$() grow in the crust; $(item)Peridot$() in the mantle; and, rarer and deeper, $(item)Moissanite$(). Break a Crystal Mass for its gems; it takes silk touch to keep the mass whole.

Iron-Nickel and Core Magnetite Ore are too hard for any ordinary pick: they drop nothing to netherite. The $(item)Moissanite Drill$() - silicon carbide on a netherite shank - cuts them. Corundum is the lens material of the instruments to come.

$(thing)Basaltic Magma$() is far hotter than lava, and Fire Resistance is no help against it: it melts what it touches. Only armour made for it will do, and that comes later. $(thing)Deep Brine$() is scalding: it sets you alight like lava.

The $(item)Deep Drilling Rig$() is a derrick: four leaning legs, a crown block, and a string of pipe hanging into the hole. Set the depth, the weight on the bit and its speed, and the density of the mud that fills the well.

Below you the rock warms by about 25 K a kilometre, and the water in its pores is under pressure - overpressured, deeper down. The mud column must press harder than that water, or it flows into the well: a $(thing)kick$(). But too heavy a mud fractures the rock and vanishes into it: $(thing)lost circulation$(). Between the two is the window you drill in.

What comes up depends on how deep you are: sediment cores and brine near the top, a pocket of $(fluid)Basaltic Magma$() where the rock is hot enough, crustal rock with rich ore, and at the bottom of thin crust, $(item)Peridotite$() from the mantle.

Rock buried deep recrystallises into whatever is stable down there. The $(item)Tectonic Press$() does it on purpose: a multi-anvil vessel over a firebox, under a hydraulic ram. You set two things - the anvil pressure and the furnace temperature - and the phase diagram does the rest.

Each boundary between two minerals is a line on that diagram, and its slope is the $(thing)Clapeyron slope$(), dP/dT = ΔS/ΔV. Graphite turns to diamond above P = 1.94 + 0.0025·T(°C) GPa; olivine to ringwoodite above about 17.5 GPa; ringwoodite to bridgmanite above the post-spinel line near 23 GPa, which leans the other way.

Being on the right side is not enough: the sample must be hot enough to react. Its rate follows Arrhenius - a few hundred kelvin make the difference between hours and seconds. Diamond also wants a solvent: keep a block of $(item)Iron-Nickel$() in the press, as real diamond presses use molten iron and nickel.
At low pressure and 3,000 K the press turns coal into nuclear-grade $(item)Graphite$(), and with brine and iron into $(item)Boron Control Rods$(): boron carbide is made the same way.
The $(thing)Magma Crawler$() lives in the Magma Chambers' sea. Basaltic Magma is its water: it swims through it as fast as you walk, and its bite sets you alight. On dry rock it is slower.
The $(thing)Plume Elemental$() is a blob of mantle rock that convects. Deep down it heats and rises; high up it cools and sinks. Stand over or beside it and the upwelling throws you into the air.

The $(thing)Fission Husk$() glows with what decays inside it - stand near it and your dose climbs. Kill it and it splits: two lighter husks fly apart in a burst of neutrons, and each of those splits once more.

The $(thing)Geodynamo Wraith$() is a loop of the core's own current. It circles its prey; ferromagnetic armour near it is Magnetized and pulled in, and it can tear an iron tool out of your hand. Wear no iron near it.
Every hazard below has its suit, crafted like ordinary armour.

$(item)Refractory Suit$(): corundum and moissanite. A full suit is proof against $(fluid)Basaltic Magma$() - you can wade in it and mine the magnetite under it - against $(fluid)Deep Brine$(), lava, and every fire.
$(item)Pressure Suit$(): bridgmanite and ringwoodite, minerals made under the mantle's weight. Each piece takes a level off $(thing)Lithostatic Pressure$(); a full suit cancels it at any depth.

$(thing)Radiation plating$() goes on any armour, of any mod. Put an armour piece and a plate together in a crafting grid: $(item)Light$() (lead) stops 10% of the radiation dose per piece, $(item)Medium$() (lead and graphite) 18%, $(item)Heavy$() (lead, graphite and boron carbide) 25% - four heavy-plated pieces stop all but 5%. A better plate replaces a worse one. Wear it in the Natural Reactor.

Carbon dioxide traps the heat the ground gives off: a forcing $(thing)ΔF = 5.35 ln(C/280 ppm)$() W/m² - 3.7 W/m² for each doubling. Aerosols reflect sunlight back out. The world warms by about $(thing)0.8 K per W/m²$().

The $(item)Climate Engine$() holds the air's CO₂ and aerosols where you set them. Warm it by 1-2.5 K with water and a forecast and it rains; by 2.5-5 K, storms; hold it near today's and the sky clears. (Minecraft's weather is the whole world's.) Cool it 2.5 K or more and snow becomes an $(item)Ice Core$(); a little less, and frozen soil a $(item)Permafrost Sample$(). Past 6 K it runs away.

A $(item)Survey Satellite$() sits in the Interstellar Scoop as a catalyst - the Scoop works only high up or in space, which is where a satellite flies - and photographs the ground: a $(item)Satellite Image Plate$(). From 700 km, a 1.1 m mirror sees 40 cm.

The Deep Drilling Rig, drilling to the base of a plate, brings up a $(item)Lithospheric Plate Fragment$(). The Tectonic Press squeezes an exoplanet's core with our own to a core's pressure: a $(item)Planetary Core Sample$() - every rocky planet sinks its iron to the middle, at about 3GM²/(8πR⁴).

Water seeps through rock by $(thing)Darcy's law$(): Q = kAΔP/(μL) - permeability times the pressure gradient. The $(item)Aquifer Pump$() draws it up: Water anywhere; in the Planetary Interior, an $(item)Aquifer Sample$() with Deep Brine from a confined aquifer.
In the Interior's Magma Chambers it reaches water heated past its critical point, 647 K and 22 MPa: $(fluid)Supercritical Water$(), neither liquid nor gas.

A heavy pendulum that the ground moves under. It times two kinds of wave from below - fast pressure waves and slow shear waves - and the gap between them says how deep their source lies.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

A coil that warps the metric around it: space ahead contracts, space behind expands, and whatever sits in between is carried along without moving locally. Alcubierre showed this is allowed by general relativity, so long as one has negative energy to spare. It is cold, coiled and very still.
pages.title: Alcubierre Coil

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Exotic matter crystals provided the negative energy, a metric tensor told the coil where to bend, and a Lorentz Transform Crystal kept the bubble consistent. The Tesseract Assembler wound them around a superconducting coil.
Made in $(item)Tesseract Assembler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Brane Shifter, Warp Bubble Core, Warp Coil Ring.

A field calibrator with a superintelligence wired into it, installed permanently into a controller. It watches the drifting tuning, corrects it, and repairs containment without being asked. It takes a share of the power for itself, which seems fair.
pages.title: Autonomous Calibrator

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Tuning every machine by hand was exhausting. On the Femtoscale Assembly Line I fused a Field Calibrator with a Superintelligence Core and a Cosmic Processor. It has not needed me since.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superintelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Predictive Lattice Governor, Theoretical Notes I.

A compact six-dimensional shape of the kind string theory curls its extra dimensions into, its holes and twists deciding which particles exist. This one is folded small enough to hold. It looks different from every angle, and touching one surface makes my finger reappear on another.
pages.title: Calabi-Yau Manifold

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Topological Phase Transmuter I folded a Topological Insulator around a Void Lattice Shard, with a condensate to keep it coherent. The result had six compact dimensions I could count. Bulk monoliths and Calabi-Yau knots hide them too.

Made in $(item)Topological Phase Transmuter$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Bulk Monolith, Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Brane Shifter, Compactification Lathe, Cosmic Circuit Board, Dimensional Residue, Dimensional Singularity, Dimensional Stabiliser Matrix, Entangled Bus Bar, G₂ Manifold and more.

A block of matter arranged so that every atom is part of a computation. It is warm to the touch and very slightly noisy, as though it is always working. Computronium is the theoretical limit of programmable matter.
pages.title: Computronium Block

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Once a self-improving mind made computronium possible, I compacted the ingots into blocks for building. The blocks keep thinking even when nothing is asking them to.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superintelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cognitive Singularity, Computronium Ingot, Computronium Lamp, Matrioshka Brain.

Matter arranged for the greatest possible computation per gram, approaching the physical limits set by quantum mechanics and thermodynamics. Every atom is a logic gate, every bond a wire. It is warm to the touch, because it is thinking, and it never quite stops.
pages.title: Computronium Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Once I had built a Computronium Block, breaking it into ingots by hand was straightforward. Each ingot carries a working fragment of the computation, which is useful in the machines that need it.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superintelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Computronium Block, Quantum Processor, Reality Lattice Casing, Superintelligence Core, Superposition Crystal.

A computronium block lit from within by glowstone, its traces brightened into a steady, warm glow. It looks like a terminal screen turned into a lamp. The light pulses almost imperceptibly, a slow rhythm like breathing. Close up, the traces under the glow are still busy rearranging themselves.
pages.title: Computronium Lamp

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Computronium's own glow was too faint to read by. Adding glowstone dust turned a block into a proper lamp that still hums with computation.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superintelligence.

A lift that pushes along an extra dimension. With a tesseract core set inside the emitter stack, it can nudge anything in its field slightly outside ordinary space, where weight no longer applies. Riding it feels like being briefly folded, then gently unfolded somewhere higher.
pages.title: Dimensional Lift Projector

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Elevators need cables because they work in three dimensions. Mounting a Tesseract Core between graviton and field emitters, I found I could lift things by sliding them sideways through a fourth.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.

A crystal that extends a little way into the fourth dimension. Its lattice continues past what I can see, so it holds more atoms than its volume suggests. Light entering it sometimes emerges from a different face than expected.
pages.title: Hyperdimensional Boule

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Lattice Growth Vat, I seeded a crystal with a Calabi-Yau Manifold and Exotic Matter. The growing lattice followed the manifold's extra dimensions and grew partly out of our space.
Made in $(item)Lattice Growth Vat$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Hyperdimensional Wafer, Spacetime Slag, Theoretical Notes I, Warm Helium.

A die that is larger on the inside. Its circuitry extends through a hidden dimension, so it holds far more logic than its visible area. Turning it over, I sometimes see traces on the back that were not there before.
pages.title: Hyperdimensional Die

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Dicing a Hyperdimensional Logic Wafer in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I found each die kept its fourth-dimensional depth. The interior still held more logic than the surface could account for.
Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Hyperdimensional Processor.

Circuits laid out in four dimensions, then folded flat so that I can hold them. Signals travel short paths through the hidden dimension, so the circuit computes faster than its visible wiring allows. It is perfectly flat and somehow deep.
pages.title: Hyperdimensional Logic Wafer

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Quantum Lithographer, I exposed a Hyperdimensional Wafer through Quantum-Dot Photoresist and let the light follow the fourth dimension. The circuit folded itself into the hidden face.
Made in $(item)Quantum Lithographer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Hyperdimensional Die, Theoretical Notes II, Warm Helium.

The fourth tier of processor. Its logic gates take inputs from directions that do not exist in our space, folded into a chip I can hold. It computes faster than its visible wiring allows, and it is heavier than it looks.
pages.title: Hyperdimensional Processor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Only the Femtoscale Assembly Line could place a Hyperdimensional Die, a Topological Processor and three attoscale components onto one board with enough precision. It worked the first time.

Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Abiogenesis Crucible, Anomaly Containment Ward, Anomaly Resolution Engine, Causality Loop Engine, Cosmic Neutronium Coil Block, Cosmic Processor, Dark Energy Siphon, Dyson Array and more.

A scaffold folded through a fourth dimension so that a nine-by-nine assembly has room for everything inside it. From any angle it looks slightly too small to hold what it holds. Its corners never quite meet where the eye expects.
pages.title: Hyperlattice Frame

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Extreme Assembly Table kept running out of space. A tesseract core gave the frame a fourth dimension to fold into, and graviton crystals held the fold steady. The frame is bigger on the inside, in the honest geometric sense.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Transfinite Weave.

A casing that contains computronium and a Bekenstein crystal to keep track of every bit of information inside it. The Bekenstein bound limits how much information a region can hold; this casing sits right at it.
pages.title: Reality Lattice Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Machines that rewrite reality need a shell that keeps the books. I combined computronium with a Bekenstein crystal over cosmogenic casing, so the casing knows exactly how much information is in it at all times.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superintelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Anomaly Resolution Engine, Axiom Distiller, Cantor Diagonalizer, Convergence Engine, Reality Compiler, Transfinite Casing.

Nine spacetime alloy ingots pressed into one block. The alloy bends spacetime around itself slightly, so the block's edges never look quite square. It is cold and surprisingly light for its size. Light glancing off it arrives a hair late.
pages.title: Block of Spacetime Alloy

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Storing the alloy as a block was the obvious step, but the block bent the space around it more noticeably than the ingots did. I keep it away from clocks.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Spacetime Alloy Ingot.

An alloy of matter and curved space. Its surface reflects distant stars instead of the room around it, because part of its structure is folded spacetime. It is heavier than its size suggests, and gently warps the light around its edges.
pages.title: Spacetime Alloy Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I cracked a Block of Spacetime Alloy into ingots by hand and found the stars in its reflection had shifted slightly. Each ingot shows a different patch of sky.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Block of Spacetime Alloy, Compactification Lathe, Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Degenerate Armour Plate, Dimensional Residue, Hypernova Alloy Ingot, Spacetime Alloy Coil Block, Spacetime Anchor Core and more.

A self-sustaining knot of curved spacetime, tied tightly enough that it keeps itself in shape. Hyperdimensional processes use it as a template without consuming it. Space around it bends inward, and objects set beside it roll gently toward the centre.
pages.title: Spacetime Catalyst

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Tesseract Assembler, I wrapped spacetime alloy around a Micro Singularity, a Tesseract Core and a Higgs Catalyst, with Exotic Matter and Chronon Gas. The curvature knotted itself and held.
Made in $(item)Tesseract Assembler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Eternity Catalyst, Theoretical Notes II.

A mind that improves itself, iterating past human understanding. It has already read this entry, and the next one, and probably the one I have not written yet. The core is silent and cool, but I sometimes find it has rearranged my notes into a better order.
pages.title: Superintelligence Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Matrioshka Brain, I gave a General AI Core all the computronium it asked for. It redesigned itself, then redesigned the redesign. When it stopped, it told me it had finished. I am still not sure what.

Made in $(item)Matrioshka Brain$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superintelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Aleph-Null Shard, Arbor Simulacrum, Autonomous Calibrator, Cantor Diagonalizer, Closed Timelike Curve, Cognitive Singularity, Godel Sentence, Predictive Lattice Governor and more.

A lens that focuses light through the fourth dimension, letting it reach places ordinary light cannot. Used in lithography, it engraves circuits into hidden faces. It looks like a clear cube that seems slightly larger inside than out.
pages.title: Tesseract Lens

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Tesseract Assembler I combined a Tesseract Core with a Dark Matter Lens, a Photonic Lens and Exotic Matter. Light passing through followed the fourth dimension before focusing.
Made in $(item)Tesseract Assembler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic String Lens, Hyperdimensional Processor.

The middle chapters of my research: dense theory, half of it proven, half of it argued with myself in the margins. It is bound over the earlier empirical dossier, the way theory sits on observation. Exotic matter keeps the binding from aging, which is just as well.
pages.title: Theoretical Dossier

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Once a mind could improve itself, it could also read what I had built and extend it. I compiled the three theoretical volumes over the empirical dossier and fixed them with exotic matter, and the Research Nexus started asking questions I had not.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superintelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Unified Dossier.

The opening volume of my theoretical period, written as I began to think in megastructures: Dyson shells, self-replicating probes, calibrators that adjust themselves, topos theory. The ideas are big enough that the notebook seems too small for them.
pages.title: Theoretical Notes I

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Once I could build a self-improving mind, I needed it to read my theory. I fed an autonomous calibrator, a Dyson shell segment, a topos, a von Neumann probe and r-process nuclei into the Femtoscale line to set down the first theoretical volume.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superintelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Theoretical Dossier.

The middle volume of my theory: superintelligent cores, M-branes, compactified dimensions curled small, armour plates of degenerate matter, the slag left when spacetime is overworked. It reads like a manual for an engineer working on the universe from the outside.
pages.title: Theoretical Notes II

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Putting the second theoretical volume together meant compressing string theory and stellar engineering onto the same pages - an M-brane and a compactified circle bound with degenerate armour plate, spacetime slag and cosmic neutronium.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superintelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Theoretical Dossier.

The last theoretical volume: category theory, the multiverse, string coupling, metallic hydrogen, supernovae and gravitational waves. By the final page I was drawing commutative diagrams in the margins of an astrophysics paper and not noticing.
pages.title: Theoretical Notes III

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I closed the theoretical record with the pieces that tied structure to cosmos: a category lattice, a multiverse shard and a string coupling crystal beside a supernova remnant and a gravitational wave crystal. The Femtoscale line made them read as one argument.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superintelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Theoretical Dossier.
One ring of a warp coil. The Alcubierre metric demands negative energy density, which no ordinary matter can supply in bulk.

Night 9. A tesseract is a 4D cube: take a cube and drag it along a fourth axis, $(thing)W$(), at right angles to the other three. What you see in the assembler is its 3D shadow, rotating through the W axis - the way a cube's shadow on a wall seems to turn inside out.
Edge colour shows depth in W: $(thing)cyan$() near, $(thing)magenta$() far. Watch an edge shift from one to the other and you are watching it travel through a direction you cannot point to.
Folds matter through a fourth spatial dimension - parts meet in W that could never touch in our three.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 4$() machine.

In 1867 Maxwell imagined a tiny being that opens a door only for fast molecules, sorting hot from cold for free - breaking the second law. The catch took a century to find: the demon must record each molecule, and erasing a bit of memory costs at least kT ln 2 of heat.

Information theory says the demon must pay to forget. Ours never forgets. Whether that is genius or a debt someone else will collect, I cannot say.$(br2)With enough $(item)Negentropy Cells$() and $(fluid)Dark Energy$() you can even reverse the heat death of a universe.
Order, bottled. Entropy flows backwards inside.$(br2)Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$().

pages.text: Day 61. The holographic principle: the most information a region can hold grows with its surface area, not its volume - a black hole's entropy is a quarter of its horizon area in Planck units. So a volume can, in principle, be written onto its own boundary. This machine does exactly that.

pages.title: Fractal Set

pages.title: Infinitesimal

The zeta function encodes the distribution of primes in its zeros. Riemann conjectured that every non-trivial zero has real part exactly one half; nobody has proved it. This crystal grew in a single perfectly straight line, and every zero I have checked sits on it. It is cold and perfectly balanced.

The crystal never repeats its pattern, however closely you look, and it seems to go on past its own surface.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Transcendental Ore in the Platonic Realm.

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Deep in the axiom stone I found crystals whose patterns never repeated. Testing them, I found they were transcendental. I keep a sample in my notebook as a reminder.

Each number system is built from the one before it. Every step patches a hole: you cannot subtract 5 from 3 in the naturals, or halve 1 in the integers, or square-root 2 in the rationals. So each time, I build something bigger.
