Feynman's insight: a particle takes every possible path at once, and the probabilities add up with phases. Most paths cancel; the classical one survives. The integral shimmers with countless faint trails, all overlapping.
pages.title: Path Integral

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Summing virtual quark trajectories weighted by the Hamiltonian, I found that the straight paths dominated while the rest cancelled. The Analytic Continuator kept them all.
Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Theory of Everything.
$(thing)Planck Mite$(). Lives in: Quantum Foam.$(br)Drops: Foam Substrate, Virtual Monopole.
pages.title: Planck Mite

pages.text: A two-level quantum system held in superposition: zero and one at once, weighted by complex amplitudes, until a measurement forces it to choose. Carrying it is an exercise in restraint, because looking too closely collapses it. It feels slightly cold, and its faint glow flickers between two colours without ever settling.
pages.title: Qubit

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Quantum Entangler I trapped one half of an Entangled Photon Pair inside a Quantum Dot. The dot's two energy levels held the photon's state cleanly, and I had my first stable qubit: a bit that refused to be either value.

Made in $(item)Quantum Entangler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Entanglement.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Antimatter Penning Trap, Axiom Schema, Chronon Capacitor, Chronon Field Inverter, Chronon Gas, Error-Correction Lattice, Femtoscale Transistor, Formal Proof Assistant and more.

The place where general relativity fails. Curvature becomes infinite and the equations stop giving answers. The fluid is cold and black, and space around it is torn. Rulers placed in it disagree with themselves, and clocks show no time at all.
pages.title: Relativity Breakdown

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)At the heart of a singularity, relativity predicts its own failure. I found a fluid where that failure was made manifest, a pool of broken spacetime.
Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Christoffel Symbol, Einstein-Rosen Core, Geodesic Thread, Stress-Energy Tensor.

The boundary where quantum mechanics stops behaving. It is a still, cold fluid in which superpositions persist indefinitely, never collapsing. Looking at it, I see both outcomes at once. Measurements dipped into it return every answer at once.
pages.title: Schrödinger's Limit

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pushing quantum systems to their edge, I found a limit beyond which they never collapsed. Schrodinger's cat would live and die forever here.
Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Eigenstate Lattice, Hamiltonian Operator, Path Integral, Wavefunction.

A coil of wire cooled below its critical temperature, where electrical resistance drops to exactly zero. Current set running in it circulates forever, and the magnetic field it produces is steady as bedrock. It is frosted with cold and pulls gently at anything iron nearby.
pages.title: Superconducting Coil

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Winding neutronium wire through a bath of Superfluid Helium in the Metamaterial Weaver, I watched the resistance fall off a cliff to zero. Weeks later the current was still running. Derelict stations kept spares, I later noticed.

Made in $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Anomaly Vault chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Cryogenics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Alcubierre Coil, Analytic Continuator, Antimatter Pellet, Antimatter Penning Trap, Antiproton Decelerator, Autonomous Extreme Assembler, Axiom Distiller, Cantor Diagonalizer and more.

Helium so cold it flows without friction. It climbs the walls of its container in a thin film, leaks through gaps too small for any normal liquid and never stops swirling once set in motion. It is utterly clear and almost weightless in the pipe.
pages.title: Superfluid Helium

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Distilling warm helium in the Fractionation Spire, the bottom tier collected a liquid that crept up the column walls by itself. Below the lambda point, helium-4 had lost all viscosity.

Made in $(item)Fractionation Spire$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Cryogenics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Abiogenesis Crucible, Annihilation Core, Anomaly Containment Ward, Anomaly Resolution Engine, Antihelium Nucleus, Antihydrogen Crystal, Antimatter Pellet, Autonomous Calibrator and more.

A crystal lattice that has not decided which arrangement of atoms it is in, so it occupies several configurations at once. Its outline shimmers slightly at the edges, and its weight seems to vary depending on how I hold it. Every facet reflects a slightly different room.
pages.title: Superposition Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I placed a Qubit on a scrap of Foam Substrate in the Quantum Entangler, hoping to stabilise it. Instead the qubit's indecision spread into the substrate, and the whole lattice entered superposition without collapsing.

Made in $(item)Quantum Entangler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Entanglement.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Attoscale Transistor, Claytronic Catom, Crystalline Matrix Ingot, Error-Correction Lattice, General AI Core, Hyperframe Casing, Neural Synthesizer, Psionic Crystal and more.

A boule doped with topological insulator, so its surface conducts and its interior never will. Sliced into wafers, each slice keeps the same protected edges. It is dark grey with a faint metallic sheen around its outside.
pages.title: Topological Boule

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Growing a boule from a Lattice Seed Crystal with Topological Insulator and a condensate in the Lattice Growth Vat, I found the protected surface states grew with it, layer by layer.
Made in $(item)Lattice Growth Vat$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Topological Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Empirical Notes II, Spacetime Slag, Topological Wafer, Warm Helium.

A die of topologically protected logic, cut from a braided wafer. Its anyon braids survive the cut because topology does not depend on where the edge is. It is grey and unremarkable to look at, which belies how hard it is to break.
pages.title: Topological Die

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Planck-Scale Cutter, I diced a Topological Logic Wafer, worried I would cut through the braids. Each die simply formed new protected edges where I had sliced.
Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Topological Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Topological Processor.

An insulator in its interior but a conductor on its surface, and the surface states are protected by topology: no small defect or scratch can remove them, any more than a knot can be undone without cutting. It feels like dull grey glass, yet current skates around its skin without hesitation.
pages.title: Topological Insulator

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pushing a Metamaterial Sheet through a phase transition in the Topological Phase Transmuter, with a qubit to read the band structure, I saw the edge states appear and refuse to vanish no matter how I damaged the sample.

Made in $(item)Topological Phase Transmuter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Topological Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Attoscale Transistor, Calabi-Yau Manifold, Differential Manifold, Dimensional Stabiliser Matrix, Hawking Emitter, Hyperframe Casing, Möbius Strip, Plasma Nozzle Tip and more.

A wafer of braided anyons: quasiparticles whose exchange paths store information in the topology of their braids. Errors cannot touch them, because no small disturbance can untie a braid. Its surface carries a faint woven pattern.
pages.title: Topological Logic Wafer

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Quantum Lithographer, a Topological Wafer engraved through Quantum-Dot Photoresist produced anyons at the edges. Braiding them by moving the light, I wrote logic into their paths.
Made in $(item)Quantum Lithographer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Topological Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Topological Die, Warm Helium.

A pump whose rotor spins so fast that its blades knock gas molecules out of the chamber one by one. It whines at a pitch just below hearing. Ultra-high vacuum starts here. The rotor blades are angled like a jet turbine, and they spin faster than the eye can follow.
pages.title: Turbomolecular Vacuum Pump

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Mechanical pumps stop at a rough vacuum. A turbomolecular rotor, driven by a superconducting coil on neutronium and spacetime casing, kicked out the remaining molecules.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Cryogenics.

A pipe of containment field glass and metamaterial lined with Casimir plates, so the space inside is emptier than empty. A particle beam runs through it without touching anything at all. Peering inside shows nothing, not even a reflection.
pages.title: Vacuum Beam Pipe

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Particle beams scatter off any gas. I lined containment glass with Casimir plates, which push out even virtual particles, and wrapped it in metamaterial. The beam stopped scattering.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Metamaterials.
$(thing)Vacuum Drifter$(). Lives in: Quantum Foam.$(br)Drops: False Vacuum Membrane, Virtual Graviton.
pages.title: Vacuum Drifter

pages.text: A quantum of gravity that has not decided to exist yet, flickering between being and not being. It pulls faintly on everything near it, and then on nothing. Nobody has ever detected a real graviton; this one is not quite real.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Ephemeral Graviton Ore in the Quantum Foam; dropped by the Vacuum Drifter (the Quantum Foam).
pages.title: Virtual Graviton

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Vacuum Drifters in the Quantum Foam dropped these when killed. The Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester let me catch more from between Casimir plates, cooled with superfluid helium.

Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Ephemeral Graviton Ore$(), in veins through the Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Vacuum Drifter.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Graviton Crystal, Miniature Black Hole, Miniature Wormhole.

A magnet with only one pole, borrowed from the vacuum and destined to return. Real monopoles have never been found, though grand unified theories predict them. This one pushes one end of a compass needle away and never pulls the other.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Ephemeral Monopole Ore in the Quantum Foam; dropped by the Planck Mite (the Quantum Foam).
pages.title: Virtual Monopole

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Planck Mites in the Quantum Foam dropped these. Harvesting more from between Casimir plates, I found they only lasted as long as the superfluid helium kept them cold.

Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Ephemeral Monopole Ore$(), in veins through the Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Planck Mite.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Magnetic Monopole, Penteract Display, Tesseract Display.

pages.title: Virtual Pair

pages.text: Light that was never emitted and will never be absorbed, existing only between two charges as the carrier of their force. It glows faintly from no direction in particular and vanishes from view when looked at directly.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Ephemeral Photon Ore in the Quantum Foam; dropped by the Virtual Pair (the Quantum Foam).
pages.title: Virtual Photon

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Virtual Pairs left these behind in the Quantum Foam. Later I harvested them from between Casimir plates, where they press the plates together in the Casimir effect.

Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Ephemeral Photon Ore$(), in veins through the Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Virtual Pair.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dyson Sphere Model, Eigenstate Lattice, Entangled Photon Pair, Galaxy in a Box, Miniature Pulsar, Miniature White Hole, Pocket Universe Display.

A quark borrowed from the vacuum, existing only on credit granted by the uncertainty principle. The more energy it has, the sooner it must be returned. It tugs constantly at the hand, trying to fall back into nothing.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Ephemeral Quark Ore in the Quantum Foam; dropped by the Virtual Pair (the Quantum Foam).
pages.title: Virtual Quark

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Virtual Pairs in the Quantum Foam dropped these when they split. Later, the Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester let me pull them from between Casimir plates and keep them cold enough to stay.

Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Ephemeral Quark Ore$(), in veins through the Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Virtual Pair.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Antiproton Bundle, Miniature Quasar, Path Integral, Strange & Charm Quarks, Unified Notes III, Up & Down Quarks.

Everything a particle could be, written as one complex-valued function. Its square gives the probability of finding the particle anywhere. The function hovers above the palm as a faint, shifting haze that never settles into one shape.
pages.title: Wavefunction

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Combining a qubit with the complex plane on a foam substrate, and adding Schrodinger's Limit, I described a particle's state completely. The Analytic Continuator called it a wavefunction.
Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Feynman Diagram, Hamiltonian Operator, Quantum Singularity.
Casing for a machine that stitches with entanglement. Two particles that share one state stay linked, however far apart the weave carries them.

pages.text: How it works for real: a pump photon enters a nonlinear crystal and splits into two lower-energy photons with correlated polarisations. Measure one and you know the other, however far away. No signal travels - Einstein's 'spooky action', but no message.

First dive. Below the Planck length, spacetime is not smooth. The $(item)Planck Diver$() takes me there.

Wheeler called it quantum foam. Inside: membranes of $(item)Foam Substrate$() between bubbles of nothing, where false-vacuum bubbles swell and pop. A false vacuum is a state that looks stable but is not the lowest - I try not to stand near them.

Matter here is borrowed. $(item)Ephemeral Ores$() condense out of the foam and vanish again a few minutes later, and anything dropped dissolves back into the vacuum within half a minute. Mine fast. (Virtual particles live on borrowed energy too: the bigger the loan, the sooner it is repaid.)

Every virtual particle has a $(thing)resonance$() that changes smoothly from place to place. The $(item)Resonance Probe$() reads all four where you stand; the strongest field decides which ore grows there.

The $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$() catches whichever particle its dial is tuned closest to - so the same harvester makes quarks in one place and gravitons fifty blocks away. Read the probe, then tune. It took me a whole afternoon of unwanted gravitons to learn that.
Shrinks you past the Planck length into the Quantum Foam. Use again to come back.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.
Reads the four virtual-particle resonances where you stand in the Quantum Foam.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.

The $(item)Topological Phase Transmuter$() changes a material's topology without changing its chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.
pages.title: Topological Phase Transmuter

pages.text: Topology is about what survives smooth deformation: a mug and a doughnut are the same shape, one hole each. In topological materials the same atoms can sit in phases that differ only in such global properties. Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz shared the 2016 Nobel for it.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

Final pages. Every computation the universe will ever perform, converging on a single point at the end of time: the $(item)Omega Point$(). It is the last thing you can make.

Frank Tipler's 1994 idea: a collapsing universe in which computation speeds up without limit, so infinite thought fits before the end. Cosmology has since argued against it. Mine exists anyway - and a Zero-Point Extractor will happily run on it for ten hours.
The final state of all computation. It already knows how this ends.$(br2)Made in $(item)Omnilex Engine$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Omega Point$(): Identity Kernel, Omega Simulator, Omnilex Engine, Omniscience Catalyst, Omnium Energy Cell and more

Final entry in this series. A captive black hole wrapped in anchors, lenses and stabilisers - used as a computer. It simulates stars, galaxies, universes, and keeps what falls out.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 7$() machine.

pages.text: Note to self: this controller is too complex for a crafting grid. It has to be built on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts before ordering anything.

Why a black hole? By the $(thing)Bekenstein bound$(), a horizon holds the most information any region of space can. Bekenstein and Hawking showed its entropy scales with horizon area, not volume. If anything can hold a universe in memory, it is this.

Three simulations, each gated by coil tier:$(li)a $(thing)stellar life cycle$() (tier 4)$(li)a $(thing)galaxy$() (tier 5)$(li)a whole $(thing)cosmology$() (tier 5)$(br2)Each run returns a huge spread of materials - and $(item)Horizon Shards$().
Last note on throughput: field emitter tiers multiply its parallels, just like every other multiblock. I keep looking into the lens and feeling it look back.

A $(thing)kugelblitz$() (German: 'ball lightning') is a real prediction of general relativity: energy curves spacetime just as mass does, so enough light in a small enough volume forms a horizon. Nobody has made one. The required intensity is absurd. Apparently, not here.

Lesson learned the hard way: while running, the singularity at its heart bends light around it ($(thing)gravitational lensing$()) and pulls in loose items and creatures. My spare tools are gone. Keep your distance.

Observation log. A running singularity bends light around its horizon: the room behind it is smeared into an $(thing)Einstein ring$(), with a bright $(thing)photon ring$() at the edge of the shadow.$(br2)White holes do the opposite.

The physics: mass curves spacetime and light follows the curve. A source directly behind the hole reaches me from every side - the ring. At 1.5 Schwarzschild radii photons can orbit; that is the photon ring, the same feature the Event Horizon Telescope imaged in M87*.
Practical note: if this conflicts with a shader pack, it can be disabled in the client config ($(thing)gravitationalLensing$()). The universe will still be curved; you just won't see it.

Beef, pork, chicken, mutton, rabbit and cod, every edible animal pressed into one dense block. It smells of a farmyard, a kitchen and a fishing dock all at once. It is technically food, and absolutely not for eating.
pages.title: Biosphere Compendium

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Building the catalyst meant compressing every field of knowledge, including biology. On the Extreme Assembly Table I pressed one of each edible creature together into a single record of the food chain.
Made in $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Engineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omniscience Catalyst.
The shell of an observatory that waits for bursts lasting milliseconds that never repeat. It is built to sit very still for a very long time.

Nine ingots of cosmic neutronium fused into a block denser than the inside of a neutron star. It is hard to pick up and harder to put down gently. It casts a faint, cold shadow even in full light. A few faint points of light swim deep inside it.
pages.title: Block of Cosmic Neutronium

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Cosmic neutronium was too precious to leave loose. Pressing it into a block was easy; moving the block afterwards was not, but the supply is safe.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Engineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Singularity Energy Cell, Transcendent Cache.

Neutronium compressed together with dark matter in the heart of a star. Starlight drifts through its interior, slowly, as though it were a tiny galaxy. It is the heaviest thing I own and gives off a faint, cold glow.
pages.title: Cosmic Neutronium Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Breaking a Block of Cosmic Neutronium apart by hand, I found each ingot still held its own drifting starlight. It is the strongest material I have ever worked.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Engineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Pedestal, Biosphere Compendium, Block of Cosmic Neutronium, Cantor Diagonalizer, Cosmic Flux Coupler, Cosmic Neutronium Coil Block, Dimensional Residue, Hyperdimensional Pearl and more.

A sliver of a disc that recorded the Big Bang, cut from Cherenkov quartz and neutronium. Play it and you hear the cosmic microwave background, a faint hiss left from the first moments of everything. It is cool and heavy, and vibrates faintly.
pages.title: Cosmic Record Fragment

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Cherenkov quartz responds to fast particles; neutronium records pressure. Pressing them together on the Extreme Assembly Table, I found the fragment picked up the oldest signal in the universe.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omniscience Catalyst.

A one-dimensional defect in spacetime left over from a phase transition in the early universe: a line of trapped false vacuum, thinner than a proton but immensely heavy. Space around it is cut and rejoined with a missing wedge, so objects beside it appear doubled. It hums when it moves.
pages.title: Cosmic String Segment

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)When a White Hole Fragment emitted through a Hawking Emitter, its outflow cooled too quickly and froze into defects. In the White Hole Emitter I caught one: a filament of the early universe. A bulk monolith also held one, coiled up.

Made in $(item)White Hole Emitter$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Bulk Monolith chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): White Holes.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Circuit Board, Cosmic String Lens, Cosmic String Segment, Dark Energy, Dimensional Residue, Exotic Matter, Exotic Matter Crystal, Exotic Matter Singularity and more.
A mass packed so tightly that time itself runs slow around it. Clocks set nearby lose seconds to the rest of the world, and never get them back.
pages.title: Dense Mass Core

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Time Dilation Chamber.

A stabiliser that holds the number of dimensions in a region fixed while machines nearby try to change it. A dimensional stabiliser matrix sets the count, and a field emitter enforces it. Near it, corners look properly square.
pages.title: Dimensional Stabiliser

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Hyperdimensional machines kept bleeding extra dimensions into the lab. I built a stabiliser around a dimensional stabiliser matrix with a field emitter and hyperframe casing, and the room stayed three-dimensional.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.

pages.text: The final second of an evaporating black hole: hotter and brighter the smaller it gets, until nothing is left but the light.
pages.title: Last Flash of a Black Hole

A casing with a dark metamaterial skin over spacetime casing and neutronium plate: whatever reaches it from inside does not come back out. It is utterly black and seems to absorb the edges of nearby objects.
pages.title: Event Horizon Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Machines handling black holes needed housings that behaved like horizons. A metamaterial sheet that bends light around itself, over neutronium plate and spacetime casing, made a one-way wall.

Matter with negative energy density, the stuff wormholes and warp drives require. It pushes against gravity, bends light the wrong way, and sits in its flask like a pool of shadow that is somehow lighter than air.
pages.title: Exotic Matter

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Separating dimensional residue in the Fractionation Spire, one fraction refused to sink or rise in the usual way. It had negative energy density. The exotic matter of Morris and Thorne, distilled from leftovers.

A compact emitter of neutronium plate, Cherenkov quartz and a quantum dot that projects a field shaped by the dot's quantum state. Change the state, change the field. It sits warm and quiet, faintly buzzing.
pages.title: Field Emitter

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Multiblocks kept needing local fields of different shapes. A quantum dot can hold a programmed state, and Cherenkov quartz can turn that state into a field. I have also found ready-made emitters in anomaly vaults.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Anomaly Vault chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chronal Field Projector, Dark Energy Siphon, Dark Matter Halo Collector, Dimensional Lift Projector, Dimensional Stabiliser, Graviton Field Emitter, Graviton Field Projector, Hawking Radiation Collector and more.

A dark-matter lens trimmed so its Einstein ring falls exactly where it is needed. Gravitational lensing bends light from distant objects into rings and arcs; this one is tuned to focus gravity on a chosen point. It looks like a faint distortion in empty air.
pages.title: Gravitic Lens Element

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Metamaterial Weaver I trimmed a Dark Matter Lens with Metamaterial Sheet and Entangled Photon Pairs to measure the focus. Adjusting the Dark Matter, the Einstein ring settled exactly where I wanted it.

Made in $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Anomaly Resolution Engine, Empirical Notes III, Graviton Field Emitter, Graviton Lens Array.

An array of gravitic lens elements that bend spacetime to focus gravitational waves, the way a glass lens bends light. Inside, the space seems to pinch toward the centre. Straight edges seen through its centre appear to bow outward, as if viewed through a thick drop of water.
pages.title: Graviton Lens Array

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Gravitational lensing is real: massive objects bend light. I set gravitic lens elements into event horizon casing over a hyperframe, and the array focused gravitational waves to a point.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Eye of the Event Horizon, Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester.

pages.title: Harmonic Pedestal

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Pedestal.

Metamaterial tuned to soak up the thermal glow of an evaporating black hole. Hawking radiation has a characteristic spectrum, and this plate absorbs it perfectly. It is warm on its front face, cool on the back, and very black.
pages.title: Hawking Absorber Plate

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Hawking radiation was leaking away from my experiments. In the Casimir Vacuum Press I bonded a Metamaterial Sheet to Neutronium Plate, tuning the metamaterial to the black hole spectrum.

Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Entangled Bus Bar, Entropy Horizon, Hawking Radiation, Hawking Radiation Collector, Horizon Diver, Last Flash of a Black Hole.

A device that channels Hawking radiation, the faint thermal glow every black hole gives off as quantum fields near its horizon split into escaping and falling particles. It feels like holding a warm coal that slowly loses mass. The colder its source, the hotter it shines.
pages.title: Hawking Emitter

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Hawking radiation leaks in every direction, so I needed a waveguide that did not care which way it came in. A Topological Insulator does just that, and wrapping it around the glow in the Chronon Field Inverter let me point it.
Made in $(item)Chronon Field Inverter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Bekenstein Crystal, Cosmic String Segment, Exotic Matter.

The faint glow of a black hole evaporating. Pairs of particles at the horizon are split, one falls in and the other escapes, carrying away a sliver of the black hole's mass. It is thermal, dim and cold, and in it the hole slowly dies.
pages.title: Hawking Radiation

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Hawking showed black holes are not quite black. Feeding a Kugelblitz Seed through the Penrose Ergosphere Generator, my detectors picked up a thermal glow leaking from the horizon itself.

Made in $(item)Micro Black Hole Evaporator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Bekenstein Crystal, Cosmic String Segment, Exotic Matter, Gravitational Wave Crystal, Graviton Crystal, Hawking Emitter, Residual Starlight, Spacetime Singularity and more.

A collector of Hawking absorber plates and entangled photons that catches the faint radiation evaporating black holes give off. It is warm, and the warmth comes from somewhere it should not. It glitters faintly with stray photons.
pages.title: Hawking Radiation Collector

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Black holes radiate, very faintly, as Hawking predicted. I combined absorber plates with entangled photons to catch the partners of the emitted particles and mounted them on a field emitter.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Eye of the Event Horizon.

A sliver of event horizon, carried out of a black hole simulating a universe of its own. By the holographic principle the horizon area stores everything that ever fell inward, so this shard is less a surface than an archive. It is black from every angle and slightly cold, as Hawking radiation would predict.
pages.title: Horizon Shard

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Eye of the Event Horizon computes a whole universe on a black hole's surface. Seeding a fresh simulation with a universe seed, liquid spacetime and an existing shard, I found a new sliver of horizon peeled off as the simulated cosmos ended.

Made in $(item)Eye of the Event Horizon$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Axiomatic Field Emitter, Cosmological Constant, False Vacuum, Graviton Crystal, Heat Death Remnant, Horizon Shard, Inflaton Field, Pocket Universe and more.

A casing laced with topological insulator and superposition crystal, so that its interior exists in several overlapping configurations at once. It looks solid but sounds slightly hollow, as though echoing in a direction I cannot see.
pages.title: Hyperframe Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Hyperdimensional machines needed a frame that could be in more than one shape. Topological insulators conduct only on the surface and superposition crystals hold several states, and together over spacetime casing they gave the frame its depth.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chronoplastic Casing, Compactification Lathe, Containment Cache, Dimensional Stabiliser, Graviton Condenser, Graviton Lens Array, Higgs Field Modulator, Hyperlattice Frame and more.

Enough energy concentrated in one place that it collapses into a black hole under its own gravity. Energy curves spacetime just as mass does, so even pure light, focused tightly enough, falls inward. The seed hums with heat, and I never point it toward anything I value.
pages.title: Kugelblitz Seed

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Kugelblitz Chamber I annihilated antimatter against strange matter inside a shell of dark matter, so none of the energy escaped. Focused enough, it stopped being light and became a horizon waiting to form.
Made in $(item)Kugelblitz Chamber$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Empirical Notes I, Hawking Radiation, Micro Singularity.
A mast that holds mass where its curvature bends passing light. A gravitational lens has no single focal point: it brings light together along a line.
pages.title: Lens Pylon

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Lensing Concentrator.

Spacetime itself, flowing like a liquid. Distances inside it are fluid, and it ripples with gravitational waves when disturbed. It is cold and has no colour, only the distortion of what is behind it. Poured, it bends the light of the room around the stream.
pages.title: Liquid Spacetime

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Some theories describe spacetime as an emergent fluid. Feeding a Cosmic String Segment and raw star matter into the Eye of the Event Horizon, the simulation melted spacetime into a liquid.

Made in $(item)Eye of the Event Horizon$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmological Constant, False Vacuum, Graviton Crystal, Heat Death Remnant, Horizon Shard, Inflaton Field, Omnium Ingot, Pocket Universe and more.

A casing that holds plasma away from its own walls with superconducting magnetic fields, tuned by dilithium. It works on the same principle as a tokamak. It hums, and the hum gets louder when plasma is near.
pages.title: Magnetic Confinement Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Plasma at stellar temperatures melts anything it touches. I wound superconducting coil around spacetime casing and tuned it with dilithium so the field keeps the plasma floating in the middle and away from the walls.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Matter-Antimatter Annihilation Reactor, Mirror Matter Foundry, Neutron Star Forge, Nucleosynthesis Chamber, Nuclide Forge, Plasma Crucible Casing, Plasma Injection Nozzle, Stellar Containment Plate and more.

The object that tells you how to measure distance and time in curved spacetime: feed it two directions and it returns a number. In flat space it is simple; around stars and black holes it varies from point to point. The tensor is smooth and slightly warped when held.
pages.title: Metric Tensor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Flat Minkowski geometry was not enough near massive things. I differentiated the lattice and weighted it with a neutronium plate, and the Tensor Calculus Engine returned the curved metric that described it.

Made in $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Alcubierre Coil, Brane Tether, Causal Set Seed, Riemann Curvature Tensor, Spacetime Singularity, Spin Foam Lattice, Spin Network Loom, Spin Network Node and more.

One step past degenerate electrons: here the electrons have been pressed into the protons and only neutrons remain, packed shoulder to shoulder as in a neutron star. Something keeps it from springing back to ordinary matter, and I am grateful.
pages.title: Neutronium Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I first found bars of it stacked in an anomaly vault, already stabilised by someone who came before me. Working out how they held it together became the backbone of everything I built afterwards, and I have used it in nearly every machine since.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Anomaly Vault, Crashed Satellite, Fallout Shelter Stores, Observatory Ruin chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Notes II, Block of Neutronium, Bose-Einstein Condenser, Brane Shifter, Casimir Vacuum Press, Chronosteel Ingot, Coherent Wiring Harness, Computronium Ingot and more.

A sheet of neutron-degenerate matter rolled down to a thickness of a few femtometres, a handful of nucleons across. It is strong enough to hold back vacuum pressure and thin enough that light should barely notice it, yet it blocks everything. Bending it feels like trying to fold a mountain into a letter.
pages.title: Neutronium Plate

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Ordinary rollers simply sank into neutronium ingots. The Casimir Vacuum Press solved it: by letting the vacuum itself push from both sides, I could squeeze the ingot evenly until it spread into a plate thinner than an atomic nucleus.

Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Analytic Continuator, Bioreactor, Brane Tether, CPT Mirror, Casimir Plate, Chemical Reactor, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Dipole Bending Magnet and more.

A nozzle that fires plasma into a confinement chamber at a precisely controlled rate. Magnetic confinement steers it, a cryocooler keeps the coils cold, and the tip glows white when in use. The air around the tip crackles.
pages.title: Plasma Injection Nozzle

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Feeding plasma into a nucleosynthesis chamber needs precision. I fitted a plasma nozzle tip into magnetic confinement casing with a superconducting coil block and a cryocooler, and the plasma went exactly where I aimed.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Nucleosynthesis Chamber.

A casing of neutronium plate around a photonic processor and a femtoscale inductor, built so that nothing inside it vibrates by more than a fraction of a proton. It is dead silent and dead still. Even the dust on it seems to settle more carefully.
pages.title: Precision Assembly Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Femtoscale assembly is ruined by the slightest tremor. I combined photonic processors for control with femtoscale inductors to cancel vibration, and the casing held parts steady enough to join.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Abiogenesis Crucible, Femtoscale Assembly Line, Gene Sequencer, Research Nexus.

Wheat, carrot, potato, beetroot, melon and pumpkin, every staple crop combined into a single seed. It is warm and slightly damp and seems ready to sprout into all of them at once. Planting it would probably be unwise.
pages.title: Primordial Harvest

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Agriculture belonged in the catalyst too, so I pressed every crop I could grow into one seed on the Extreme Assembly Table. It holds the genome of a whole harvest.
Made in $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Engineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omniscience Catalyst.

A quadrupole magnet with four pole tips that squeeze a particle beam in one direction while stretching it in the other. Pairs of them focus a beam the way lenses focus light. Its four poles alternate north and south around the bore, and the field between them is zero at the very centre.
pages.title: Quadrupole Focusing Magnet

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A beam spreads as it travels. Quadrupoles focus it like lenses. I fitted quadrupole pole tips to a superconducting coil on spacetime casing and the beam stayed tight.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Hyperion Synchrotron.

The matter of a star, as simulated inside a black hole. It behaves exactly as stellar material should, because the horizon simulates it perfectly. It glows with the light of a star that does not exist.
pages.title: Raw Star Matter

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Feeding a Stellar Core and dark matter into the Eye of the Event Horizon, the black hole simulated a star, and the simulation left matter behind. Raw star matter, from computation.

Made in $(item)Eye of the Event Horizon$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic String Segment, Dark Energy, Exotic Matter, Exotic Matter Crystal, Horizon Shard, Liquid Spacetime, Micro Singularity, Multiverse Shard and more.
Casing for a refinery that runs on chance. Each stage passes its product to the next by probability alone, and the averages come out exact.
pages.title: Refinery Casing

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Markov Chain Refinery.

A pedestal tuned to ring in sympathy with its neighbours, as a wine glass sings to a matching note. The first and plainest of its kind.
pages.title: Resonance Pedestal

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Harmonic Pedestal.

At the centre of this cell sits a tiny singularity, wrapped in cosmic neutronium. Energy falls into it and is held behind the horizon until it is needed. The casing never warms, though it carries more than any star.
pages.title: Singularity Energy Cell

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A black hole is the densest possible store of energy. Wrapping a Micro Singularity in cosmic neutronium around a vacuum cell gave me a battery whose capacity is limited only by its horizon.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Engineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omnium Energy Cell.

A light sail balanced exactly between a star's gravity and its radiation pressure, so it hovers in place without orbiting. It is mostly metamaterial, thin as a breath and much larger than it looks when folded. Unfolded indoors, it drifts toward the nearest lamp.
pages.title: Solar Statite

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A Dyson swarm needs collectors that can stay put. In the Casimir Vacuum Press I backed a Metamaterial Sheet with a sliver of neutronium so the light pushing it outward balanced the pull of the star.
Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Engineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dyson Swarm Satellite.

A plate of degenerate armour and spacetime alloy over magnetic confinement casing, built to hold back the pressure and heat of a star. It is impossibly heavy and faintly warm. Heat haze clings to its face even when the machine it guards is cold and silent.
pages.title: Stellar Containment Plate

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Stellar machines needed walls that would not buckle. I combined degenerate armour plate with spacetime alloy and magnetic confinement, and the plate held a star's pressure.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.

A casing of neutronium plate over event horizon casing with a Higgs field capacitor to steady its mass. It is built to hold the weight and heat of a star, and it glows faintly gold at the seams. Standing beside it feels like standing near a hearth.
pages.title: Stellar Frame Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Stellar machines put their housings under both gravity and heat. Event horizon casing kept the energy in, neutronium plate kept the shape, and a Higgs capacitor let me adjust the mass of the casing itself.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Stellar Lamp.

A stellar frame casing with glowstone at its heart, so it shines with a warm, golden light like a small star seen through a window. It is warm to stand next to. The colour is the warm yellow of a midday sun, steady and comforting, and the seams of the casing glow brightest of all.
pages.title: Stellar Lamp

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Stellar frame casing glowed at its seams already. Adding glowstone dust turned it into a lamp that gives off starlight. It is my favourite light.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Focus Receiver.

A drum of superconducting coil wound around spacetime casing. Current, once started, circulates in it forever with no loss at all. The field it makes tugs gently at anything metal nearby. Frost gathers along the windings, a reminder of how cold the wire must stay.
pages.title: Superconducting Coil Block

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Large machines needed strong, steady fields. Winding superconducting coil around spacetime casing gave me a coil that carries current indefinitely without heating, and a magnetic field that never flags.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chronosteel Coil Block, Dipole Bending Magnet, Femtoscale Assembly Line, Neutrino Condenser, Plasma Crucible Casing, Plasma Injection Nozzle, Quark-Gluon Collider.
Lead-lined shell for a fusion hall. Deuterium-tritium fusion sends out 14.1 MeV neutrons that pass through anything thin, so these walls are not.
pages.title: Tokamak Casing

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Evaporator Shield.
Casing for a ring of extreme acceleration. An accelerated observer finds warm thermal radiation where an inertial one sees empty vacuum: the Unruh effect.
pages.title: Unruh Ring Casing

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.

A projector that changes what empty space is. Exotic matter in its core shifts the vacuum energy of the region it covers, so the field inside is a slightly different universe. The edge of the effect shimmers.
pages.title: Vacuum State Projector

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The vacuum is not unique; there are many possible ground states. Feeding Exotic Matter Crystal into the projector stack let me nudge a region into a neighbouring one, briefly and safely.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.

A shard of a white hole, the time-reverse of a black hole: a horizon nothing can enter, from which matter and light only ever pour out. General relativity allows them, though nature seems shy. It feels like holding a pressure that pushes my fingers apart.
pages.title: White Hole Fragment

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The White Hole Emitter took Ejecta Rock and Primordial Ejecta from the far side of a horizon and pushed Hawking radiation through them in reverse. What crystallised could not be entered: a white hole in miniature.

Made in $(item)White Hole Emitter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): White Holes.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Notes I, Closed Timelike Curve, Cosmic String Segment, Dimensional Residue, Ejecta Rock, Exotic Matter, Miniature White Hole, Planck Shard and more.
Extracts the rotational energy of a spinning black hole via the $(thing)Penrose process$(). My first real power from a singularity.$(br2)Generates power.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.

Running figures: a $(item)Micro Singularity$() burns for twenty minutes at 65,536 FE/t. Energy leaves through the controller and any $(item)Interface Port$().

pages.text: Theory check: the equations of general relativity are time-symmetric, so every black hole solution has a reversed twin - a $(thing)white hole$(), a horizon that can only be left, never crossed inward. None has ever been observed. Its lensing ring, I note, behaves the opposite way to a black hole's.

Feed it Bose-Einstein Condensate and keep it below 5 K. Set the density, the flow, and the laser step: the flow must be subsonic before the step and supersonic after it. The Hawking temperature, ħκ/2πk_B, must stand out of the condensate's own warmth over enough shots - only Bose-Einstein Condensate as the coolant is cold enough.

Day 112. The $(item)Horizon Diver$() takes me through an event horizon. Rule one: $(thing)carry a Geodesic Anchor$(). Without one, tidal forces kill within two seconds - in the black hole and the white hole alike.

Why the tides kill: near a black hole, gravity changes so steeply over the length of a body that the feet are pulled far harder than the head. The stretching is called $(thing)spaghettification$(), and it is not a figure of speech.

Even anchored, it is hostile down here. Time is dilated: I move, swing and dig slower. Gravity is 2.5 times as strong. Below y=16 the singularity tears everything apart. $(thing)Tidal Horrors$() hunt in the dark, and their touch $(thing)spaghettifies$().

Log, second descent. An $(item)Einstein-Rosen Bridge$() stands at 0, 121, 0. I stepped through and came out inside the $(thing)white hole$() - a black hole run backwards, which nothing can enter, only leave. Low gravity, blinding light, everything pushed outward. The $(thing)Photon Moths$() here are harmless.

Neither side is enough alone. From the black hole: $(item)Tidal Alloy$() and $(item)Frozen Photons$(). From the white hole: $(item)Retrocausal Crystals$() and $(item)Primordial Ejecta$(). Together they make the $(item)Einstein-Rosen Core$() - and with it, new bridges I can build myself.
Crosses an event horizon - inward. Use again to come back out, which should be impossible.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.
Keeps your worldline your own. Without one, the inside of a black or white hole kills you in two seconds.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.

pages.title: Causality Loop Engine

pages.text: A $(thing)closed timelike curve$() is a path through spacetime that returns to its own past. General relativity allows them in a few exotic solutions; nobody has ever found one in nature.$(br2)This controller is too complex for a crafting grid. Build it on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts.

How it works: feed an item together with a $(item)Closed Timelike Curve$() and both come back - plus a second copy of the item. It works on Tesseract Cores, singularities, white hole fragments, superintelligences, stellar cores, wormhole throats and even pocket universes. I try not to think about the last one.

Is a dead universe dead forever? Statistical mechanics says no. In a finite system every state recurs (Poincaré recurrence) - for a de Sitter universe after about e^{10¹²²} years. Long before that, fluctuations happen by chance: P ∝ exp(−(Δ_E − TΔ_S)/k_BT). A single brain is far more likely than a whole world - the $(thing)Boltzmann brain$() problem.
The $(item)Entropy Horizon$() waits for one: a horizon shard and negentropy in the haze give a $(item)Boltzmann Fluctuation$() - which a Psionic Resonator turns into two $(item)Boltzmann Brains$().
And the other way out is $(thing)Conformal Cyclic Cosmology$() (in Strings & the Multiverse): the end of one aeon is the beginning of the next.

The second branch of time is $(thing)Finality$(). $(thing)Cosmic Eschatology$() starts from the acceleration equation, ä/a = −4πG(ρ + 3p/c²)/3 + Λc²/3: matter and radiation decelerate the expansion, dark energy accelerates it - and ours is accelerating (q₀ ≈ −0.53).

What happens next depends on dark energy's equation of state w = p/ρc²:$(li)w = −1 (a cosmological constant): expansion forever, to the $(thing)Heat Death$().$(li)w < −1 (phantom energy): the $(thing)Big Rip$().$(li)decaying dark energy or enough matter: the $(thing)Big Crunch$() - and perhaps a $(thing)Bounce$().$(li)at any moment, if the vacuum is metastable: $(thing)Vacuum Decay$().

spacetime/finality_eras.title: The Long Dark: Protons and Black Holes

pages.text: If the universe expands forever, its history after the stars falls into eras. The last red dwarfs die after 10¹⁴ years; then the $(thing)Degenerate Era$() of white dwarfs, neutron stars and planets - until, if grand unification is right, $(thing)Proton Decay$() dissolves them: p → e⁺ + π⁰, with a lifetime above 10³⁴ years.
Watch a tank of water long enough, like Super-Kamiokande: in the $(item)Neutrino Condenser$(), Cherenkov quartz and neutronium under 4,000 mB of water catch $(item)Proton Decay Residue$().

Then the $(thing)Black Hole Era$(): only black holes remain, radiating at T = ħc³/(8πGMk_B). A solar-mass hole takes 10⁶⁷ years to evaporate, getting hotter as it shrinks, and ends in a flash. A $(item)Kugelblitz Chamber$() evaporates a micro singularity down to its $(item)Last Flash$().

The likeliest end: maximum entropy. After the black holes, an empty de Sitter space is left, with a horizon c/H away that glows at ħH/(2πk_B) ≈ 3×10⁻³⁰ K and holds S = πc⁵k_B/(GħH²) ≈ 2×10¹²² - the most entropy there can ever be. Nothing more can happen, because nothing can get colder than its surroundings.

Build the $(item)Entropy Horizon$(). It runs matter forward to the end: proton decay residue and a black hole's last flash become $(item)Heat Death Embers$() and $(fluid)Dark Era Haze$() - photons, neutrinos and positronium atoms wider than today's observable universe. Embers under dark energy give $(item)De Sitter Horizon Shards$(), and embers with a shard give $(item)Heat Death Remnants$().

In its Operation console the simulated age must pass 10³⁴ years (or the protons have not decayed); a faster expansion makes a smaller, hotter horizon - too hot, and it boils the containment. Horizon shards and phantom cells also make a $(item)Cosmological Constant$() in the Siphon.

$(thing)The Big Rip$(): phantom dark energy (w < −1) grows denser as space grows. With w = −1.5 the Rip comes 22 billion years from now: clusters go a billion years before, the Solar System three months before, atoms in the last instant. The $(item)Dark Energy Siphon$() bottles it in a $(item)Phantom Energy Cell$().

$(thing)The Big Crunch$(): expansion reverses and everything falls together. In loop quantum cosmology the Friedmann equation gains a factor (1 − ρ/ρ_c): at the Planck density gravity repels and the collapse $(thing)bounces$(). The $(item)Neutron Star Forge$() crushes spin foam and degenerate matter into a $(item)Bounce Core$().

$(thing)Vacuum Decay$(): a bubble of the true vacuum needs a radius 2σ/ε to grow; bigger, it expands at nearly the speed of light, and inside it chemistry is impossible. The $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$() holds a $(item)True Vacuum Seed$() just below the critical radius. Please keep it there.

Two long arms at right angles, a laser split between them, and mirrors that hang free. A passing gravitational wave stretches one arm and squeezes the other by a thousandth of a proton's width.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.

pages.text: $(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

Balance the laser power and the arms' finesse between shot noise and radiation-pressure noise; add isolation stages against the ground's shaking (other machines nearby make it worse; underground is quieter); cool the test masses to beat thermal noise. A black hole merger needs a signal-to-noise of 8 at h = 10⁻²¹; a neutron star merger, five times fainter, needs cold mirrors.

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Einstein and Rosen found their bridge in the Schwarzschild solution, but it pinches shut too fast to cross. I propped the throat open with an Einstein-Rosen Core, framed it in horizon glass and tidal alloy, and it stayed open.

A spinning mass drags spacetime round with it. Near the Earth the effect is tiny; near a spinning black hole, inside its ergosphere, nothing can stand still.
Stand near a running $(item)Penrose Ergosphere$() or $(item)Kugelblitz Chamber$() and you are carried sideways: $(thing)Frame Drag$().

Light climbing out of gravity loses energy. Over a height H the fraction lost is $(thing)gH/c²$() - about 2.5×10⁻¹⁵ up a 22.5-metre tower. In 1959 Pound and Rebka measured it with the gamma ray of iron-57, whose line is so sharp that even this shows.

The $(item)Pound-Rebka Tower$() is built 1 to 8 storeys tall, 7.5 m each. A $(item)Cobalt-57 Source$() sits on a Doppler drive at the foot, the absorber at the top. Move the source up at exactly $(thing)v = gH/c$() - under a micrometre a second - and the climb is cancelled.

Counting decides how sure you are: the line is 190 µm/s wide, and N gamma rays find its centre to 190/√N. Count until the shift stands five times above that error, and set v within two of it. Keep the tower at the air's temperature: each kelvin between source and absorber shifts the line by 0.66 µm/s - as much as the whole effect.

Two black holes spiralling together shake spacetime: a wave passes, stretching space one way and squeezing it the other, by a strain h of 10⁻²¹ when it reaches us. The $(item)Laser Interferometer$() is an L of two long arms with a $(item)Test Mass$() at each end: a laser split between the arms comes back to interfere, and a wave changes the pattern.

Four noises hide the wave. $(thing)Shot noise$(), the graininess of light, falls as the laser power P and the arms' finesse F rise - but $(thing)radiation pressure$(), the photons' kicks on the mirrors, grows with them. Both depend only on F√P; where they are equal is the standard quantum limit.

$(thing)Seismic noise$() falls tenfold with each isolation stage - more stages, slower to lock. Machines running nearby shake the ground; below sea level it is quieter, as at KAGRA. $(thing)Thermal noise$() in the mirrors falls as √T: cool them with your coolant.

A black hole merger, h = 10⁻²¹, needs a signal-to-noise of 8. A neutron star merger is five times fainter: only cold mirrors will do. Its record points a telescope at the $(thing)kilonova$() - where gold and platinum were made - and every detection gives a great deal of Insight. The chirp's parameters are read off by Bayesian inference: the Analyzer takes black hole records as evidence.

In 1975 Colella, Overhauser and Werner split single neutrons with a perfect silicon crystal and joined them again - and tilted the whole thing. One path ran a few centimetres higher than the other; gravity slowed the neutron on it; the two waves came back out of step. Gravity, acting on a quantum wave: $(thing)Δφ = 2πm²gλA·sin α/h²$().

Grow a $(item)Silicon Boule$() (fused silica and coal in the Crystal Growth Furnace), study it for its Laue Pattern, and cut two into a $(item)Perfect Crystal Interferometer$() - three blades still joined at the base, their lattices aligned to a fraction of an atom.

The $(item)Neutron Interferometer$() runs on a radium-beryllium source. Choose the wavelength and tilt it until gravity has turned the phase at least 30 radians and lands it on a bright fringe; count until the phase is known to 0.1 rad. Each record is a great deal of Insight.

Sound in a fluid flowing faster than sound cannot make headway upstream. Where the flow crosses its own speed of sound there is a horizon for sound - and the mathematics of sound near it is the mathematics of light near a black hole. Hawking radiation included.

The $(item)Analog Black Hole$() makes the flow out of $(fluid)Bose-Einstein Condensate$(): it streams toward a laser step, subsonic, and falls over it, thinned and fast - supersonic. Set the density (sound speed grows as its square root), the flow and the step depth so that both hold.

At the horizon phonon pairs appear, one carried off downstream, its partner escaping up: a glow at $(thing)T_H = ħκ/2πk_B$(), a few nanokelvin. The condensate itself must be colder than that to see it, and the correlations summed over many shots. Nothing but Bose-Einstein Condensate is cold enough as the coolant.

Two experiments have put quantum theory and gravity into one equation: gravity bending a neutron's phase, and a horizon glowing with quantum pairs. Both are $(thing)semiclassical$(): the quantum world on a smooth, classical spacetime.

Beyond them, spacetime itself must be quantum. One way to compute it is to sum over every way of building spacetime out of simple pieces - at random. With Semiclassical Gravity, the Monte Carlo Engine runs these $(thing)causal dynamical triangulations$(): four records of each experiment and two Metric Tensors make a $(item)Spin Foam Lattice$().
From here the road leads on to quantum gravity itself, and to the strings and singularities of the Codex's far end.
Clocks deep in a gravity well run slow: by $(thing)1/√(1 − r_s/r)$() at a distance r from a mass with Schwarzschild radius r_s.

The $(item)Time Dilation Chamber$() holds samples round a dense core. Set its mass and how close they sit: at three times dilation it grows Time-Dilated Samples in bulk; radium ages into polonium; at five, liquid spacetime is strained into $(fluid)Strained Spacetime$(). Too close and they fall through the horizon. Each storey (1 to 7) holds more.

A spinning mass drags spacetime round with it: a gyroscope near the Earth turns by $(thing)Ω = 2GJ/(c²r³)$(). A $(item)Precision Gyroscope$() carried in the off hand holds you steady: no Frame Drag, no Tidal Strain.

Tides are the difference between the pull on your two ends: $(thing)2GML/r³$(). Near a small black hole they pull you into spaghetti. Tidal shear crystals, a gyroscope and a micro-singularity knot spacetime into a $(item)Lense-Thirring Vortex Core$().

A falling body follows a $(thing)geodesic$(): the straightest path through curved spacetime. The $(item)Geodesic Compass$() points along one. A mass squeezed inside $(thing)r_s = 2GM/c²$() lets no light out.
Light follows geodesics too, and is bent by $(thing)α = 4GM/(c²b)$() - 1.75″ at the Sun's edge. A mass exactly in front of a star turns it into an Einstein ring.

The $(item)Lensing Concentrator$() aims at a star through a lens mass and turns the focused light into power - at night, under open sky. The magnification $(thing)A = (u² + 2)/(u√(u² + 4))$() grows without limit as the alignment u → 0, but the aim jitters by 0.3 milliarcseconds: choose a massive, near lens so the Einstein radius is big. Above A = 20 it grows an $(item)Einstein Ring Lens$().

Two compact stars spiral in as gravitational waves carry off their orbit; how fast the pitch rises depends only on the $(thing)chirp mass$() (m₁m₂)^(3/5)/(m₁ + m₂)^(1/5). The Binary of the Accretion Frontier drops Chirp Signal Records and Merger Remnants.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the The Binary.

The Laser Interferometer, listening to a chirp with a strain sensor, can hear a $(item)Gravitational Wave Echo$() - repeats after the ringdown, if a horizon is not quite a horizon. Played in the Frontier, an echo summons The Binary just as a Binary Black Hole Merger record does.

Alcubierre found a solution of general relativity that moves a bubble of flat space at any speed: space contracts ahead of it and expands behind. Its wall must be made of $(thing)negative energy$() - from $(item)Negative Energy Lattices$() of Casimir plates.

The $(item)Warp Field Forge$() shapes the bubble. Set its speed, radius and wall sharpness: the negative energy needed grows as v²R²σ, the shear across the wall as vσ (above 5 it tears a passenger apart), and a wall too thick for its bubble (Rσ < 10) leaks. A $(item)Warp Bubble Core$() must be superluminal, with under one solar mass of negative energy.
Use a Warp Bubble Core to anchor where you stand: it becomes an $(item)Anchored Warp Bubble$(). Use that, anywhere, to return there - once. Recipes only take the plain core.

Maldacena and Susskind: two entangled particles are joined by a wormhole too small to cross. The $(item)ER=EPR Weaver$() makes pairs and sends their halves to two mouths. Fidelity falls with the distance and with the weaver's own heat - and every pair heats it. Cold, and close, it weaves an $(item)ER Bridge Thread$().

AdS/CFT: gravity inside a space is a quantum field theory on its boundary. The Holographic Encoder turns a holographic matrix, an island and quantum spacetime condensate into a $(item)Holographic Screen$(), and a screen and Hall bars into a $(item)Boundary CFT Chip$(). For gravity in three dimensions, the boundary theory's central charge is exactly 3L/2G.

A black hole of mass M glows at $(thing)T = ħc³/(8πGMk)$(), radiates power ∝ 1/M², and evaporates in a time ∝ M³. A stellar hole is colder than the sky; one of a billion kilograms, hotter than any star.

The $(item)Micro Black Hole Evaporator$() holds one (a Kugelblitz Seed in a slot) and feeds it dust exactly as fast as it radiates. Feed it less and it shrinks, heats, runs away and explodes; more, and it swells. Below 6×10⁸ kg its gamma rays are too much for the lead. It gives great power and $(fluid)Hawking Radiation$(); above 10¹³ K, $(item)Hawking Quanta$() too.

A black hole has entropy $(thing)S = Ac³/(4Għ)$() - its area in Planck units over four - the most any region can hold: the $(item)Bekenstein Crystal$(). It evaporates; if what comes out is purely thermal, what fell in is gone, and quantum mechanics forbids that.

The $(item)Page Curve Analyzer$() follows Hawking quanta through an evaporation. Firewalls and soft hair are two answers. The third: the radiation's entropy rises, then after the $(thing)Page time$() - when half the hole's entropy is gone, at M/√2 - falls back to zero. A $(item)Page Curve Record$() carried in the off hand keeps your hotbar in order (no Information Loss). With an ER bridge, it finds the $(item)Island$() that makes the curve turn.

Loop quantum gravity quantises space: areas come in steps of $(thing)8πγℓₚ²√(j(j+1))$(). The $(item)Spin Network Loom$() weaves Planck Shards into $(item)Planck Area Tiles$(), tiles into $(item)Spin Network Nodes$(), and nodes with liquid spacetime into $(fluid)Quantum Spacetime Condensate$().

Causal set theory scatters events at random and keeps only their order: the Monte Carlo Engine sprinkles a $(item)Causal Set Seed$(). Asymptotic safety follows gravity's coupling to a fixed point instead of infinity: a node and a seed together make a $(item)Fixed-Point Lattice$().
Empty space looks empty only if you are not accelerating. Accelerate at a, and the vacuum glows at $(thing)T = ħa/(2πck)$() - one kelvin needs 2.5×10²⁰ m/s².

The $(item)Unruh Accelerator$() is a storage ring: electrons of Lorentz factor γ bent by a field B feel a = γ²c²/r, with r = γmc/eB. Gently, it calibrates an $(item)Unruh Thermometer$() (1-10 K). Hard - above 5000 K - its bath turns superfluid helium into Hawking radiation. But the beam radiates as γ³B, and the cavities replace only 500 kW.

Day 58. The $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$() works up from $(item)Lorentz Transforms$() and the $(item)Minkowski Lattice$() to the $(item)Metric$() and $(item)Riemann Curvature Tensors$() and finally the $(item)Einstein Field Core$().

The order follows the physics. First flat $(thing)Minkowski$() spacetime, where the $(thing)Lorentz transform$() says how lengths and times change between moving observers. Then gravity: the $(thing)metric$() measures distance in curved spacetime, the $(thing)Riemann tensor$() measures the curvature, and Einstein's equations tie that curvature to matter.

Why it matters: wormhole throats need an $(item)Einstein Field Core$(), and Alcubierre coils need $(item)metric tensors$(). Kugelblitz chambers can merge black holes into $(item)Gravitational Wave Crystals$() - the ripple of two horizons becoming one, frozen solid.
Lengths shrink and clocks slow as you approach light speed. This crystal is always moving at 0.99c.$(br2)Made in $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$().
g_μν: the rule for measuring distance in curved spacetime.$(br2)Made in $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$().
Matter tells spacetime how to curve; spacetime tells matter how to move. Both halves, in one core.$(br2)Made in $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$().

Novikov's principle, plainly: if time travel is possible, the only histories allowed are ones that are already consistent. You cannot stop your own birth; something always intervenes.$(br2)Here it is enforced. Closed timelike curves now need a Novikov Crystal: a time loop is only allowed if it can never produce a paradox.

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Firing neutrino flux and a sterile neutrino at a supernova remnant in the Nucleosynthesis Chamber, I saw nuclei capturing neutrons faster than they could decay. Heavy elements formed in a single flash.

Made in $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Nucleosynthesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Flerovium Ingot, Hypernova Alloy Ingot, Nuclide Forge, Stellar Singularity, Theoretical Notes I.

When a star exhausts the hydrogen in its core it swells, and its outer layers expand and cool to a dull red. The Sun will do this in about five billion years. The envelope is enormous and tenuous, a thin, glowing fog that barely seems to weigh anything.
pages.title: Red Giant Envelope

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Running a stellar core in the Nucleosynthesis Chamber past hydrogen exhaustion, I watched its outer layers puff outward. Separating the swollen envelope from the core left me with this bloated fog.
Made in $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Evolution.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Magnetar Shard, Stellar Singularity, Supernova Remnant.
$(thing)Dyson Sphere$()$(br2)Close the swarm into a shell and capture a star's entire output.
pages.title: Dyson Sphere

$(thing)Nucleosynthesis$()$(br2)Every element heavier than helium was made in a star. Iron is where fusion stops; supernovae make the rest.
pages.title: Nucleosynthesis

The light left over when matter goes beyond stellar temperatures. It is a hot, glowing gas that carries the memory of every star that went into it. It moves like a slow, luminous fog. Its glow is the colour of a sky just after a star has set.
pages.title: Residual Starlight

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pushing a Stellar Core beyond its limits in the Transcendent Plasma Forge, with magnetar and pentaquark shards, the matter gave off a glowing gas. Residual starlight, the afterglow of transcendence.

Made in $(item)Transcendent Plasma Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Transcendence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Cosmic String Segment, Dark Energy, Dimensional Residue, Exotic Matter, Exotic Matter Crystal, Horizon Shard, Hypernova Alloy Ingot and more.

Iron forged in the core of a star, where fusion stops being profitable. Iron has the most tightly bound nucleus, so fusing it or splitting it costs energy. The ingot is dense and dull grey and carries a faint heat that seems to come from somewhere deep inside it.
pages.title: Stellar Iron Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Combining a white dwarf core with ordinary iron in stellar plasma, I drove fusion until it stopped. Iron was where nucleosynthesis ended, and the Chamber left me an ingot of star-forged metal.
Made in $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Nucleosynthesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dyson Shell Segment, Magnetar Shard, Stellar Singularity, Supernova Remnant.

The expanding shell of gas and the collapsed core left when a massive star's core can no longer support itself. The shockwave seeds space with heavy elements. This remnant is a dense nugget wrapped in a faint, glowing haze of debris.
pages.title: Supernova Remnant

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Neutron Star Forge I collapsed a stellar iron core under neutronium pressure and flooded it with neutrinos. The red giant envelope blew outward and left a small, heavy remnant.

Made in $(item)Neutron Star Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Nucleosynthesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Gold Ingot, Hypernova Alloy Ingot, Magnetar Shard, Quark Star Core, R-Process Cluster, Stellar Singularity, Theoretical Notes III and more.

In the forge, above stellar-core temperatures, properties like hardness and conductivity stop being fixed and start being chosen. This ingot is what a metal looks like when someone else chose them. It weighs exactly what the forge decided, and feels faintly as though it might change its mind.
pages.title: Transcendent Metal Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I fed the forge a hypernova alloy and things that are barely matter at all: an aleph-null shard, Russell's paradox, a cosmic processor. The processor set the rules, the paradox loosened the old ones, and the metal accepted whatever properties it was given.

Made in $(item)Transcendent Plasma Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Transcendence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Apeiron Ingot, Axiomatic Field Emitter, Omniscience Catalyst, Omnium Ingot, Pleroma Confluence.

Plasma above the temperature where matter has fixed properties. It is no longer any element; it is all of them and none. It glows every colour at once and has no fixed density. Instruments dipped into it return a different reading every time, all of them correct.
pages.title: Transcendent Plasma

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pushing hypernova alloy with an Aleph-Null Shard and a Russell Paradox Set into the Transcendent Plasma Forge, the plasma stopped having fixed properties. Stellar transcendence.

A coil of hypernova alloy wound around an aleph-null shard over a cosmic neutronium coil, superconducting at room temperature. It carries a current that never quite finishes counting itself. The windings seem to continue past the point where the coil should end.
pages.title: Transfinite Coil Block

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Above stellar-core temperatures even cosmic neutronium coils fail. I wound hypernova alloy around an aleph-null shard with a room-temperature superconductor and a cosmic processor, and the coil held.

A self-replicating machine that builds copies of itself from whatever material it finds. Send one to a star system and it builds more, which build more, until every star has one. Von Neumann proved such machines were possible. This one is small, neat and patient.
pages.title: Von Neumann Probe

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Nanite Assembler I gave a Dyson Swarm Satellite claytronic catoms and a Quantum Processor, so it could fabricate its own parts. It began printing a copy of itself before I had finished writing the entry.
Made in $(item)Nanite Assembler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Dyson Swarm.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Theoretical Notes I.

What remains when a modest star sheds its outer layers: a core of carbon and oxygen about the size of the Earth, held up against gravity only by electron degeneracy pressure. It is fiercely hot and absurdly heavy for its size, and will cool for longer than the universe has existed.
pages.title: White Dwarf Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)After the red giant phase, the Nucleosynthesis Chamber left a small, glowing ember behind. Electron degeneracy held it up, exactly as Chandrasekhar described, and it slowly radiated away its leftover heat.
Made in $(item)Tectonic Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Evolution.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Singularity, Stellar Iron Ingot, Stellar Singularity.

pages.text: Almost every atom heavier than helium in my body was cooked inside a star. This chamber runs that process on a workbench: a gas cloud falls in on itself, fusion lights, the star swells, and it dies. My notes on stellar evolution follow each stage.

Day 77. A star begins as a cloud. I harvest $(fluid)Nebular Gas$() with the Dark Matter Halo Collector and collapse it into a $(item)Protostar$() in the $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().

Gravity squeezes until the core reaches millions of degrees and hydrogen fuses. I ignite the protostar into a $(item)Stellar Core$(). When a real star runs low on hydrogen its outer layers balloon outward; mine swells into a $(item)Red Giant$(), and I keep its $(item)White Dwarf$() - the bare, glowing core left behind.

White dwarfs forge $(item)Stellar Iron$() - the end of fusion. Iron's nucleus is among the most tightly bound there is; fusing it costs energy instead of releasing it. Dyson shells are made of stellar iron.

A red giant crushed onto stellar iron goes supernova. Its remnant feeds the $(item)r-process$() - rapid neutron capture, nature's way of making gold and everything heavier - and it is needed for every quark star.
A collapsing knot of nebular gas, hot enough to glow but not yet to fuse.$(br2)Made in $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().
Iron from the core of a star - the end of fusion. Making anything heavier costs energy instead of releasing it.$(br2)Made in $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().
