A device that keeps its bearer's worldline intact inside a black or white hole. Without it, tidal forces and causal chaos are lethal within seconds. It is heavy and cool and hums faintly, like a gyroscope.
pages.title: Geodesic Anchor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Inside a black hole I nearly lost my worldline. Combining a Kerr metric shard, graviton crystal and chronon capacitor in a hyperlattice frame on the Extreme Assembly Table, I built an anchor to keep it.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.

At sufficiently high energy, the electromagnetic, weak and strong couplings run together and meet. Grand unified theories predict magnetic monopoles and proton decay as a consequence. The core is bright and calm, three forces resting in a single symmetry.
pages.title: Grand Unified Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Running the Standard Model's couplings upward with superpartners included, I saw them converge. In the Tesseract Assembler, a monopole and a quantum string held the high-energy state long enough to crystallise it.

Made in $(item)Tesseract Assembler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Grand Unification.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Eschaton Core, Standard Model Singularity, Theory of Everything, Transcendent Metal Ingot, Transcendent Plasma.

Gravitons are the hypothetical quanta of gravity, and this crystal holds them frozen in a lattice. It feels heavier than it is: the stored gravitons pull on my hand as well as on the floor. Near it, falling dust curves slightly toward the crystal before reaching the ground.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Graviton Wisp (the Bulk (Graviton Reef)).
pages.title: Graviton Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I cooled Virtual Gravitons from the quantum foam in Superfluid Helium inside the Graviton Condenser until they could not escape. Graviton Wisps carry them naturally, and I found more in vaults, monoliths and derelict stations.

Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Graviton Wisp.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Anomaly Vault, Bulk Monolith chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Brane Tether, Bulk Crystal, Bulk Stone, Compactification Lathe, Cosmic Processor, Cosmic String Lens, False Vacuum, Geodesic Anchor and more.

A web of straps and plates that takes the pull of a crushing field and spreads it through every bone at once, so no single joint bears it. Tidal forces kill by difference, not by strength; the harness erases the difference. Wearing it feels like being hugged by a planet.
pages.title: Graviton Harness

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A walk through a high-gravity field nearly broke both my ankles. I laid graviton crystals across neutronium plating and added an inertia damper to smooth the gradients, so that the field pulls on all of me equally and none of me in particular.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.
$(thing)Graviton Wisp$(). Lives in: Graviton Reef, The Bulk.$(br)Drops: Graviton Wisp Core, Graviton Crystal, Void Lattice Shard.
pages.title: Graviton Wisp

pages.text: All that is left of a universe that has reached maximum entropy: no stars, no gradients, nothing to drive any process at all. It is cold, perfectly even and perfectly still, a uniform grey with no texture to catch the light. Holding it feels like holding silence.
pages.title: Heat Death Remnant

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I let a Pocket Universe in the Universe Forge run to its end. Trillions of years compressed into a few minutes, and the bubble came out like this: inert, even, and oddly peaceful. Its stillness is what makes new universes possible.
Made in $(item)Universe Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Cosmogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Singularity, Boltzmann Brain, Inflaton Field, Universe Seed.

A two-dimensional membrane from M-theory, the eleven-dimensional framework in which strings are the edges of membranes. A brane like this could host an entire universe on its surface, with gravity alone leaking into the Bulk. It is a sheet of light that ripples when I breathe on it.
pages.title: M-Brane

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wove a D-Brane Sheet with a G2 Manifold and a String Coupling Crystal on the String Resonance Loom, turning the coupling up until the strings fused into a membrane. Eleven dimensions, counted twice to make sure.

Made in $(item)String Resonance Loom$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): M-Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Dimensional Singularity, Exotic Matter Crystal, Inflaton Field, M-Theory Core, Multiverse Shard, Penteract Display, Theoretical Notes II and more.

Five superstring theories turned out to be limits of one eleven-dimensional theory, whose fundamental objects include membranes as well as strings. Witten called it M-theory, and nobody knows what the M stands for. The core vibrates in more directions than seem possible.
pages.title: M-Theory Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Wrapping an M-brane on a G2 manifold and a compactified circle in the Compactification Lathe, I found all five string theories as limits of one. Exotic matter kept the eleventh dimension open.
Made in $(item)Compactification Lathe$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): M-Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Singularity, Theory of Everything.

A one-dimensional vibrating string, the fundamental object of string theory. Its mode of vibration decides what it is: one note an electron, another a photon, another a graviton. In the hand it is a thread of light that hums, changing its tune slightly with my pulse.
pages.title: Quantum String

Two branches of physics are about time itself: $(thing)Origin$(), how a universe begins, and $(thing)Finality$(), how it ends. Origin starts with $(thing)The Hot Big Bang$(): run the expansion backwards and everything was once hotter and denser than the core of a star.

The $(thing)Friedmann equation$() says how fast space expands: H² = 8πGρ/3 − kc²/a² + Λc²/3. Matter and radiation slow it, curvature bends it, and the vacuum energy Λ - dark energy - takes over in the end. Exactly flat space has the critical density, about five protons per cubic metre.

$(li)$(thing)Primordial Nucleosynthesis$(): for three minutes the universe fused hydrogen into helium. $(item)Primordial Nucleosynthesis Ash$() comes from quark-gluon plasma (or reheating plasma) in the $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().$(li)$(thing)Cosmic Inflation$() and $(thing)Reheating$(): see the next chapter.$(li)$(thing)Leptogenesis$(), $(thing)Vacuum Stability$(), $(thing)Creation from Nothing$() and $(thing)Conformal Cyclic Cosmology$() come after.

Where Finality ends, Origin begins. Roger Penrose noticed that at the end of a heat death only massless particles remain - and light has no clock: it cannot tell an infinitely large, cold universe from a tiny, hot one. Rescale the dead universe's infinite future and it is the Big Bang of the next $(thing)aeon$().

In the $(item)Inflation Chamber$(): $(item)Heat Death Embers$(), a $(item)De Sitter Horizon Shard$() and $(fluid)Dark Era Haze$() make an $(item)Aeon Boundary Shard$(); the Shard with a $(item)No-Boundary Seed$() and inflaton condensate makes two $(item)Universe Seeds$(). A $(item)Bounce Core$() from a Big Crunch makes one too.

Origin also feeds what came before it: the $(item)Universe Forge$() can make a $(item)Pocket Universe$() from first principles - a seed, a true-vacuum bubble, the asymmetry, the ash and the plasma - and the Eye of the Horizon's and the Omnilex's universes now want Primordial Ash and a No-Boundary Seed.

The Big Bang alone cannot explain why opposite sides of the sky have the same temperature to one part in 100,000: they were never in contact. $(thing)Inflation$() does: before the hot Big Bang, a scalar field - the inflaton - sat high on its potential and made space grow exponentially, sixty e-folds in 10⁻³² s.

Build the $(item)Inflation Chamber$(). It condenses the $(fluid)Inflaton Field$() and $(fluid)False Vacuum$() into $(item)Inflaton Condensate$(). In its Operation console keep the slow-roll ε = 2/φ² below 1 and N = (φ₀² − 2)/4 above 50 - but start the field too high and inflation turns $(thing)eternal$(): quantum jumps outrun the roll, and the bubble never ends (in our universe, other bubbles still may).

$(thing)Reheating$(): at the bottom of its potential the inflaton oscillates and decays. The chamber turns Condensate and a little quark-gluon plasma into $(fluid)Reheating Plasma$() - every particle there is, at 10⁹ GeV and more. That plasma is the raw stuff of every other Origin material.

Reheating makes matter and antimatter in equal amounts, and they should have annihilated into light. For every billion photons there is one baryon left over. Andrei Sakharov's conditions say what it takes: baryon number violation, C and CP violation, and a moment out of equilibrium.

$(thing)Leptogenesis$() meets all three: heavy right-handed neutrinos decay a little more often into leptons than antileptons, and sphaleron transitions of the electroweak vacuum convert that excess into baryons. In a $(item)Quark-Gluon Collider$(), antimatter and sterile neutrinos in $(fluid)Reheating Plasma$() leave a $(item)Baryon Asymmetry Crystal$(). With the antimatter of the Antiverse, crystals become a $(item)Baryogenesis Seed$() in the $(item)Mirror Foundry$().

$(thing)Vacuum Stability$(): a universe can fail before it starts. A vacuum energy larger by a factor of a hundred and no galaxy forms; the measured one is 10¹²⁰ times smaller than quantum theory's natural guess - the $(thing)cosmological constant problem$(). And the Higgs coupling runs downwards with energy until, near 10¹⁰ GeV, a deeper vacuum opens: ours is $(thing)metastable$(). The $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$() maps it into a $(item)Metastable Vacuum Lattice$().

$(thing)Creation from Nothing$(): quantise a whole closed universe and its wave function obeys the Wheeler-DeWitt equation. Vilenkin's universe tunnels through a barrier from no space at all; Hartle and Hawking's has no boundary - near the start time turns into space, and asking what came before is like asking what is south of the South Pole.
The $(item)Inflation Chamber$() folds spin foam, inflaton condensate and a metastable vacuum into a $(item)No-Boundary Seed$().

Every journey to another dimension - by Brane Shifter, rift, wormhole, falling through the void or the hyperobject - now takes a moment: the travel animation builds up on screen for under two seconds, and only then do you jump. The loading screen of each world is its own.

Wherever you arrive, you arrive standing: never inside blocks, never in mid-air, never on top of a world's ceiling (the Quantum Foam's Relativity Breakdown, the build limit), never in a fluid or on something that burns. The ground nearby is searched for two free blocks over solid ground - open sky first, otherwise the spot nearest the height you left from.
Only when there is nowhere at all is a small platform built for you, with the room above it cleared. Laws of the place still apply: carry its attunement item.

The $(thing)Planetary Interior$() is the exception to open sky: it has a bedrock roof, so you arrive under it, on dry rock as near y 100 as the cave allows, with a Mantle Breach beside you for the way back.

Every strange dimension has the item that lets you survive it. Each one was made from what you brought back from the places before it - so it carries their protection too.$(br2)Carry an attunement item and every dimension whose own item comes $(l)earlier$() in this list cannot touch you at all: no debuffs, no strange gravity, no rules.
$(li)$(item)Form of the Self$(): the Platonic Realm$(li)$(item)Penning Harness$(): the Antiverse$(li)$(item)Coherence Stabiliser$(): the Quantum Foam$(li)$(item)Brane Tether$(): the Bulk

In its own dimension, each item works as it always has.

Brane cosmology says our universe is a membrane adrift in a higher-dimensional $(thing)Bulk$(). The $(item)Brane Shifter$() slips me sideways into it, and back. It requires the Brane Cosmology research.

First crossing. The Bulk is an endless void of floating islands under the shadow of a vast hypercube - a four-dimensional cube, of which I only ever see a 3D shadow. Monoliths hide vaults of exotic materials, and $(item)Void Lattice Ore$() is common here.
Physics aside: in brane-world models only gravity leaks out into the Bulk, which might be why it is so much weaker than the other forces. Standing out here, I believe it.
Slip sideways out of this brane and into the Bulk.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.

Ruins and impossible structures keep their treasure in $(item)Containment Caches$(), not chests. Each dimension seals its own kind: the Bulk Cache borrows room from a fifth dimension, the Euclid Reliquary of the Platonic Realm closes on an exact right angle, the Hilbert Locker is always full and always has room for one more.
A cache works like a chest of 27 slots; hoppers and pipes can reach it. Breaking it spills its contents and drops the cache itself. You can make an ordinary $(item)Containment Cache$() of your own.
Sunday. Even a lab deserves some style. Put a block of any high-tech material in a $(item)Stonecutter$() for plating, tiles, bricks and pillars - and back again, so nothing is wasted.

Surround a material block with glowstone dust for four $(item)Lamps$(). Most bricks and tiles also come as stairs, slabs and walls.$(br2)Chronosteel, Spacetime Alloy, Cosmic Neutronium, Dilithium and Void Lattice each have a storage block too - which is how I keep the hoard tidy.
Made in a crafting grid.
Nether expedition, day 2. $(item)Dilithium$() grows down here. Its lattice is porous to antimatter, which makes it the only practical regulator for an annihilation reactor.

Field notes: annihilation turns all the rest mass of matter and antimatter into energy - E = mc², the full amount, against under 1% for fusion. The hard part has always been holding antimatter without it touching anything. A crystal it can pass through gently is exactly what such a reactor needs.
Porous to antimatter. It regulates annihilation reactions.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Dilithium Ore in the Nether.
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Dilithium Crystal$(): Annihilation Core, Block of Dilithium, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Dilithium Crystal, Magnetar Shard and more
Every other place has its own law, and the law is not kind to visitors. Carry the right $(thing)attunement$() anywhere in your inventory and you will live - with a reminder of where you are.

$(li)$(item)Brane Tether$(), the Bulk: without it, $(thing)Dimensional Bleed$(); with it, half gravity and twice the knockback.$(li)$(item)Primordial Charter$(), Hyperdimensional Reality: without it a hostile new law every few seconds; with it, a new law (good or bad) every minute and a half.

$(li)$(item)Form of the Self$(), the Platonic Realm: without it, $(thing)Imperfection$(); with it, only a $(thing)sword$() can dig - pickaxes barely scratch the ideal.$(li)$(item)Coherence Stabiliser$(), the Quantum Foam: without it, constant $(thing)Decoherence$(); with it, you still blink a few blocks now and then.

$(li)$(item)Well-Ordering Charm$(), the Transfinite Hierarchy: without it, $(thing)Infinite Regress$() deepens every ten seconds; with it, Regress I and hunger.$(li)$(item)Geodesic Anchor$(), both holes: without it, death in two seconds. In the white hole gravity points $(thing)up$() - sneak to fall.$(li)$(item)Identity Kernel$(), the Transcendental: without it, $(thing)Dissolution$().
Ties your mass to our brane. Carry it in the Bulk - or in any field of extra dimensions.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.
Your own ideal form, cut in crystal. Carry it in the Platonic Realm.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.
Keeps your wavefunction in one piece. Carry it in the Quantum Foam - or in an altered vacuum.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.
Every descent ends somewhere. Carry it in the Transfinite Hierarchy.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.
A copy of the laws as they were first written. Carry it in Hyperdimensional Reality.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.
Keeps your worldline your own. Without one, the inside of a black or white hole kills you in two seconds.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.

None of these places has a bottom you can die on. Fall off the floor of one and you fall into another:$(li)off the $(thing)Bulk$(): back onto our own brane$(li)through the $(thing)Platonic Realm$(): into the Transfinite Hierarchy$(li)below the $(thing)Transfinite$(): into the Quantum Foam

$(li)through a $(thing)black hole$()'s singularity: out of its white hole$(li)past the top of a $(thing)white hole$(): home$(li)between the branches of $(thing)Hyperdimensional Reality$(): into the Bulk$(li)out of the $(thing)Transcendental$(): into Hyperdimensional Reality$(br2)Carry the right attunement for wherever you land.

One world is different. The $(thing)Planetary Interior$() has a true floor - the $(item)Inner Core Boundary$(), solid iron that nothing yet cuts - and a roof of bedrock. There is nothing to fall through: you leave the way you came, by a $(item)Mantle Breach$().

The floor of the Planetary Interior: the edge of the solid inner core, 5,150 km down. Iron here is crystallised under 330 GPa and about 5,400 C - as hot as the Sun's surface, yet solid because the pressure will not let it melt.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Planetary Interior.

A hole bored through bedrock by the Core Drill. Step into it and you fall to the Planetary Interior; on arrival a second breach opens in the floor beside you, and stepping into that one brings you back up.
Stand inside a structure built in more dimensions than three and your eyes stop agreeing with your feet. The deeper you go, the more space folds to match the object you are in:

$(li)$(thing)Tesseracts$() and Bulk monoliths: nested cubes turning inside one another$(li)$(thing)Fractals$(): the view contains itself, again and again$(li)$(thing)Platonic solids$(): mirrored through their symmetry$(li)$(thing)Hilbert's Hotel$() and the Ordinal Spire: an endless corridor$(li)$(thing)Calabi-Yau knots$() and Hopf rings: space wound round itself

$(li)$(thing)Graviton reefs$(): light bent into an Einstein ring$(li)$(thing)Anomaly vaults$(): the picture tears$(li)the heart of the $(thing)Transcendental$(): all of it at once.$(br2)It is harmless, and fades as you walk out. It can be switched off in the client config (structureDistortion).

The $(thing)Planetary Interior$() needs no attunement item - its laws are only the planet's own, and they press harder the deeper you go. You reach it with the $(item)Core Drill$() (research $(thing)Plate Tectonics$()), cutting the Overworld's bedrock floor; you leave by any $(item)Mantle Breach$() - one opens beside you wherever you arrive.

$(li)$(thing)Lithostatic Pressure$(): below y 100, one level for every 25 blocks deeper; you move and mine slower.$(li)$(thing)Tremors$() in the Crustal Caverns: a few seconds of Seismic Vertigo.$(li)$(thing)Mantle plumes$() in the Mantle Convection Zone throw you upwards.$(li)$(thing)Geomagnetic storms$() in the Geodynamo Core leave you Magnetized: compasses spin.

$(li)The $(thing)Natural Reactor$() is radioactive - its background is far above the Overworld's, and Fission Fragment seams are hot. Carry a Geiger Counter.$(li)$(fluid)Basaltic Magma$(), the Interior's sea, does 10 damage a hit and Fire Resistance does not help. $(fluid)Deep Brine$() sets you alight like lava.
The floor is the $(item)Inner Core Boundary$(): solid iron under 330 GPa, which no tool yet made can break. The roof is bedrock, which the Core Drill cuts again from below.

Others have been down here before. In the Crustal Caverns stand $(thing)Deep Boreholes$(): drill holes cased in steel and abandoned two dozen blocks down, a broken drill floor at the top and a cache at the bottom of the hole.

In the Natural Reactor, lead-walled $(thing)Oklo Reactor Ruins$() are dug round the reactor seam itself - fission fragments and uraninite in the floor. Bring a Geiger Counter and radiation-plated armour; their caches hold fuel, graphite and control rods.

A plinth that waits for a conclusion. When the right answer is placed on it, the surrounding proof settles into consistency and the room grows quiet. A wrong answer sits there and does nothing at all.
pages.title: Answer Pedestal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)At the heart of each proof chamber stood this pedestal. I understood it once I realised the whole chamber was a theorem waiting for its final line.
$(item)Anticarbon Ore$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
pages.title: Anticarbon Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).
$(item)Anti-Gold Ore$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
pages.title: Anti-Gold Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).
$(item)Antihydrogen Ice$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
pages.title: Antihydrogen Ice

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).
$(item)Anti-Iron Ore$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
pages.title: Anti-Iron Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).
$(item)Antisilicon Ore$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
pages.title: Antisilicon Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).

Soil of the Antiverse, made of antiprotons, antineutrons and positrons. It is stable only because everything around it is antimatter too; brought into contact with ordinary matter, a gram of it would release about 180 TJ.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Antiverse.
pages.title: Antisoil

pages.text: Planks cut from the Arbor, pale and fine-grained, with faint branching lines running along their length. The wood smells of rain and seems to grow warmer when people walk across it. Nails go in easily and never split it.
pages.title: Arbor Planks

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I split Arbor heartwood into planks for building. The grain branched instead of running straight, and every board I cut was slightly different.
$(thing)Used in$(): Arbor Planks Slab, Arbor Planks Stairs.

A lamp that shines when its axiom is in force. Its light is steady and colourless, and when the axiom is withdrawn it simply goes dark. Rows of them read like a truth table drawn in light. Watching them, I finally understood how much of mathematics is a matter of choice.
pages.title: Axiom Lamp

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)These lit and darkened as I flipped axiom toggles inside the proof. They showed me which postulates I had accepted, and which I had not.

A switch that adopts or rejects an axiom. Flip it and the local truths rearrange; some things become provable, others not. It moves with a satisfying click, like choosing between Euclidean and hyperbolic geometry.
pages.title: Axiom Toggle

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Inside the proof I found switches wired to the axiom lamps. Each one admitted or denied a single postulate. Solving the room meant choosing a consistent set.

Two bodies coiled round each other in a tightening spiral, shedding gravitational waves. Each turn is faster than the last, until the chirp ends in a merger.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Chirp Signal Record, Merger Remnant.
pages.title: The Binary

pages.text: A thread pulled from a brane, the membrane on which strings end. It is strong beyond any material, because its tension is a property of spacetime rather than chemistry. It hums faintly and pulls back toward the surface it came from.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Brane Strider (the Bulk (Moduli Wastes, Graviton Reef)).
pages.title: Brane Tension Fiber

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Brane Striders walk on membranes in the Bulk, and when they fell they left these threads behind. I found more in derelict stations, still taut as if attached to something invisible.
Made in $(item)String Resonance Loom$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Brane Strider.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): D-Brane Sheet.
Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 4 and 70. Gives Bridgmanite when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Bridgmanite Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).
Bigger on the inside: it borrows a little room from a fifth dimension. In brane cosmology our whole universe floats in such a bulk.
pages.title: Bulk Cache

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Transcendent Cache.

A translucent crystal from the Bulk whose facets seem to point in directions I cannot quite name. Light passing through comes out a little out of phase with itself, as if it had taken a short detour through another axis.
pages.title: Bulk Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I found these growing in the Bulk where the extra dimensions are most tightly curled. Looking through one, I saw my own hand from an angle I should not have been able to see it from.

Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Brane Tension Fiber, Bulk Cache, Graviton Wisp Core, Silicon Life Spore, String Coupling Crystal.

The bedrock of the higher-dimensional Bulk: a grey stone that seems to have more surfaces than it shows. Edges blur where the extra dimensions curl back in. It is cool and unremarkable to the touch, which is somehow worse.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Bulk (Moduli Wastes, Graviton Reef).
pages.title: Bulk Stone

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Everything in the Bulk rests on this stone, and I first broke some off to see if the extra dimensions would follow it home. They did, a little - enough to make it useful in crafting.

Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dilaton Crystal, Hyperdimensional Pearl, Kaluza-Klein Shard, Moduli Crystal, Void Lattice Shard.

Rather than order, this ore measures size. Its crystals pair up perfectly with one another, unless they come from a larger infinity, in which case some are always left over. It is heavier than it looks, and denser in every sense.
pages.title: Cardinal Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Next to ordinal veins I found a second kind of ore that refused to be sorted, only compared. Diagonal arguments on the samples always left a remainder, the clear mark of a larger cardinal.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Transfinite Hierarchy (mine it for its drop).
The shell of a chamber where time runs at another rate. Even on Earth, a clock a kilometre higher gains about one part in 10¹³.
pages.title: Time Dilation Chamber Casing

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.
Tiles laid in no repeating order, each pattern drawn at random. Any stretch that looks designed is a coincidence the dice were always going to throw.
pages.title: Chance Tiles

pages.text: Cherenkov quartz cut into small bricks, each one glowing softly blue along its edges. A wall of them looks like a shallow pool at night. They are smooth and slightly cool to the touch. Every joint carries its own thin line of blue light, so the whole wall seems sketched in glow.
pages.title: Cherenkov Bricks

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I cut Cherenkov quartz into bricks to make glowing walls with more texture than plain blocks. The light catches along every seam.
$(thing)Used in$(): Cherenkov Bricks Slab, Cherenkov Bricks Stairs, Cherenkov Bricks Wall.

A column of Cherenkov quartz that glows along its length with an even blue. Placed at a doorway it reads like a beam of light holding up the lintel. It is cool and faintly humming. Rows of them along a corridor make it feel like walking beneath a reactor pool.
pages.title: Cherenkov Pillar

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pillars of Cherenkov quartz gave the labs a sense of structure and a little light. They were easy to cut and look better than they have any right to.
A stony meteorite: rock that has not melted since the planets formed. Found in craters out in open country.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in Meteorite Crater structures in the Overworld.
pages.title: Chondrite

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

A chronosteel panel painted with warning stripes, used to mark doorways, machine edges and anything I do not want to walk into. The stripes look very slightly out of step with each other. Yellow and black on dull metal - a language every lab in every universe seems to share.
pages.title: Chronosteel Hazard Panel

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)After walking into a running time field once, I started marking hazards. Chronosteel panels with stripes were the clearest way to say keep out.

A column of chronosteel, banded and fluted, that carries a load without complaint. It reflects light in a slightly delayed blur and gives a doorway the feel of an engine room. Its bands are spaced at regular intervals, like the ticks on a clock face.
pages.title: Chronosteel Pillar

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Chronosteel pillars were stronger than I needed and looked better than stone. I used them to frame machine halls. They also make a reliable time reference.

Chronosteel rolled into plates and fixed to a block face. Its sheen is cool and slightly blurred, as if the surface had moved a moment before it was seen. It gives a wall a clean, mechanical look. Rivets mark each corner, set in perfectly even rows.
pages.title: Chronosteel Plating

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I had spare chronosteel, so I plated walls with it. The blurred reflections are a side effect of the metal's own clock and I have grown fond of them.
$(thing)Used in$(): Chronosteel Plating Slab, Chronosteel Plating Stairs.

A chronosteel grille that lets air pass between rooms. The slats are angled to keep light out and air moving, and a faint draught always seems to be flowing through it, even when the room is still. The slats never collect dust, though I have never cleaned them.
pages.title: Chronosteel Vent

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Labs full of machines get stuffy. Chronosteel vents were the obvious fix, and they look the part. The slats were angled by trial and error until the hum of the machines dropped.
Casing for a climate engine. Earth's climate balances about 340 W/m² of incoming sunlight against heat radiated back to space.
pages.title: Climate Engine Casing

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.

A pane of metamaterial that bends light around itself, so the glass is nearly invisible from any angle. Only the edges betray it, as a faint distortion in the room. Walking past it, the room behind seems to shift a little too smoothly, like a painted backdrop.
pages.title: Metamaterial Cloaking Glass

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Metamaterials can steer light around an object. I built them into glass to see if I could make a window that vanished, and it nearly did.

A panel of computronium with fine glowing traces running across its face, like a circuit board that is thinking. It is warm and faintly busy to the touch. The traces brighten when someone stands close, then fade once they walk away, as though the panel had finished noticing them.
pages.title: Computronium Panel

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Computronium walls were too warm as solid blocks. Thin panels gave me the look of a working computer without heating the room.

Computronium cut into tiles, each one lit by faint, shifting traces. A floor of them flickers softly, as if computing something about whoever walks across it. Patterns chase each other across the joints between tiles, too fast to follow, and settle into stillness when the room empties.
pages.title: Computronium Tiles

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I tiled a floor with computronium offcuts. It flickers gently underfoot, and I am almost sure it is only decorative. It has never miscounted anything.
$(thing)Used in$(): Computronium Tiles Slab, Computronium Tiles Stairs.
A great curved array of mirrors that gathers light from a field of heliostats onto one focus. The Odeillo furnace reaches about 3,500 °C this way.
pages.title: Concentrator Mirror

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Meteoritics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Solar Furnace.
Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 1 and 48. Gives Magnetite when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Core Magnetite Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

Cosmic neutronium rolled into plating, dark as space with faint pinpricks of light. A wall of it looks like a window onto the night sky that happens to be load-bearing. Running a hand over it feels like touching cold glass, and the lights inside never quite stay still.
pages.title: Cosmic Neutronium Plating

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Plating walls with cosmic neutronium was extravagant, but the effect was worth it. It is the closest thing to a sky I have indoors.

Cosmic neutronium cut into dark tiles that seem to have tiny points of light deep inside them, like stars seen through a deep well. The floor they make feels impossibly solid. The tiny lights drift very slowly if I watch them long enough, like stars wheeling over a night.
pages.title: Cosmic Neutronium Tiles

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I had offcuts of cosmic neutronium and laid them as tiles. The faint lights inside them were a surprise, and I left them as they were.
$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Neutronium Tiles Slab, Cosmic Neutronium Tiles Stairs.
The iron return path of a cyclotron magnet. It carries the flux back from pole to pole, so the field across the gap stays strong and even.
pages.title: Cyclotron Yoke

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.
Found in the Overworld, between Y -64 and 0. Gives Raw Pitchblende when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Deepslate Pitchblende Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Overworld's deepslate (mine it for its drop).

End stone cracked around knots of matter so compressed that its electrons are packed into the lowest states quantum mechanics permits. Pauli exclusion holds it up, not chemistry. The block is far heavier than it looks, and the pick rings against it.
pages.title: Degenerate Matter Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the End, where dead stars seem to have been scattered, a pickaxe bounced off a seam of end stone that was much too heavy. Under the crust was matter pressed into degeneracy, like a fragment of a white dwarf.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the End (mine it for its drop).
The tall frame over a well that carries the crown block and the whole string of pipe. The word comes from Derrick, a seventeenth-century Tyburn hangman.
pages.title: Derrick Frame

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Deep Borehole Surface chests.

In string theory, the dilaton is a field whose value sets the string coupling: how readily strings split and join. This crystal froze one value of it. Hold it up to the light and everything behind it looks slightly more or less substantial.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Dilaton Ore in the Bulk (Graviton Reef).
pages.title: Dilaton Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I found these growing on the Graviton Reefs of the Bulk and inside the Calabi-Yau Knot. Their facets responded to string interactions, and I realised they had frozen the dilaton field in place.

Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Dilaton Ore$(), in veins through the Bulk.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Singularity, String Coupling Crystal.

Pale, oddly variable mineral whose hardness seems to drift as I handle it. The dilaton is the scalar field in string theory that sets the coupling strength of strings; here it is pinned into crystal, and wherever it sits the rules of interaction loosen or tighten slightly.
pages.title: Dilaton Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the bulk stone a seam kept changing how hard my tools struck it. Plotting the variance against depth, I realised the local string coupling was shifting, a frozen dilaton field showing through the rock.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Bulk (mine it for its drop).

Scorched nuggets blown out of a white hole. They are rich in elements that should not exist together, flung up from a region that admits no entry. The surfaces are glassy from the violence of their exit.
pages.title: Ejecta Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The ejecta rock is peppered with dense, blistered lumps. I first took them for meteorites until I traced their trajectories back to a point nothing can enter.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the white hole interior (mine it for its drop).
Creation from nothing, made a machine. It does not convert energy - it simply has it: it gives unlimited FE to every block beside it, and charges the items of every player within 16 blocks.
pages.title: Ex Nihilo Engine

pages.text: A tall brick chimney. The hot gas inside is lighter than the air outside, so the taller the stack, the harder it draws.
pages.title: Exhaust Stack

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.
Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 36 and 126. Gives Fission Fragment Mix when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Fission Fragment Seam

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

A pocket of space sitting in a higher-energy vacuum than its surroundings, metastable and patient. If it tunnels down to the true vacuum it will expand at nearly light speed and rewrite everything it touches. The surface ripples softly, waiting for an excuse.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Quantum Foam.
pages.title: False Vacuum Bubble

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Drifting through the quantum foam, I noticed bubbles whose interior energy did not match the vacuum outside. Coleman's false vacuum, right there. I have learned to give them a very wide berth.

Photons that fell toward a horizon and appear to have stopped. To any outside observer, their final moments are stretched forever, so the ore glows a deep, slow red that never fades. It is not hot, merely luminous and patient.
pages.title: Frozen Light Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Seen from far away, anything falling into a black hole freezes at the horizon. In infall rock I found veins of that frozen light, caught at the instant it crossed and preserved there indefinitely.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the black hole interior (mine it for its drop).
A precision turntable that sets sample and detector at exact angles. The detector swings twice as far as the crystal, keeping θ and 2θ in step.
pages.title: Goniometer

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.

The heart of a Graviton Wisp: a closed loop of string vibrating in the mode that makes a graviton. Even out of the Wisp, it pulls gently on everything nearby. It is light, but holding it gives a faint sensation of falling toward it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Graviton Wisp (the Bulk (Graviton Reef)).
pages.title: Graviton Wisp Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Graviton Wisps drift through the Bulk, and when one dissipated it left this behind. I found more in the Calabi-Yau Knot, still faintly attracting dust.

Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Graviton Wisp.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Graviton Crystal.
A small creature forever evaporating. Like a black hole, the smaller it gets the hotter it glows and the faster it radiates itself away.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Hawking Quanta.
pages.title: Hawking Imp

pages.text: A mirror that tracks the Sun on two axes. At Odeillo, sixty-three of them feed one parabolic concentrator whose focus passes 3,000 °C.
pages.title: Heliostat

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Meteoritics.

Glass held together by a hexagonal force field, like a honeycomb of light. Each cell glows faintly at its edges. It is strong and very slightly warm to the touch. Tapping it makes each hexagon ring separately, a soft chiming that dies away quickly.
pages.title: Hexagonal Field Glass

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wanted a stronger glass for labs. A hexagonal field pattern spread stress evenly across every cell, and the honeycomb glow came free.

An ender pearl wrapped in bulk stone and cosmic neutronium and charged by a nether star. Thrown, an ordinary pearl takes you somewhere; this one would take you everywhere. It shimmers and is never quite in the place it appears to be.
pages.title: Hyperdimensional Pearl

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Ender pearls teleport through some hidden dimension. Wrapping one in bulk stone gave it access to all of them, and a nether star kept it from scattering on the Extreme Assembly Table.
Made in $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omniscience Catalyst.

Spheres in four dimensions leave odd traces when they intersect our three. This ore shows them as nested balls that swell and shrink as I turn the lump. It has no corners anywhere and rolls slightly uphill.
pages.title: Hyperspherical Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Slicing a 4-sphere with a 3-dimensional plane gives a growing then shrinking ball. In the ordinal stone I found ore whose cross-sections did exactly that as I rotated it. Something four-dimensional was buried here.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Transfinite Hierarchy (mine it for its drop).
Rock shattered and welded back together in the instant of an impact. It lines a meteorite crater's bowl and rim.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in Meteorite Crater structures in the Overworld.
pages.title: Impact Breccia

pages.text: The floor of the Planetary Interior: the edge of the solid inner core, 5,150 km down. Iron here is crystallised under 330 GPa and about 5,400 C - as hot as the Sun's surface, yet solid because the pressure will not let it melt. No tool breaks it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Planetary Interior.
pages.title: Inner Core Boundary

pages.text: A crucible of iridium, which melts at 2,446 °C and shrugs off most molten oxides. Laser crystals such as YAG are pulled from melts held in one.
pages.title: Iridium Crucible

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Meteoritics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Crystal Growth Furnace.
The iron-nickel mass of a meteorite, half buried where it struck. Found in craters out in open country.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in Meteorite Crater structures in the Overworld.
pages.title: Iron Meteorite

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

Kaluza and Klein noticed that general relativity in five dimensions, with one dimension curled up small, produces electromagnetism for free. Momentum around that hidden circle appears as electric charge. The shard has a faint static charge and seems to hum slightly when spun.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Kaluza-Klein Ore in the Bulk (Moduli Wastes, Graviton Reef); dropped by the Brane Strider (the Bulk (Moduli Wastes, Graviton Reef)).
pages.title: Kaluza-Klein Shard

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I first found these in the Bulk, among Brane Strider remains and derelict stations. Running bulk stone through Maxwell's Demon Sorter with helium, I could separate grains with momentum in the fifth dimension.

Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Kaluza-Klein Ore$(), in veins through the Bulk.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Brane Strider.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Compactification Lathe, Compactified Circle, Dimensional Singularity.

Bricks of lead shielding. Lead is dense and has many electrons, so it stops gamma rays well - about half of them every 1.3 cm - but it does little against neutrons. Shields as well as the Lead Shielding Block.
pages.title: Lead Bricks

pages.text: Lead shielding striped yellow and black to mark a radiation area. It shields as well as the Lead Shielding Block.
pages.title: Lead Hazard Panel

pages.text: Nearly invisible: it is seen only by how it bends the light behind it into arcs and rings, the way unseen dark matter betrays itself to telescopes.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Einstein Ring Lens.
pages.title: Lens Phantom

pages.text: Bricks of magnetite (Fe3O4), the most magnetic mineral in nature. Iron oxide is dense, so it also shields: it stops gamma rays about two thirds as well as lead, and neutrons three times better.
pages.title: Magnetite Bricks

pages.text: A hole bored through bedrock by the Core Drill. Step into it and you fall to the Planetary Interior; on arrival a second breach opens in the floor beside you, and stepping into that one brings you back up. It cannot be broken or moved.
pages.title: Mantle Breach

pages.text: $(thing)Moduli Crawler$(). Lives in: Moduli Wastes, The Bulk.$(br)Drops: Moduli Crystal, Void Lattice Shard.
pages.title: Moduli Crawler

pages.text: The extra dimensions of string theory have shapes and sizes set by fields called moduli. This crystal is those parameters frozen solid: a record of exactly how the hidden dimensions are curled. It changes shape slightly depending on the angle you view it from.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Moduli Ore in the Bulk (Moduli Wastes); dropped by the Moduli Crawler (the Bulk (Moduli Wastes)).
pages.title: Moduli Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Moduli Crawlers in the Moduli Wastes of the Bulk dropped these, and more lay inside the Calabi-Yau Knot. Measuring their facets, I found they recorded the shape and size of the compact dimensions.

Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Moduli Ore$(), in veins through the Bulk.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Moduli Crawler.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Dimensional Singularity, G₂ Manifold.

Each crystal here is a snapshot of one possible shape for the hidden dimensions. Moduli are the dials that describe the size and shape of compactified space, and this ore holds those dials fixed in mineral form. Different veins, different geometries, all perfectly valid.
pages.title: Moduli Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)String theory admits an enormous landscape of vacua, each set by its moduli. Mining the bulk, I noticed no two lumps of this ore refract light the same way. Each one has settled into a different vacuum.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Bulk (mine it for its drop).

Neutronium rolled into flat plates and riveted onto a block face. It is grey, dense and almost reflective, with seams that look as though they were drawn with a ruler. It gives a lab the look of a reactor vault.
pages.title: Neutronium Plating

pages.text: Made in a $(item)Stonecutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Block of Neutronium, Neutronium Plating Slab, Neutronium Plating Stairs, Neutronium Plating Wall.

Host rock of the Natural Reactor, modelled on Oklo in Gabon, where two billion years ago groundwater slowed neutrons enough for uranium ore to run as a fission reactor for hundreds of thousands of years. It is still slightly radioactive.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Planetary Interior (Natural Reactor), Oklo Reactor Ruin structures in the Planetary Interior (Natural Reactor).
pages.title: Oklo Rock

pages.text: Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 36 and 126. Gives Raw Pitchblende when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Oklo Uraninite Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

Ore whose crystals arrive in sequence: each one has a definite successor, and even infinite chains of them have a limit crystal waiting beyond. Breaking a lump never disturbs the order of what remains.
pages.title: Ordinal Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the ordinal stone I found a vein where crystals grew in strict succession, with a larger one capping every infinite run. Von Neumann's construction of the ordinals, rendered in mineral.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Transfinite Hierarchy (mine it for its drop).
Found in the Overworld, between Y 0 and 48. Gives Raw Pitchblende when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Pitchblende Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Overworld (mine it for its drop).

A spinning wisp that flashes on a perfect beat, like the lighthouse beam of a pulsar. Millisecond pulsars keep time nearly as well as atomic clocks.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Pulsar Timing Crystal, Cosmic Ray Shard.
pages.title: Pulsar Wisp

pages.text: Ore that knows when it is going to be mined. The vein grows brighter before my pick arrives, and splinters along lines that only make sense once the strike has happened. Holding it feels like being remembered.
pages.title: Retrocausal Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)White holes run time backwards. Mining the ejecta rock, I noticed this ore cracking a moment before I struck it. The effect preceded the cause, and the cause still happened.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the white hole interior (mine it for its drop).
Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 50 and 126. Gives Rich Copper Chunk when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Rich Copper Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).
Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 12 and 96. Gives Rich Gold Chunk when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Rich Gold Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).
Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 50 and 126. Gives Rich Iron Chunk when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Rich Iron Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).
Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 4 and 84. Gives Ringwoodite when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Ringwoodite Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

A panel of spacetime alloy whose surface seems to bend inward slightly, as if the wall behind it were further away than it is. It is cool, smooth and very faintly disorienting to look at for long. Its edges line up neatly in rows.
pages.title: Spacetime Panel

pages.text: Made in a $(item)Stonecutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Block of Spacetime Alloy.

A seam of metal pulled thin by gravity gradients. One end of every grain feels a stronger pull than the other, and the ore is threaded with stretch marks. It flexes slightly in the hand, as if still being tugged.
pages.title: Tidal Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Tidal forces are the difference in gravity across an object. Deep in infall rock I found metal that had been stretched rather than crushed, and recognised the signature of a nearby singularity.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the black hole interior (mine it for its drop).

A creature of the tide near a compact mass, where feet are pulled harder than head. It draws everything near it out long and thin, like spaghetti.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Tidal Shear Crystal, Accretion Disk Fragment.
pages.title: Tidal Stretcher

pages.text: A vein where gravity itself fizzes. The quanta of the gravitational field appear and vanish here so densely that the ore feels slightly heavier one moment and lighter the next. Nearby dust drifts in slow, uneven arcs.
pages.title: Ephemeral Graviton Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)No detector has ever caught a single graviton. Picking through foam substrate, I found a seam where my plumb line twitched in rhythm with bursts of vacuum noise. Borrowed gravitons, pinned in stone.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

A vein that points only one way. Each fleck carries a lone magnetic pole, north without south or the reverse, which classical electromagnetism forbids. A compass held close swings and holds, refusing to recover.
pages.title: Ephemeral Monopole Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Dirac showed one monopole anywhere would explain why charge is quantised. In foam substrate my compass locked onto a single seam and would not let go: monopole pairs, flickering up from the vacuum.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

Glints of light that do not come from anywhere. Virtual photons, the messengers that carry the electromagnetic force, wink in and out of this vein, so the ore glows without a source. It is cool to the touch despite the sparkle.
pages.title: Ephemeral Photon Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Every electric force is an exchange of virtual photons. Working in foam substrate I saw a seam lit from within, though nothing nearby could be lighting it. The vacuum was lending light and briefly forgetting to take it back.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

Quarks borrowed from the vacuum and caught before they could be returned. They glow in shifting red, green and blue, colour charge that never settles, and the vein flickers as pairs pop into being and vanish. Leave it alone and it seems to breathe.
pages.title: Ephemeral Quark Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In foam substrate I saw sparks that lasted only an instant, virtual quark pairs living on borrowed energy. One seam held them a little longer than the uncertainty principle should allow, long enough to mine.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

Void lattice cut into bricks - rigid blocks of nothing stacked with careful joints. The wall looks like a pattern of very clean holes in the world. Each brick has crisp, flawless edges, and the joints between them are the only part that looks like ordinary matter. Torchlight seems to fall into them.
pages.title: Void Lattice Bricks

pages.text: Made in a $(item)Stonecutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Void Lattice Block, Void Lattice Bricks Slab, Void Lattice Bricks Stairs, Void Lattice Bricks Wall.

Bulk stone holding pockets of a crystal made of nothing - a lattice of empty sites that remains rigid even though there is nothing in them. It looks like a gap in the rock that has decided to be solid.
pages.title: Void Lattice Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Mining in the Bulk, I hit a patch of rock that the pick went through as though it were air but that still dropped something. The lattice was a crystal of vacancies, ordered without anything to order.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Bulk (mine it for its drop).
Survey notes. $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$() grows deep in the deepslate layer. $(item)Degenerate Matter$() is found in End stone; smelt or blast it into $(item)Neutronium$().

$(item)Void Lattice$() only forms in the Bulk.$(br2)Names explained: Cherenkov light is the blue glow of particles outrunning light in a medium. Degenerate matter is what remains when atoms are crushed until only quantum exclusion holds them up, as in white dwarfs and neutron stars.
Glows with the blue light of particles outrunning light in a medium.$(br2)Made in $(item)Galton Board$().$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Deepslate Cherenkov Quartz Ore in the Overworld.
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Cherenkov Quartz$(): Atomic Clock, Block of Cherenkov Quartz, Casimir Plate, Casimir Vacuum Press, Chemical Reactor and more

Out past the edge of the sky, round a black hole feeding on a disk of its own fire, islands of rock and ice drift in the dark. The $(thing)Accretion Frontier$() is reached with a $(item)Light Sail$() (research $(thing)Galactic Dynamics$()): climb to y 200 or higher, stand under open sky, and unfurl it. Unfurled again in the Frontier, it brings you home and slows your fall.

It has five regions. The $(thing)Molecular Cloud Nebula$(), cold ice and dust where stars are born: you cannot see far. The $(thing)Asteroid Belt$(), where you weigh almost nothing - and $(thing)micrometeorites$() strike anyone not wearing a $(item)Whipple Shield$() (a quarter stopped per piece; a full set stops all).

The $(thing)Pulsar Field$(): crust of neutron-star iron, and a pulse of radiation every five seconds, on the beat, for anyone under open sky. Gravity is high and time runs slow (Time Dilation). The $(thing)Accretion Rim$(): slag lakes of disk plasma; it is hot enough to burn, and the disk's tidal pull stretches you. The $(thing)Lensing Void$(): black glass, sight lines bent, and frame-dragging currents that push you sideways.

Its ores: $(item)Interstellar Dust$() in the nebula's ice, $(item)Exoplanet Core Samples$() and $(item)Brown Dwarf Cores$() in the asteroids, $(item)Magnetar Crust$(), $(item)Pulsar Timing Crystals$() and $(item)Cosmic Ray Shards$() in the pulsar crust, $(item)Accretion Disk Fragments$() in the slag, and $(item)Einstein Ring Lenses$() in the void glass. Derelict Stations drift between the islands; Pulsar Beacons stand on the field.

Each of the Frontier's creatures acts out its physics. The $(thing)Nebuloid$() is a drifting knot of gas and dust; inside it you are blind. The $(thing)Pulsar Wisp$() pulses on an exact beat, once every one and a half seconds, and its pulse hurts and irradiates anyone it can see within ten blocks - dodge behind something between pulses.

The $(thing)Tidal Stretcher$() pulls you in harder the closer you are (a tidal force grows as 1/r³) and stretches what it grabs. The $(thing)Lens Phantom$() is never where it appears: its light reaches you bent round the void's mass, so its image stands a block or two from its body. Aim beside it.

The $(thing)Hawking Imp$() is a tiny black hole. It evaporates, and the smaller it gets the hotter and faster it burns (T ∝ 1/M) - until it pops. The $(thing)Boltzmann Brain$() fluctuates out of nothing, mutters, and is gone within half a minute unless caught.

$(thing)The Binary$(): play a Binary Black Hole Merger record - or a Gravitational Wave Echo - in the Frontier and two compact stars spiral out of the dark. Their gravitational waves carry off their orbit: they close in (da/dt ∝ −1/a³) and circle ever faster. Kill both before they meet - if they merge, the shockwave hits everything nearby, and nothing is left to loot.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Accretion Disk Fragment when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Accretion Rim's slag.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Accretion Disk Fragments.

$(item)Asteroid Rock$(). The rubble of planetesimals that never became planets. Its chondrules are frozen droplets from the Solar System's first few million years.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Asteroid Belt).
$(thing)Found$(): The Asteroid Belt.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): The Spectrograph sorts four into two Meteoric Iron and a Chondrite Fragment.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Brown Dwarf Core when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Asteroid Belt's rock.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Brown Dwarf Cores (also made in the Tectonic Press, from dust and cloud gas).
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Cosmic Ray Shard when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Pulsar Field's crust.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Cosmic Ray Shards (also made by the Interstellar Scoop, from glass left high up).
$(item)Dust Cloud$(). A cloud of dust grains, too thin to stand on. Now and then, broken, it leaves Interstellar Dust.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier.
$(thing)Found$(): The Molecular Cloud Nebula: you can pass through it.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Breaks into Interstellar Dust, sometimes.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Interstellar Dust when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Nebula's ice.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Interstellar Dust.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Einstein Ring Lens when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Lensing Void's glass.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Einstein Ring Lenses.

$(item)Frontier Regolith$(). Rock ground to dust by billions of years of micrometeorites. Assayed in bulk it gives back its interstellar dust and a little rare earth.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier.
$(thing)Found$(): The top of every island of the Accretion Frontier (except the Lensing Void).$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): The Spectrograph assays eight into four Interstellar Dust and a Rare Earth Oxide.
$(item)Hydrogen Cloud$(). Ionised hydrogen glowing red at 656 nm, the H-alpha line. You can walk straight through it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier.
$(thing)Found$(): The Molecular Cloud Nebula: you can pass through it.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Light: it glows. Its gases will be gathered in a later expansion.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Magnetar Crust Fragment when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Pulsar Field's crust.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Magnetar Crust Fragments.

$(item)Nebular Ice$(). Water, carbon monoxide and ammonia frozen together on dust grains at about fifteen kelvin. Starlight slowly builds larger molecules within it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Molecular Cloud Nebula).
$(thing)Found$(): Patches in the Molecular Cloud Nebula, among its clouds.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Two sublimate into 250 mB of Molecular Cloud in the Electrolytic Cell.
$(item)Oxygen Cloud$(). Doubly ionised oxygen glowing green-blue at 501 nm. You can walk straight through it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier.
$(thing)Found$(): The Molecular Cloud Nebula: you can pass through it.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Light: it glows. Its gases will be gathered in a later expansion.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Exoplanet Core Sample when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Asteroid Belt's rock.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Exoplanet Core Samples (also made in the Hypervelocity Impact Forge).
$(item)Protostar Fragment$(). Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Protostellar Ember when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): Inside the Nebula's ice.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives a Protostellar Ember: thermoelectric fuel that burns for a long time, or feed for the Accretion Disk Reactor.

$(item)Pulsar Crust$(). Iron from a neutron star's crust: a lattice of nuclei in a sea of electrons, held under a field of some hundred million tesla.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Pulsar Field).
$(thing)Found$(): The Pulsar Field.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Two with two Iron-Nickel become a Magnetar Crust Fragment in the Pulsed Magnet Lab, at 80 T.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Pulsar Timing Crystal when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Pulsar Field's crust.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Pulsar Timing Crystals.

$(item)Rim Slag$(). Cinder flung from the inner edge of an accretion disk, where gas spirals in at a fair fraction of light speed and is heated to millions of degrees.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Accretion Rim).
$(thing)Found$(): The Accretion Rim, round its plasma lakes.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Quenched with Accretion Disk Plasma in the Tectonic Press: Accretion Disk Fragments.
$(item)Station Hull$(). Aluminium skin and stringers from a spacecraft, thin enough to dent by hand. In vacuum, a few millimetres of it is all that separates air from nothing.
$(thing)Found$(): Derelict Stations drifting in the Frontier; or crafted from iron.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): The body of the Whipple Shield and the Frontier Suit.

$(item)Void Glass$(). Glass as dark as the space it came from. Gravity bends light as a lens does, and a well-aligned mass draws a background source into a full Einstein ring.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Lensing Void).
$(thing)Found$(): The Lensing Void.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Four with Fused Silica make an Einstein Ring Lens in the Optical Workshop.
Every region of the Accretion Frontier has its hazard, and each has an answer.

$(li)$(thing)Nebula$() - blinding dust: the $(item)Adaptive Optics Visor$().$(li)$(thing)Asteroid Belt$() - micrometeorites: the $(item)Whipple Shield$() (a quarter per piece); low gravity: $(item)Gravity Compensators$().$(li)$(thing)Pulsar Field$() - its radiation pulse: $(item)Radiation Plating$() on your armour; high gravity: Gravity Compensators; Time Dilation: an $(item)Atomic Clock$() in the off hand.

$(li)$(thing)Accretion Rim$() - heat: the $(item)Thermal Shroud$() (or a full Refractory Suit); its tidal pull: the $(item)Tidal Brace$() (or a Precision Gyroscope in the off hand).$(li)$(thing)Lensing Void$() - frame dragging: a $(item)Precision Gyroscope$() in the off hand; warped sight: the Adaptive Optics Visor.

The four pieces of the $(item)Frontier Suit$() are made of Station Hull, each round a piece of the region it answers: an Einstein Ring Lens, an Accretion Disk Fragment, a Tidal Shear Crystal and a Planetary Core Sample (the reference mass the boots weigh gravity against).

Found a crashed research observatory, its containment dome cracked, a supply cache still inside. They dot the Overworld. Who built them, I don't yet know.$(br2)A good source of early Cherenkov Quartz and Neutronium - worth a detour before I can make either myself.

A cache the Transcendental keeps for itself - and the one you can build: 243 kinds of item, and up to $(thing)2,147,483,647$() of each. Whatever you put in joins the pile of the same item. Scroll to move through its 27 rows; a click or shift-click takes one normal stack at a time.
Pipes put into it and take out of it (one stack at a time). Broken, it keeps everything inside. It is made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
